From the high summit of Olympus,
the Son of the most high Father,
like a stone cut from the mountain,
falling down to the lowest earth,
joined together both corners,
of the heavenly and earthly house.

But that dwelling of the heavenly ones
ever resounds with praises,
and proclaims God, three and one,
with unceasing song:
joined to those who sing,
we are rivals of holy Sion.

This temple, O King of heaven,
fill with your gracious light;
hither, O come when asked,
and receive the vows of your people,
and pour continually upon our hearts
the grace of heaven.

Here may the voices of the faithful
and the prayers of suppliants obtain
the gifts of the blessed dwelling,
and rejoice in the graces received;
until, released from the body,
they fill the blessed seats.

Let glory due to the Father
be ever rendered to the Most High,
and to the only-begotten Son of the Father,
and to the glorious Paraclete,
to whom be praise, power, and glory
eternal through the ages.
Amen.

O heavenly city Jerusalem,
blessed vision of peace,
you who are raised on high from living
stones to the stars,
and encircled in the manner of a bride
by thousands upon thousands of Angels.

O you wed to a blessed lot,
endowed with the glory of the Father,
bedewed with the grace of the Bridegroom,
most beautiful Queen,
joined in marriage to Christ the Prince,
resplendent city of heaven.

Here pearls gleam brightly,
and gates stand open to all;
for led by virtue as their guide,
a mortal is brought thither,
whoever endures torments
struck with love of Christ.

By the wholesome blows of the chisel
and by much hammering,
polished by the builder's mallet,
these stones build up this structure,
and fitted together in proper bonds
are set in their high place.

Let glory due to the Father
be ever rendered to the Most High,
and to the only-begotten Son of the Father,
and to the glorious Paraclete,
to whom be praise, power, and glory
eternal through the ages.
Amen.

With glad voices let us follow
the Blood poured out for Christ
and the victories of the Martyrs
and the laurel crown worthy of heaven.

With the terror of the world overcome
and the punishments of the body scorned,
by the swift passage of holy death
they possess the blessed life.

The Martyrs are given to the fire
and to the teeth of beasts;
the hand of the frenzied torturer
brandishes armed hooks.

Their naked bowels are exposed,
their sacred blood is shed;
but they remain unmoved,
by the grace of eternal life.

You now, O Redeemer, we implore,
that you join us who pray
to the fellowship of the Martyrs
through all eternal ages.
Amen.

O God, the lot, crown, and reward
of your soldiers:
as we sing the praises of the Martyr,
free us from the bond of sin.

For he, reckoning the joys of this world
and the enticing food of deception
as bitter gall,
arrived at the things of heaven.

He ran bravely through his punishments
and bore them manfully,
and, shedding his blood for you,
now possesses eternal gifts.

For this, with suppliant prayer
we entreat you, most merciful One;
in this triumph of the Martyr
forgive your servants their offenses.

Let enduring praise and glory
be to the Father, and to the Son,
and likewise to the Holy Paraclete,
through all eternal ages.
Amen.

Let the world exult with joy;
let heaven resound with praises;
the earth and stars sing together
the glory of the Apostles.

You, judges of the ages
and true lights of the world:
we pray with the vows of our hearts,
hear the voices of suppliants.

You who shut the gates of heaven
and open locks with a word,
bid us, who are guilty of offense,
to be loosed, we pray.

At whose commands sickness and health
at once take effect:
heal our ailing minds;
grant us increase in virtues.

That when Christ the Judge
returns at the end of the age,
he may grant us to be partakers
of everlasting joy.

To the Father, and likewise to the Son,
and to you, Holy Spirit,
as it was, so let it ever be
through all the ages, glory.
Amen.

Let us all praise the woman
of strong and manly heart,
who shines renowned everywhere
with the glory of holiness.

Wounded by holy love,
while she shudders at the harmful love
of the world, she traveled
the arduous way to heaven.

Taming the flesh with fasts
and nourishing her mind
with the sweet food of prayer,
she possesses the joys of heaven.

O Christ the King, strength of the strong,
you who alone accomplish great deeds,
hear graciously, at her prayer,
us your suppliants.

Let glory be to God the Father,
and to his only Son,
with the Spirit the Paraclete,
now and through every age.

Let glory be to the Father, and to the Son his offspring,
and to you, O Spirit, power equal to them both,
God ever one, through every age of time.

Jesus, more exalted crown
and more sublime truth,
who render to your confessing servant
an everlasting reward:

grant to this suppliant assembly,
at his prayer, remission
of the guilt of sin
by breaking the bond of its chain.

As the year's season returns,
the day has shone with its light

Let enduring glory be to the Father,

This Confessor of the Lord, whom the peoples
piously praise and celebrate throughout the world,
on this day merited joyfully
to ascend the blessed seats.

Who, devout, prudent, humble, and pure,

sick members that lay here and there,

Three and One.

O weeping eyes, shed your tears,
and let the depths of hearts resound with grief;
I recall the punishments and fierce wounds
inflicted upon the Lord by the wicked.

Alas! a band of servants girded with swords
assaults the arrested Lord with clubs;
now they strike him with blows,
now they batter the divine Head with horrible strokes.

There is no end to the wickedness: Christ
is handed over to the wicked executioner;
without delay the barbarian fears not,
with impious daring, to turn his right hand against the King of heaven.

Hear, O peoples, the beloved Lord,
with blood flowing from his shoulders on all sides,
bears the assault of the frenzied lictor,

Who would not weep! Already I have recounted new things:
the wickedness of the untamed people devises new torments.
Alas for the grief! it drives into his head
a crown rough with wild thorns.

Alas the crime! The Lord is dragged with wicked ropes
to the place of deadly punishment;
there he died, restoring his spirit in death
to his Father.

For one who suffered such fierce wounds
for wretched sinners, let fitting glory resound on earth;
and may the human race ceaselessly raise
the sacred Name to heaven.
Amen.

O glorious among virgins,
exalted among the stars,
you nourish at your milky breast
him, small, who created you.

What sad Eve took away
you restore by your holy offspring:
that the sorrowful may enter the stars,
you open the hinges of heaven.

You are the gate of the high King
and the shining hall of light:
rejoice, O redeemed peoples,
for life was given through the Virgin.

To Jesus be glory,
who was born of a Virgin,
with the Father and the gracious Spirit,
unto ages of ages.
Amen.

The more beautiful sun proclaims
the Paschal joy to the world,
when the Apostles behold Jesus
splendent with new light.

They marvel at the wounds in Christ's flesh
gleaming like stars,
and all that they see
they proclaim as faithful witnesses.

O Christ, most merciful King,
possess our hearts:
that our tongue may render
due thanks to your name.

That you may be the everlasting
Paschal joy of our minds, O Jesus;
free those reborn to life
from the dreadful death of sins.

Let glory be to God the Father,
and to the Son who rose from the dead,
and to the Paraclete,
unto ages of ages.
Amen.
The first stanza of the following hymn is said kneeling.

Hail, star of the sea,
gentle Mother of God,
and ever Virgin,
happy gate of heaven.

Receiving that Ave
from the mouth of Gabriel,
establish us in peace,
changing the name of Eve.

Loose the chains of the guilty,
bring forth light to the blind,
drive away our evils,
beg for all good things.

Show yourself to be a mother;
let him receive through you our prayers,
who, born for us,
consented to be yours.

O singular Virgin,
gentle above all others,
free us from our sins
and make us gentle and chaste.

Grant a pure life,
prepare a safe journey,
that, beholding Jesus,
we may rejoice together always.

Let praise be to God the Father,
and honor to Christ the Most High,
and to the Holy Spirit,
one honor to the Three.
Amen.

He whom earth, sea, and stars
worship, adore, and proclaim,
who governs the threefold frame of the world,
the womb of Mary bears.

He whom moon, sun, and all things
serve through the ages,
poured through with the grace of heaven,
the maiden's womb carries.

Blessed is the Mother in her office,
whose heavenly Maker,
holding the world in his fist,
was enclosed under the ark of her womb.

Blessed at the announcement of heaven,
fruitful by the Holy Spirit,
he who was desired by the nations
was poured through her womb.

To you, O Jesus, be glory,
who were born of a Virgin,
with the Father and the gracious Spirit
unto ages of ages.
Amen.

O glorious King of Martyrs,
crown of confessors,
who lead those who spurn earthly things
to the things of heaven:

straightway turn your gracious ear
to our voices:
we sing of sacred trophies:
forgive what we have done wrong.

You conquer among the Martyrs
and are merciful to confessors:
conquer also our sins,
O bestower of pardon.

Let glory be to God the Father,
and to his only Son,
with the Spirit the Paraclete,
now and through every age.
Amen.

The Redeemer is tossed by the fierce whirlwind of sorrows,
overwhelmed by dark punishments,
bearing bitter suffering,
nailed to the Cross.

Feet and hands are bloodied
by the horrible wound of the nail;
heart, face, limbs, and breast
overflow with sacred blood.

He weeps, he prays, and crying out he dies;
the stricken heart of his Mother falters;
alas, Mother! alas, Son! let this grief
break ungrateful hearts.

Mountains, tombs, and rocks
are split; fields, rivers,
cliffs, and the sea tremble,
and the veil of the Temple is torn.

Sun, moon, sky, and stars
mourned, and the world groans.
O you men, you little ones,
O wives, maidens, weep,

stand in sorrow at the Cross,
anoint his blessed feet,
wash them with tears, dry them
with your hair, and kiss them with your lips.

You, the victim of charity,
that you might take away our sins,
accomplish for us, by your saving Blood,
our adoption.

Be therefore our peace and joy,
be our life, O Jesus, and our reward,
be our guide and light on the way,
our recompense and crown in our homeland.
Amen.

Let us sing together
the renowned joys of the Saints,
their deeds and brave acts:
an eager heart urges to set forth in song
the noblest kind of victors.

These are they whom the foolish world abhorred;
this fruit-barren, flower-dry world
was despised by the followers of your name,
O Jesus, good King of heaven.

For you they trod underfoot
the frenzies and savage threats of men
and cruel stripes:
the tearing hook vigorously yielded to them
and did not pierce their inmost parts.

They are cut down by swords as sheep:
no murmur resounds, no complaint;
but with undaunted heart, a well-formed conscience
preserves their patience.

What voice, what tongue will be able to recount
the gifts you prepare for the Martyrs?
For with laurels bright with flowing crimson blood
they encircle their temples.

You, O supreme and only Deity, we beseech;
that you drive away our sins and remove our harmful deeds,
grant peace to your servants; that to you they may sing glory
through the succession of years.
Amen.

Behold, God himself hangs on the infamous wood,
wet with his shed blood;
behold, his gracious hand is cleft deeply
by the merciless nail.

Him, as the minister of a wicked crime,
in the midst of unworthy thieves,
consider; this was the dreadful will
of the cruel people.

Alas, his face grows pale; behold his head
drops and bends; with eyes closed, the Redeemer
pours forth his spirit from his sacred mouth,
laden with merits.

O heart, you surpass hard bronze in mourning,
unless you wipe away your sin; your fault
nailed Christ to the stake; your fault
has subjected him to dark death.

Let all eternal glory be to God for ever,
who, the merciful Redeemer of our race,
washed away by his Blood the stain of sin
that was harming the wretched guilty.
Amen.

Let us sing with joyful hearts
the eternal gifts of Christ,
the glory of the Apostles,
and their palms and due hymns.

Princes of the Churches,
triumphal leaders of battle,
soldiers of the heavenly court,
and true lights of the world.

The devoted faith of the Saints,
the unconquered hope of believers,
the perfect charity of Christ
crushed the tyrant of the world.

In them the glory of the Father,
in them the Son triumphs,
in them the will of the Spirit,
heaven is filled with joy.

To the Father, and likewise to the Son,
and to you, Holy Spirit,
as it was, so let it ever be
through all the ages, glory.
Amen.

The Apostles were sorrowful
at the bitter death of Christ,
whom the wicked servants
had slain with a most cruel death.

The truthful Angel had foretold
to the women:
Christ would soon bring joy
to the flock of the faithful by his word.

The women, as messengers, at once run
to the anxious Apostles,
and there they find and meet
the footsteps of the shining Christ.

The Apostles betake themselves
to the high mountains of Galilee,
and finding Jesus, their desire fulfilled,
are blessed by his gracious light.

That you may be the everlasting
Paschal joy of our minds, O Jesus;
free those reborn to life
from the dreadful death of sins.

Let glory be to God the Father
and to the Son who rose from the dead,
and to the Paraclete
unto ages of ages.
Amen.

O Offspring of the Virgin and Maker of your Mother,
whom a Virgin bore and a Virgin brought forth:
we sing the glorious triumphs won in death
by the Virgin's child.

For she, blessed in the lot of a double palm,
while she eagerly strove to master
the weakness of her sex,
mastered also the bloodthirsty tyrant by her death.

And so fearing neither death
nor the thousand kinds of punishment
that are death's companions,
by the shedding of her blood she merited
to ascend the serene heaven.

At her prayer, O gracious God,
remit from us the fitting punishments of our sins;
that with a pure heart we may resound
a worthy hymn to you.

Let glory be to the Father, and to the Son his offspring,
and to you, O Spirit, power equal to them both,
God ever one, through every age of time.
Amen.

O Offspring of the Virgin and Maker of your Mother,
whom a Virgin bore and a Virgin brought forth:
we sing the feast of the blessed Virgin;
receive our offering.
At her prayer, O gracious God,
remit from us the fitting punishments of our sins;
that with a pure heart we may resound
a worthy hymn to you.

Let glory be to the Father, and to the Son his offspring,
and to you, O Spirit, power equal to them both,
God ever one, through every age of time.
Amen.

Joseph went up * from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, to be enrolled with Mary.
The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary, and Joseph, and the Infant lying in the manger.
Behold, the Angel of the Lord * appeared in a dream to Joseph, saying: Arise, and take the Child and his Mother, and flee into Egypt.
Joseph, rising up, * took the Child and his Mother by night, and withdrew into Egypt; and he was there until the death of Herod.

When Herod was dead, * the Angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying: Arise, and take the Child and his Mother, and go into the land of Israel; for those who sought the life of the Child are dead.
Joseph took * the Child and his Mother, and came into the land of Israel.
Hearing that Archelaus * reigned in Judea in place of Herod his father, Joseph was afraid to go there.

Being warned in a dream, * Joseph withdrew into the parts of Galilee; and coming, he dwelt in a city called Nazareth, that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: He shall be called a Nazarean.
The Father of Jesus * and his Mother were marveling at the things that were said of him; and Simeon blessed them.
Mary has been taken up into heaven: * the Angels rejoice, praising and blessing the Lord.
The Virgin Mary has been taken up * into the heavenly bridal chamber, where the King of kings sits on a starry throne.
In the fragrance * of your ointments we run: the young maidens have loved you greatly.
Blessed * are you, daughter, by the Lord: for through you we have shared in the fruit of life.
You are beautiful * and lovely, O daughter of Jerusalem: terrible as an army set in array.
The kings of the earth stood up, * and the princes assembled together, against the Lord and against his Christ.
Many are they who afflict me; many rise up against me.
Unjust witnesses * rose up against me, and iniquity lied to itself.
My enemies have spoken evil against me: When shall he die, and his name perish?
Let them be confounded * and put to shame, who seek my soul to take it away.
My enemies have trodden me down all the day long; all their thoughts against me are for evil.
The sons of men: their teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
They have bent their bow, a bitter thing, * to shoot in secret at the blameless.
I am become * like a man without help, free among the dead.
Blessed is the man * who meditates on the law of the Lord: his will endures day and night, and all things whatsoever he shall do shall always prosper.
Blessed is this holy one, * who has trusted in the Lord, who has proclaimed the precept of the Lord, established on his holy mountain.
You are my glory, * you are my protector, O Lord; you lift up my head, and you have heard me from your holy mountain.
The Lord heard * his holy one when he called; the Lord heard him, and set him in peace.
Let all rejoice * who hope in you, O Lord; for you have blessed the just, and crowned him with the shield of your goodwill.
O Lord, our Lord, * how wonderful is your name throughout all the earth! For you have crowned your holy one with glory and honor, and set him over the works of your hands.
O Lord, * this holy one shall dwell in your tabernacle; he has worked justice, and shall rest on your holy mountain.
He has asked life * of you, and you have granted it to him, O Lord: you have set glory and great beauty upon him; you have placed on his head a crown of precious stone.
He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Savior: for this is the generation of those who seek the Lord.
Blessed are you * among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
Like choice myrrh, * you have given forth a fragrance of sweetness, O holy Mother of God.
Before the couch * of this Virgin, strike up sweet songs of praise for us.
The Angel of the Lord * announced to Mary, and she conceived by the Holy Spirit.
In your beauty * and your comeliness go forth, advance prosperously, and reign.
God will help her * with his countenance: God is in her midst, she shall not be moved.
As the dwelling * of all of us rejoicing is in you, O holy Mother of God.
Rejoice, O Virgin Mary: * you alone have destroyed all heresies throughout the whole world.
Grant me to be worthy * to praise you, O holy Virgin: give me strength against your enemies.
After childbirth, * O Virgin, you remained inviolate: O Mother of God, intercede for us.
I will take the chalice * of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.
With those * who hated peace I was peaceful: when I spoke to them, they attacked me without cause.
From unjust men * deliver me, O Lord.
Keep me * from the snare they have set for me, and from the stumbling-blocks of those who work iniquity.
I looked to the right, * and I saw, and there was none who would know me.
Lord, you delivered to me * five talents: behold, I have gained five more.
Well done, good servant, * faithful in a little: enter into the joy of your Lord.
The faithful and prudent servant, * whom the Lord has set over his household.
Blessed is that servant * whom, when his Lord shall come and knock at the door, he shall find watching.
Good * and faithful servant, enter into the joy of your Lord.
Direct, * O Lord my God, my way in your sight.
Return, * O Lord, and deliver my soul: for in death there is none who is mindful of you.
Lest at any time * he seize my soul like a lion, while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save me.
In a place of pasture * there he has settled me.
The sins * of my youth and my ignorances, do not remember, O Lord.
I believe to see * the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
May it please you, * O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, look upon me to help me.
Heal my soul, * O Lord, for I have sinned against you.
My soul thirsted * for the living God: when shall I come and appear before the face of the Lord?
Your house, O Lord, * is becoming in holiness for length of days.
My house * shall be called a house of prayer.
This is the house of the Lord * firmly built; well founded upon a solid rock.
The house of the Lord * is well founded upon a solid rock.
All your walls * are of precious stones, and the towers of Jerusalem shall be built with gems.
While the King was * at his rest, my nard gave forth its fragrance of sweetness.
His left hand * is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
I am dark * but beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem; and so the King has loved me, and brought me into his chamber.
Now the winter is past, * the rain is over and gone: rise up, my beloved, and come.
You have been made beautiful * and sweet in your delights, O holy Mother of God.
Come, my chosen one, * and I will place my throne in you, alleluia.
She is glorious * among the daughters of Jerusalem.
Behold the great priest, * who in his days pleased God and was found righteous.
There was none found like him * who kept the law of the Most High.
Therefore with an oath * the Lord made him increase among his people.
Priests of God, * bless the Lord: servants of the Lord, sing a hymn to God. Alleluia.
The bones that were humbled * shall rejoice before the Lord.
Hear, O Lord, * my prayer: to you all flesh shall come.
Your right hand * has upheld me, O Lord.
From the gate of hell * deliver my soul, O Lord.
Let every spirit * praise the Lord.
I was scourged * all the day, and my chastisement was in the mornings.
I came to the mountain of myrrh * and to the hill of incense; like a lamb led to the slaughter, I was silent and opened not my mouth.
They pierced my hands * and my feet: they numbered all my bones.
I sought one to comfort me * and found none: they gave gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
When Jesus had received * the vinegar, he said: It is consummated; and bowing his head, he gave up his spirit.
This is the wise Virgin, * and one of the number of the prudent.
This is the wise Virgin * whom the Lord found watching.
This is she who knew not * the marriage bed in sin: she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.
This is my commandment, * that you love one another, as I have loved you.
Greater love * no one has, than that one lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends, * if you do what I command you, says the Lord.
Blessed are the peacemakers, * blessed are the pure of heart: for they shall see God.
In your patience * you shall possess your souls.
Jacob begot * Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ, alleluia.
The Angel Gabriel * was sent from God to a city of Galilee, whose name was Nazareth, to a Virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, alleluia.
Joseph also went up * from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth into Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, alleluia.
And they came with haste * and found Mary, and Joseph, and the Infant lying in the manger, alleluia.
And Jesus himself * was beginning to be about thirty years of age, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, alleluia.
In the law of the Lord * was his delight day and night.
Proclaiming * the commandment of the Lord, he was established on his holy mountain.
With my voice * I cried to the Lord: and he heard me from his holy mountain.
Sons of men, * know that the Lord has made his holy one wonderful.
With the shield of your good will * you have crowned him, O Lord.
In all the earth * you have crowned him with glory and honor.
The Lord is just * and has loved justice: his face has beheld equity.
He shall dwell * in your tabernacle: he shall rest on your holy mountain.
You have set, O Lord, * upon his head a crown of precious stone.
Into all the earth * their sound has gone forth, and to the ends of the world their words.
The just cried out, * and the Lord heard them.
You shall make them * princes over all the earth: they shall be mindful of your name, O Lord.
The princes of the peoples * are gathered together with the God of Abraham.
You have given an inheritance * to those who fear your name, O Lord.
They have declared * the works of God, and have understood his deeds.
The horns of the just * shall be exalted, alleluia.
Light has risen * for the just, alleluia; and gladness for the upright of heart, alleluia.
They kept * his testimonies and his commandments, alleluia.
The Angel Gabriel * was sent to Mary, the Virgin betrothed to Joseph. (Alleluia.)
Hail, Mary, * full of grace; the Lord is with you: blessed are you among women. (Alleluia.)
Fear not, Mary, * you have found favor with the Lord: behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. (Alleluia.)
The Lord God shall give him * the throne of David his father, and he shall reign for ever. (Alleluia.)
Behold the handmaid of the Lord: * be it done to me according to your word. (Alleluia.)
O wondrous exchange: * the Creator of the human race, taking on an animate body, deigned to be born of a Virgin; and proceeding as man without seed, he bestowed upon us his Divinity.
When you were born * ineffably from the Virgin, then the Scriptures were fulfilled: as rain upon a fleece you came down, to save the human race: we praise you, our God.
The bush which Moses saw * burning but unconsumed, we have known to signify your laudable virginity preserved: O Mother of God, intercede for us.
The root of Jesse has budded, * a star has arisen from Jacob: a Virgin has brought forth the Savior; we praise you, our God.
Behold, Mary has borne * for us the Savior, whom John seeing cried out, saying: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sins of the world, alleluia.
O how beautiful * is the chaste generation with splendor!
Return, * return, O Shulammite; return, that we may behold you.
Many waters * could not quench charity.
Draw me after you, * in the fragrance of your ointments we shall run: your name is oil poured out.
All the Saints— * what great torments they endured, that they might safely attain the palm of martyrdom.
With the palm * the Saints have come to the kingdom, and have merited crowns of beauty from the hand of God.
The bodies of the Saints * were buried in peace: and their names shall live for ever.
O martyrs of the Lord, * bless the Lord for ever.
O choir of martyrs, * praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia.
I will please the Lord * in the land of the living.
Woe is me, O Lord, * for my sojourning is prolonged.
The Lord keeps you from all evil: * may the Lord keep your soul.
If you, O Lord, shall mark iniquities: * O Lord, who shall endure it?
The works * of your hands, O Lord, do not despise.
Whoever shall confess me * before men, I also will confess him before my Father.
Whoever follows me * does not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life, says the Lord.
Whoever serves me, * let him follow me: and where I am, there also shall my servant be.
If anyone serves me, * my Father who is in heaven will honor him, says the Lord.
I will, Father, * that where I am, there also shall my servant be.
Your Saints, * O Lord, shall flourish like the lily, alleluia: and like the fragrance of balsam they shall be before you, alleluia.
In the heavenly kingdoms * is the dwelling of the Saints, alleluia: and their rest is for ever, alleluia.
Beneath the veil * your Saints cried out, O Lord, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
O spirits and souls * of the just, sing a hymn to our God, alleluia, alleluia.
The just will shine * like the sun in the sight of God, alleluia.
Beside the running waters * he planted the vineyard of the just, and in the law of the Lord was their delight.
As gold * in a furnace the Lord tried his chosen ones, and as a burnt offering he received them for ever.
If in the sight of men * they suffered torments, the hope of the chosen is immortal for ever.
I will give to my Saints * a named place in the Kingdom of my Father, says the Lord.
To his holy ones who are in his land, * he has made wonderful all my desires among them.
The holy ones who hope in the Lord * shall have strength; they shall take wings as eagles, they shall fly, and shall not grow weary.
But the just * shall live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord.
They delivered * their bodies to death, that they might not serve idols; therefore, crowned, they possess the palm.
Behold, the reward * of the Saints is abundant with God; though they died for Christ, they shall live for ever.
The just shall stand * with great constancy against those who afflicted them, alleluia.
Behold, * how they are counted among the sons of God, and their lot is among the saints, alleluia.
Perpetual light * shall shine upon your Saints, O Lord, and an eternity of ages, alleluia.
Lift up your gates, * O you princes, and be lifted up, O eternal gates.
The Lord shall be my God, * and this stone shall be called the house of God.
Moses built * an altar to the Lord God.
This place is none other * than the house of God and the gate of heaven.
Jacob saw a ladder, * whose top touched the heavens, and angels descending, and said: Truly this place is holy.
Jacob erected * a stone as a pillar, pouring oil upon it from above.
He who dwells * in the shelter of the Most High shall abide in the protection of the God of heaven.
The temple of the Lord * is holy; it is the work of God, it is the building of God.
Blessed * is the glory of the Lord from his holy place, alleluia.

10 So we are fools because of Christ, but you are discerning in Christ? We are weak, but you are strong? You are noble, but we are ignoble?
11 Even to this very hour, we hunger and thirst, and we are naked and repeatedly beaten, and we are unsteady.
12 And we labor, working with our own hands. We are slandered, and so we bless. We suffer and endure persecution.
13 We are cursed, and so we pray. We have become like the refuse of this world, like the residue of everything, even until now.
14 I am not writing these things in order to confound you, but in order to admonish you, as my dearest sons.

Let us proclaim to the holy Martyrs the grace of the Lord's Passover: that, as we preach the opened gates of that burial, so may their tombs likewise be opened; as we declare that his dead body suddenly revived with warm veins, so may the already cold limbs of these saints be warmed by the heat of immortality. For the same power that raised the Lord raises the Martyrs. For as they experienced the way of his Passion, so shall they also experience that of his life; for it is written in the Psalm: You have made known to me the ways of life. This is surely said in the Resurrection in the person of the Savior: so that he who, while returning after death from the lower regions to the upper, begins to know the way of life, which before was unknown.

Who then is the faithful and wise servant whom the Lord has set over his household? Although he exhorts us all alike to the unwearying care of watchfulness, yet he assigns a special solicitude to the leaders of the people, that is, to bishops, in looking forward to and awaiting his coming. If such a one is obedient to his word and observant of his commandments, that is, if he strengthens the weak with the opportuneness and truth of teaching, consolidates what is broken, converts what is depraved, and dispenses the word of life as food of eternity for the nourishment of the household, and is found doing this and devoted to these things: he shall receive glory from the Lord as a faithful steward and profitable overseer, and shall be set over all goods; that is, he shall be placed in the glory of God, because there is nothing beyond which is better.

For indeed, when he was proposing new commandments to those who followed him, he said: Unless a man renounces all that he possesses, he cannot be my disciple. For he was contemplating, as much as the weakness of the human eye of the mind is able to fix itself in a riddle upon eternity, how great are the joys of the heavenly city; and, unable to recount them, he cried out in wonder: What have I in heaven? As if to say: It surpasses my strength, it surpasses the capacity of my eloquence, it transcends the capacity of my understanding, that splendor, that glory, that loftiness by which our Lord Jesus Christ, having removed us from the disquiet of men, in the hidden place of his face, will reform the body of our lowliness, configured to the body of his glory. In contemplation of this perfect freedom, he feared no danger, he dreaded no punishment: and if he could die a thousand times, he did not think that he could merit this worthily by any means whatsoever.

And so the patience of the blessed Martyr was crowned; the unrepentant malice of the torturer was delivered over to eternal torments. Mindful of this in his agony, the glorious Athlete of Christ did not shrink from prison. After the example of his Head, he endured reproaches, bore mockeries, feared not the scourges: and as many punishments as he suffered for Christ before death, so many sacrifices of himself did he offer. For what the Apostle had given him to drink, he held deeply within: that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the future glory which shall be revealed in us. And because this momentary and light tribulation works for us an eternal weight of glory in the heavens. Suspended from earthly things by love of this promise, and ineffably moved by the foretaste of heavenly sweetness, he said with the Psalmist: What have I in heaven, and what have I desired of you upon earth? My flesh and my heart have fainted: O God of my heart, and God is my portion for ever.

The four holy living creatures, which are foreseen by the spirit of prophecy as future realities, are described with subtle narration, when it is said: Four faces to each one, and four wings to each one. What is expressed by the face, but knowledge; and what by the wings, but flight? For by the face each one is recognized; by the wings, the bodies of birds are lifted into the heights. The face, therefore, pertains to faith, the wing to contemplation. For by faith we are known to almighty God, as he himself says of his sheep: I am the good shepherd, and I know my sheep, and my sheep know me. Who says again: I know those whom I have chosen. By contemplation, however, by which we are lifted above ourselves, we are raised as it were into the air.

When, therefore, the Hyades come with their rains, the sun is drawn to the higher regions of the sky: for when the knowledge of the Doctors shines forth, and our minds are watered by the shower of preaching, the warmth of faith is increased. And the earth, when drenched, advances to fruit as the light of the heavens blazes: because we bring forth more abundantly the harvest of good works, the more brightly we burn in the heart through the flame of sacred learning. And as through them day by day heavenly knowledge is more and more revealed to us, a springtime of interior light is opened for us, so that the new sun may shine upon our minds, and, being made known to us through their words, may sparkle more clearly each day. For as the end of the world presses on, heavenly wisdom advances, and grows more abundantly with time.

Now there are two kinds of persecutors: one that rages openly, and another that beguiles with feigning and deceit. Wishing to fortify and instruct us against both, the Saviour commands us above to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and here not to fear the slaughter of executioners; because, after death, neither the cruelty of the latter nor the dissembling of the former can endure. Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings? If, he says, the most insignificant creatures, and birds that fly hither and thither through the air, God cannot forget — you, who have been made in the image of the Creator, ought not to be terrified by those who kill the body; because he who governs irrational creatures does not cease to care for rational ones.

Now two things are commanded: to gird the loins and to hold lamps; that there be purity of chastity in the body, and the light of truth in action. For our Redeemer it is in no way possible for one to please without the other: whether it be he who does good yet still does not forsake the defilements of lust; or he who excels in chastity yet does not yet exercise himself through good works. Neither, therefore, is chastity great without good work, nor is any work good without chastity. But if both are practiced, it remains that whoever it may be should tend in hope toward the heavenly homeland, and should refrain from vices not for the sake of worldly honor.

Behold, the Lord sends out his disciples two by two to preach: that by this he may silently indicate to us that whoever has no charity toward another ought by no means to take up the office of preaching. And it is well said that he sent them before his face into every town and place where he himself was about to come. For the Lord follows his preachers: because preaching goes before, and then the Lord comes to the dwelling of our heart when the words of exhortation have run ahead; and thus truth is received into the mind.

"I am," he says, "the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser." Are the vinedresser and the vine one? According to this, then, Christ is the vine, according to what he says: "The Father is greater than I." But according to what he says: "I and the Father are one," he himself is also the vinedresser — not such as those who render service by working from without, but such as to give increase even from within. For neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God, who gives the increase. But certainly Christ is God, since the Word was God: wherefore he and the Father are one. And if the Word was made flesh, what he was not, what he was remains.

Therefore, salt that has lost its savour is good for nothing but to be cast out and trodden underfoot by men. He, then, is not trodden underfoot by men who suffers persecution; but rather he who, through fear of persecution, loses his savour. For only what is inferior can be trodden underfoot; but he is not inferior who, though he may endure much in the body upon earth, has his heart fixed in heaven.

And rightly did he climb the tree, that the good tree might bring forth good fruit, and that he, cut off from the wild olive by nature, and contrary to nature grafted into the good olive, might be able to bear the fruit of the law. For the root is holy, even if the branches are unprofitable. The people of the Gentiles, by the faith of the Resurrection, transcend their unfruitful glory, as if by a certain elevation of the body. Zacchaeus, therefore, is in the sycamore; the blind man is on the road: the Lord is on the point of showing mercy to one, and honours the other with the distinction of his lodging; he questions one in order to heal him, and invites himself, uninvited, to the other. For he knew that the reward of his hospitality would be abundant. Yet, though Zacchaeus had not yet heard the voice of the one inviting him, he had already seen his kindly affection.

"And four wings to each one": because they all proclaim the Lord, the Son of almighty God, our Lord Jesus Christ, with one accord and in harmony; and, raising the eyes of the mind to his divinity, they fly with the wing of contemplation. The face of the Evangelists therefore pertains to the humanity of the Lord, the wing to his divinity: for upon him whom they behold in the body, they fix their face, as it were; but as they declare him to be uncircumscribed and incorporeal by reason of his divinity, they are lifted, as it were, into the air by the wing of contemplation. Because, therefore, the faith of his Incarnation is one in all, and the contemplation of his divinity is equal in each one, it is rightly said here: "Four faces to each one, and four wings to each one."

"Be like men who await their Lord, when he returns from the wedding feast: that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once." The Lord comes when he hastens to judgment; and he knocks when, through the afflictions of sickness, he signals that death is near. To him we open at once, if we receive him with love. For he who trembles at departing from the body does not wish to open to the judge who is knocking; and he fears to see as a judge him whom he remembers having despised. But he who is secure in his hope and his deeds opens at once to one who knocks, for he awaits the judge with joy; and when the time of approaching death draws near, he rejoices in the thought of the glory of retribution.

Who are designated by the name of the Hyades, who come after the Orions, if not the Doctors of the holy Church? Who, when the Martyrs had been taken away, came to the knowledge of the world at a time when faith shines more brightly, and when, the winter of unbelief being repressed, the sun of truth burns more intensely in the hearts of the faithful. Who, when the storm of persecution had passed and the long nights of unbelief had been fulfilled, arose for the holy Church at a time when a more luminous year was already opening for her through the spring of faith.
From the Book of Saint Ambrose the Bishop on Widows
Prope finem

I behold this field of the Church as fertile: now blooming with the flower of virginity, now flourishing with the dignity of widowhood, now also abounding with the fruits of marriage. For although they are diverse, they are all fruits of one field; and lilies of the garden are not as many as the ears of the harvest, the sheaves of the fields; and broad expanses of plain are prepared to receive seeds, rather than to repay the fields with their returned fruits. Good, then, is widowhood, praised so many times by apostolic judgment. For widowhood is the teacher of faith, the teacher of chastity.

On the occasion of this passage, certain people introduce the thousand years after the Resurrection, saying that then the hundredfold of all the things we have left behind, along with eternal life, is to be rendered to us: not understanding that, if the reward were fitting in the other cases, in the matter of wives it would appear unseemly — that he who has left one wife for the Lord's sake should receive a hundred in the future. The meaning, therefore, is this: he who has left carnal things for the Saviour's sake shall receive spiritual ones: which, by comparison and by their own worth, will be as if a hundredfold number were compared with a small number.

The sword is the sharpest of all weapons, in which resides the authority of power, the severity of judgment, and the punishment of sins. And by the name of this weapon, the frequent testimony of the prophets declares that the preaching of the new Gospel is signified. Let us therefore recall that the word of God is named by the sword; which sword was sent upon the earth, that is, the preaching of it was infused into the hearts of men. And there arises a grave dissension within a single household, and those of the household shall be enemies to the new man; because he who has been divided from them by the word of God will rejoice to remain both interior and exterior, that is, both body and soul, in the newness of the spirit.

She is the mother of him who was begotten by the Father before all beginning; whom Angels and men acknowledge as Lord of all things. Do you wish to know how much this Virgin excels the heavenly Powers? They stand before him with fear and trembling, veiling their faces; she offers to him the human race she has borne. Through her we obtain pardon even for sins. Hail, therefore, O Mother, O heaven, O maiden, O virgin, O throne. The ornament, glory, and foundation of our Church: pray without ceasing to Jesus, your Son and our Lord, that through you we may find mercy on the day of judgment, and may obtain the good things laid up for those who love God, by the grace and kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ: with whom, to the Father and likewise to the Holy Spirit, be glory, honor, and dominion, now and always, for ever and ever. Amen.

This cloud, passing beyond the air, the Angels, and the stars, found the Word of God in the very bosom of the Father, and drank him in with all her heart. For who, having found so great a good, would leave it? "Your name is as oil poured out; therefore young women have loved you, and have drawn you to themselves." Finally, those words — "they who neither marry nor are given in marriage, but shall be as the angels of God in heaven" — are not mine to withhold. Let no one wonder, then, if virgins are compared to the Angels, who are united to the Lord of the Angels.

These indeed love their neighbor, and yet do not attain those sublime rewards of love: because they bestow their love not spiritually but carnally. Hence, when the Lord said: "This is my commandment, that you love one another," he immediately added: "as I have loved you." As if to say openly: Love in the same way that I have loved you. In this matter, dearest brothers, it must be carefully discerned that the ancient enemy, while drawing our mind toward love of temporal things, stirs up against us a weaker neighbor, who strives to take away those very things that we love.

For herein Isaiah says to those same preachers: "Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God." And herein the Psalmist says to the children: "Make a way for him who ascends above the west." The Lord ascends above the west: for from the very point where he set in his Passion, he manifested his greater glory by rising again. He ascends above the west, for he trampled down by rising again the death which he had endured. We therefore make a way for him who ascends above the west, when we proclaim his glory to your minds, so that he himself, coming after, may illuminate them by the presence of his love.

When therefore Jesus had received the vinegar, he said: "It is consummated" — and bowing his head, he gave up his spirit. The Saviour declares that it is now consummated, because the power of the Jews to rage against him reached its end through his death. For what did they not devise? What of the utmost cruelty against his human nature was left undone? What manner of striking, what manner of insult was not employed? Rightly, therefore, he says that it is consummated. And since it was now time for him to preach also to the spirits in the underworld — for he had come to be Lord of the living and the dead alike — he accepted death for our sake: and this suffering proper to our nature he willingly underwent according to the flesh, even though, as God, he is life by nature, so that, having despoiled the underworld, he might become, as the Scriptures say, the first-fruits of those who sleep and the first-born of the dead, and so bestow upon our nature the return to life.

For before the coming of Christ, the way of life was unknown, untrodden by the footstep of any who had yet risen again. But when the Lord rose, it was made known and trodden by the feet of many — of whom the holy Evangelist says: "The bodies of many saints rose with him and entered into the holy city." Hence, when the Lord said at his Resurrection: "You have made known to me the ways of life," we too can now say to the Lord: "You have made known to us the ways of life." For he made known to us the ways of life, who revealed to us the path to life. For he made known to me the ways of life, when he taught me faith, mercy, justice, and chastity: for by these paths one arrives at salvation.

Now every person subsists in the five bodily senses; and the fivefold number, doubled, makes ten. And since the multitude of the faithful is gathered from both sexes, the holy Church is declared to be like ten virgins. In which, because the evil are mixed with the good and the reprobate with the elect, she is rightly said to be like both wise and foolish virgins. For there are many who are continent, who guard themselves from exterior appetite and are drawn by hope toward interior things, who mortify the flesh, and with all desire long for their heavenly homeland, who seek eternal rewards, and do not wish to receive the praise of men for their labors. These indeed do not place their glory in the mouth of men, but conceal it within their conscience. And there are many who afflict the body through abstinence, but who seek human favor for that very abstinence.

At the regeneration, when the Son of Man shall sit upon the throne of his majesty — when even the dead shall rise incorruptible from corruption — you also shall sit upon twelve thrones judging, and you shall condemn the twelve tribes of Israel: because while you believed, they refused to believe. And everyone who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for my name's sake shall receive a hundredfold and shall possess eternal life. This passage accords with that saying in which the Saviour speaks: "I have not come to send peace, but a sword. For I have come to separate a man from his father, and a daughter from her mother, and a daughter-in-law from her mother-in-law: and a man's enemies shall be those of his own household." Those, therefore, who for the faith of Christ and the preaching of the Gospel have despised all affections, and riches, and the pleasures of the world, shall receive a hundredfold and shall possess eternal life.

For throughout the whole Church, "You are Christ, the Son of the living God" is said daily by Peter; and every tongue that confesses the Lord is imbued with the teaching of this voice. This faith conquers the devil and looses the bonds of his captives. This faith, snatching men from the world, inserts them into heaven, and the gates of hell cannot prevail against it. For it is fortified by God with such solidity that neither the wickedness of heresy could ever corrupt it, nor the perfidy of paganism overcome it. In these ways, then, dearest ones, let this day's festival be celebrated with rational worship, so that in the person of my humility it may be he who is understood, it may be he who is honored, in whom the solicitude of all pastors perseveres with the care of the sheep entrusted to them, and whose dignity does not fail even in an unworthy heir.

He bowed his head. For this is what happens to the dying when the vigor of the flesh is now spent and the soul, which holds the body together, departs: a bowing of the head. This, therefore, is the language the Evangelist used. So also "gave up his spirit" is said after the manner of our experience; for many are said to be extinguished and to die in this way. Although it seems to me that the Evangelist did not say simply that he died, but that he gave up his spirit, because he commended his soul into the hands of God the Father, as he himself said: "Father, into your hands I commend my spirit." This furnishes us with a great foundation and source of hope.

At that time, Jesus said to his disciples: This is my commandment: that you love one another, as I have loved you. Et cetera.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope.
Homilia 27. in Evangelia.

Since all the sacred eloquences are full of the Lord's commandments, what is the meaning of the Lord's saying of charity as if it were a singular commandment: "This is my commandment, that you love one another" — unless it be that all commandments are of charity alone, and all are one commandment? Because whatever is commanded is grounded in charity alone. For as many branches come forth from one root, so many virtues are generated from one charity. And the branch of good work has no greenness in it unless it abides in the root of charity.

At that time, Jesus, knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said: I thirst. Et cetera.

A Homily of Saint Cyril, Bishop of Alexandria
Comment. in Ioannem. Lib. 12., cap. 35

When all things had been wrought with the savage impiety of the Jews, and nothing was lacking to the sum of their cruelty, at last the most holy flesh of Christ suffers something natural. For dried out by many and varied torments, it is tormented by thirst. For torments have great power to provoke thirst; for exciting the innate heat, they either consume what is moist in the body's depths, or with fiery ardors they burn the entrails of the sufferer. As Christ, therefore, willingly endured the other sufferings, so also he willingly endured this one. He asks, therefore, to drink; but they were so far removed from all humanity that instead of a helpful and pleasant draught they brought something harmful and bitter, and turned the appearance of kindness, which they seemed to show, into impiety. For when they gave to him who asked, they seemed to take up the manner of charity; but it is not possible for Scripture to lie, in which it is said in the person of Christ: "And they gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink."

A Homily of Saint Augustine the Bishop
Tract. 80 in Ioannem

This passage of the Gospel, brethren, in which the Lord calls himself the vine and his disciples the branches, he speaks according to what he is as the head of the Church and we as his members, the mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. For the vine and the branches are of one nature. Therefore, because he was God, whose nature we do not share, he became man, so that in him human nature might be the vine, of which we too, as human beings, might be branches.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilia 13 in Evang.

The reading of the holy Gospel just proclaimed, dearest brethren, is clear enough. But lest to some its very plainness seem perhaps too deep, we pass through it briefly, so that its exposition may be made known to those who do not yet understand it, without being burdensome to those who do. The Lord says: Let your waists be girded. For we gird our loins when we restrain the lust of the flesh through continence. But because it is not enough to do no evil unless one also strives to labor at good works, there is immediately added: And let lamps be burning in your hands. We hold burning lamps in our hands when by our good works we show our neighbors the example of light. Concerning which works the Lord says: Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and may glorify your Father who is in heaven.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. And so forth.

A Homily of the Venerable Bede the Priest
Lib. 4 in Lucam, cap. 12

Concerning this leaven the Apostle gave instruction: Therefore, let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. For just as a little leaven corrupts the whole mass of dough into which it is thrown, and soon taints the entire mixture with its own flavor; so likewise simulation, once it has steeped the mind, will defraud it of all the sincerity and truth of the virtues. The meaning is therefore: Beware lest you imitate dissemblers; because the day of judgment will come, on which both your virtue will be revealed to all, and their hypocrisy will be unmasked.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: And when you will have heard of battles and seditions, do not be terrified. These things must happen first. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilia 35 in Evangel.

Our Lord and Redeemer announces the evils that precede the perishing of the world, so that those things which are to come may disturb us the less, in proportion as they have been foreknown. For darts strike less deeply when they are seen in advance; and we take up the evils of the world more tolerably when we are fortified against them by the shield of foreknowledge. For behold, he says: And when you will have heard of battles and seditions, do not be terrified. These things must happen first, but the end is not so soon. The words of our Redeemer are to be weighed carefully: by them he declares that we are to suffer different things inwardly and outwardly; for battles belong to enemies, while seditions belong to citizens. Therefore, to signify that we shall be troubled both within and without, he tells us that we shall suffer one thing from enemies, another from brethren.

At that time: Jesus descended with them and stood in a level place, with a multitude of his disciples and a copious multitude of people from all of Judea and Jerusalem and the seacoast, and Tyre and Sidon. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Ambrose the Bishop
Lib. 5. in Lucam. Cap. 6., post init.

Observe all things carefully: how he ascends with the Apostles and descends to the crowds. For how could the crowd see Christ except in a lowly place? It does not follow to the heights; it does not climb to the lofty. And so, where he descended, he found the sick: for the sick cannot be on the heights. Hence Matthew also teaches that the weak were healed in the lower places. For each one must first be healed, so that, as the virtues advance step by step, he may be able to ascend the mountain; and therefore he heals each one in the lower places, that is, he draws him back from lust, he turns away the injury of blindness. He descended to our wounds: so that by a certain use and abundance of his nature, he might make us sharers in the heavenly kingdom.

At that time: The Lord designated another seventy-two, and sent them in pairs before his face, into every city and place where he was to arrive. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilia 17 in Evangelia

Our Lord and Savior, dearest brethren, admonishes us sometimes by words and sometimes by deeds. His very acts are precepts: for what he does in silence reveals what we ought to do. Behold, he sends the disciples forth in pairs to preach; for there are two commandments of charity, namely, the love of God and the love of neighbor; and charity cannot exist between fewer than two. For no one is said properly to have charity toward himself alone: but love reaches out to another, so that it may be charity.
At that time: Now it happened that, when all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized; and as he was praying, heaven was opened.
Lib. 23, contra Faust. cap. 7. 8.

Thus it was said from heaven over the water of the Jordan: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased — just as it was also said on the mountain. Nor does the fact that there too the voice sounded from heaven mean that the Son of God was not there before; since from the womb of the Virgin he assumed the form of a servant, who, though he was in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped. Moreover, the same Apostle Paul says most plainly in another place: But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive the adoption of sons. He himself, then, is the Son of God, who is also the Lord of David according to divinity, and likewise the Son of David from the seed of David according to the flesh.

At that time: Jesus said to the crowds: If anyone comes to me, and does not hate his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and yes, even his own life, he is not able to be my disciple. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homil. 37 in Evangelia

If we consider, dearest brethren, how great and how many are the things promised to us in heaven, all that is possessed on earth grows cheap in the soul. For earthly substance, compared to heavenly happiness, is a burden, not a support. Temporal life, compared to eternal life, ought rather to be called death than life. For what is the daily decline of corruption but a certain prolonged dying? Yet what tongue can tell, or what mind can grasp, how great are the joys of that heavenly city: to be present among the choirs of angels, to stand before the glory of the Creator with the most blessed spirits, to behold the very face of God, to see the uncircumscribed light, to be afflicted by no fear of death, to rejoice in the gift of eternal incorruption?

At that time: Jesus entered and walked through Jericho. And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, and he was the leader of the tax collectors, and he was wealthy. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Ambrose the Bishop
Lib. 8 in Luc., prope finem

Zacchaeus, small in stature — that is, exalted by no dignity of inborn nobility, lowly in merit as the people of the nations — upon hearing of the coming of the Lord Savior, whom his own had not received, desired to see him. But no one easily sees Jesus; no one can see Jesus while standing on the earth. And because he had neither prophets nor the law, as it were the natural grace of form, he climbed a sycamore tree, treading underfoot with his step the vanity of the Jews, and also correcting the errors of his earlier life. And therefore Jesus received him as a guest in the inner chamber of his house.

At that time: As Jesus was speaking to the crowds, a certain woman from the crowd, lifting up her voice, said to him: Blessed is the womb that bore you. And so forth.

A Homily of the Venerable Bede the Priest
Lib 4. cap. 49. in Luc. 11.

This woman shows herself to be of great devotion and faith who, while the scribes and Pharisees were at once tempting and blaspheming the Lord, recognizes his Incarnation before all others with such sincerity, and confesses it with such confidence, as to confound both the calumny of the present rulers and the perfidy of future heretics. For just as the Jews of that time, by blaspheming the works of the Holy Spirit, denied that he was the true Son of God, consubstantial with the Father; so the heretics afterwards, by denying that Mary is ever-Virgin, claimed that it was not right to confess the Only-Begotten Son of God — to whom, by the power of the Holy Spirit at work, the flesh of his human members was born — as the true Son of man, consubstantial with his mother.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its saltiness, with what will it be salted? And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Augustine the Bishop
Lib. 1 de Sermone Domini in monte, cap. 6

The Lord shows that those are to be judged foolish who, either by pursuing an abundance of temporal goods or by fearing the want of them, lose the eternal, which can neither be given nor taken away by men. And so: if salt loses its saltiness, with what will it be salted? That is, if you — through whom the peoples are to be seasoned in a certain manner — have lost the kingdoms of heaven through fear of temporal persecutions, who will be the people by whom error is removed from you, since God has chosen you as the very ones through whom he would remove the error of the rest?

At that time: Jesus spoke this parable to his disciples: The kingdom of heaven shall be like ten virgins, who, taking their lamps, went out to meet the groom and the bride. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilía 12 in Evangelia

I often admonish you, dearest brethren, to flee wicked works and to avoid the defilements of this world; but today's reading of the holy Gospel compels me to say that you must also hold fast, with great caution, to the good things you do, lest through what is done rightly by you, human favor or approval be sought; lest the appetite for praise steal in, and what is shown outwardly be emptied of its inward reward. For behold, by the voice of the Redeemer ten virgins are spoken of — all are called virgins, and yet not all were received within the gate of blessedness; because some of them, while seeking outward glory from their virginity, refused to have oil in their vessels.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: Nothing is covered that shall not be revealed, nor hidden that shall not be known. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Hilary the Bishop
Comment. in Matthaeum, can. 10 post medium

The Lord points to the day of judgment, which will betray the hidden conscience of our will; and those things which are now considered secret, it will lay bare in the light of public knowledge. Therefore, he warns us not to fear the threats, the plots, or the powers of those who persecute: for the day of judgment will reveal that all these were as nothing and empty. And what I say to you in darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, preach above the rooftops. We do not read that the Lord was accustomed to speak at night or to impart his teaching in darkness; but because all his words are darkness to the carnal, and his word is night to the faithless.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: Be vigilant. For you do not know at what hour your Lord will return. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Hilary the Bishop
Comment. in Matth. Can 26

So that we might know, though in silence, that ignorance of that day is for the benefit of all, the Lord admonished us to be watchful because of the coming of the thief, and to remain fixed in all the works of his commandments by the assiduous practice of prayer. For he shows the devil to be a thief, ever watchful to seize spoils from us and lying in ambush for the dwelling places of our bodies: so that, when we are careless and given to sleep, he might pierce them with the shafts and enticements of his designs. We must therefore be prepared: for ignorance of the day stirs up an intent solicitude of watchful expectation.

At that time: Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, and he questioned his disciples, saying: Who do men say that the Son of man is? And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Leo the Pope
Sermo 2 in anniversario assumpt. suæ, ante medium

When, as is revealed by the Gospel reading, the Lord had asked the disciples who — with many holding different opinions — they believed him to be, and blessed Peter had answered saying: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God; the Lord said: Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I say to you, that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of Hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you shall release on earth shall be released in heaven. The disposition of truth therefore endures, and blessed Peter, persevering in the strength of the rock he received, has not abandoned the governance of the Church entrusted to him.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: Do not think that I came to send peace upon the earth; I came, not to send peace, but the sword. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Hilary the Bishop
Comment. in Matth., can. 10

What is this division? For among the first precepts of the law we received: Honor your father and your mother; and the Lord himself says: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you. What then does it mean that a sword is sent rather upon the earth, and a son is separated from his father, and a daughter from her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and the enemies of a man are those of his own household? For henceforth public authority will be given over to impiety. Everywhere hatred, everywhere wars, and the sword of the Lord raging between father and son and between daughter and mother.

At that time: Jesus said to his disciples: If anyone is willing to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilia 32 in Evang.

Because our Lord and Redeemer, the new man, came into the world, he gave new commandments to the world. For he set the newness of his own way in opposition to our old life nurtured in vices. What did the old man, what did the carnal man know, except to hold fast to what was his own, to seize what belonged to others if he could; to covet it if he could not? But the heavenly physician applies remedies contrary to each vice in turn. For just as in the art of medicine, hot ailments are treated with cold remedies and cold with hot; so our Lord set contrary medicines against sins, prescribing continence for the licentious, generosity for the covetous, gentleness for the wrathful, humility for the proud.
A Reading from the holy Gospel according to Matthew.

At that time: Peter said to Jesus: Behold, we have left behind all things, and we have followed you. So then, what will be for us? And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Jerome the Priest.
Lib. 3. in Matth. cap. 19.

Great confidence! Peter was a fisherman; he had not been wealthy; he earned his food by hand and by craft. And yet he speaks with confidence: We have left behind all things. And because it is not enough merely to leave things behind, he adds what is perfect: And we have followed you. We have done what you commanded; what reward, then, will you give us? But Jesus said to them: Amen I say to you, that you who have followed me, at the resurrection, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, shall also sit on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. He did not say: Who have left behind all things — for the philosopher Crates also did this, and many others despised riches; but: Who have followed me — which belongs properly to the Apostles and to believers.

At that time: Jesus spoke this parable to his disciples: A man setting out on a long journey called his servants and delivered to them his goods. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilia 9 in Evangelia

The reading of the holy Gospel, dearest brethren, admonishes us to consider carefully lest we who are seen to have received more than others in this world be judged more severely for it by the Author of the world. For when gifts are increased, the reckoning of the gifts increases as well. Therefore, each one ought to be so much the more humble and prompt in serving God in proportion to the gift he has received, as he sees himself more obligated in giving an account. Behold, the man who goes on a long journey calls his servants and distributes talents among them for their business. But after a long time he returns to settle accounts: he rewards those who have labored well for the profit they bring; but he condemns the servant who has been sluggish in good work.

At that time: Jesus spoke this parable to his disciples: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field. And so forth.

A Homily of Saint Gregory the Pope
Homilia 11 in Evangelia

The Kingdom of Heaven, dearest brethren, is therefore said to be like earthly things, so that, from those things which the mind knows, it may rise to the unknown things which it does not know: in order that, by the example of visible things, it may be drawn swiftly to the invisible, and, as though warmed by rubbing against what it has learned by experience, it may grow hot; so that, through what it knows how to love as familiar, it may also learn to love the unknown. For behold, the Kingdom of Heaven is likened to a treasure hidden in a field; which, when a man finds it, he hides it, and out of joy for it he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.

Truly a great wonder was the blessed ever-Virgin Mary, most beloved brethren. For what greater or more glorious thing has ever at any time been found, or ever could be found? She alone surpassed the breadth of heaven and earth. What is holier than she? Not Prophets, not Apostles, not Martyrs, not Patriarchs, not Angels, not Thrones, not Dominations, not Seraphim, not Cherubim; nor, finally, can any other thing whatsoever, among all created things visible or invisible, be found greater or more excellent. We saw him, it says, and he had no appearance, nor beauty beyond the sons of men, but he was the reproach of men and as a leper, the least of men, plainly a man of sorrows struck and humbled by God; so that there was no comeliness in him, nor beauty. Not without reason are the holy Doctors designated by the name of the Hyades. For in the Greek tongue, hyetos means rain, and the Hyades received their name from rain, because when they rise they undoubtedly bring showers. Well, then, were they expressed by the name of the Hyades, those who, set in the face of the sky, as it were, for the good of the universal Church, poured down upon the parched earth of the human breast the rains of holy preaching. There is no doubt that this Joseph was a good and faithful man — Joseph, to whom the Mother of the Savior was betrothed. The commandments of the Lord are therefore both many and one: many in the diversity of action, one in the root of love. In what manner, however, this love is to be kept, he himself makes clear, who in very many sentences of his Scripture commands that friends be loved in him, and enemies for his sake. For he truly has charity who loves a friend in God, and loves an enemy for God's sake. For there are some who love their neighbors, but through an affection of kinship and of the flesh: against whom, in this love, the sacred writings do not argue. Therefore the four faces are one: for if you inquire what Matthew thinks concerning the Incarnation of the Lord, he thinks precisely what Mark, Luke, and John think. In this matter, it must also be noted that the treasure, once found, is hidden so that it may be kept safe: for he does not suffice to guard the zeal of heavenly desire from evil spirits, who does not hide it from human praise. For in this present life we are, as it were, on the road by which we press on toward our homeland. But the evil spirits beset our way like so many brigands. He who carries his treasure openly on the road invites plunder. This I say not so that our neighbors may not see our good works — since it is written: Let your good works be seen, that they may glorify your Father who is in heaven — but so that we may not seek outward praise for what we do. So let the work be in public, but the intention remain hidden; that we may both offer our neighbors the example of a good work, and yet, through the intention by which we seek to please God alone, may always desire what is secret.
