Near Minden, in Germany, the Translation of Saint Felicianus, Bishop of Foligno and Martyr; a portion of his sacred relics, brought into Germany from the Umbrian city of Foligno, was deposited there—the city where he had once suffered on the twenty-fourth of January.
At Paris, likewise the Translation of the holy Martyrs George the Deacon and Aurelius, from the Spanish city of Córdoba, in which both had formerly completed their martyrdom on the twenty-seventh of July, together with three other companions.

The twentieth of September

At Pozzuoli, in Campania, the holy Martyrs Januarius, Bishop of the city of Benevento; his Deacon Festus and the Lector Desiderius; Sossius, Deacon of the Church of Misenum; Proculus, Deacon of Pozzuoli; Eutychus and Acutius. All of these, after imprisonment and chains, were beheaded under the Emperor Diocletian. The body of Saint Januarius was carried to Naples and honorably entombed in the church there; where also the blood of the most blessed Martyr, preserved in a glass vial, is seen, when placed before his severed head, to liquefy and bubble up as if fresh.
In Palestine, the holy Martyrs and Bishops of Egypt: Peleus, Nilus, and Elias; who, in the time of the Diocletianic persecution, were consumed by fire for Christ, together with many Clergy.
At Nocera, the birth into heaven of the holy Martyrs Felix and Constance, who suffered under Nero.
On the same day, the holy Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Dorymedon, under the Emperor Probus. Of these, Sabbatius was beaten with rods at Antioch by order of the prefect Atticus until he gave up his spirit; while Trophimus was sent to Synnas, in Phrygia, before the prefect Perenninus, where, after many torments, he completed his martyrdom by beheading together with the Senator Dorymedon.
At Eleutheropolis, in Palestine, Saint Susanna, Virgin and Martyr; who, born of the pagan priest Arthmeus and a Jewish woman named Martha, was converted to the Christian faith after her parents' death, and, on account of that same faith, variously tortured and cast into prison by the Prefect Alexander, she passed away there in prayer to her Spouse.
At Córdoba, in Spain, Saint Pomposa, Virgin and Martyr; who, in the Arabian persecution, was beheaded with a sword for her fearless confession of Christ, and received the palm.
At Canterbury, Saint Theodore, Bishop, who, sent to England by the blessed Pope Vitalian, shone forth in learning and holiness.
At Tours, in Gaul, Saint Eustochius, Bishop, a man of great virtues.
In the territory of Langres, Saint Sequanus, Priest and Confessor.
At Barcelona, in Spain, blessed Mary of Cervelló, Virgin, of the Order of Our Lady of Mercy for the Redemption of Captives; who, on account of the present aid she bestows upon those who invoke her, is commonly called Mary of Help.
In the village of Druelle, in the diocese of Rodez, in Gaul, Saint Mary Guillélmine-Émilie de Rodat, Virgin, foundress of the Congregation of the Sisters of the Holy Family, most devoted to educating girls and relieving the poor, who was enrolled among the holy Virgins by Pope Pius XII.

The twentieth of August

In the territory of Langres, the deposition of Saint Bernard, first Abbot of Clairvaux, glorious in life, learning, and miracles, whom Pope Pius VIII declared a Doctor of the universal Church and confirmed him as such.
At Rome, the deposition of Saint Pius X, Pope and Confessor, outstanding for integrity of faith and an invincible champion of ecclesiastical liberty, and remarkable for zeal for religion, whose feast is recalled on the third of September.
Near Monte Senario, in Etruria, the birth into heaven of Saint Manettus, Confessor, one of the seven Founders of the Order of the Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary; who, while singing hymns to her, breathed his last. His feast and that of his companions is celebrated on the day before the Ides of February.
In Judea, Saint Samuel the Prophet, whose holy bones (as blessed Jerome writes) the Emperor Arcadius transferred to Constantinople and placed near the Seventh milestone.
In Cyprus, Saint Lucius, Senator, who, having witnessed the steadfastness of Theodore, Bishop of Cyrene, in his martyrdom, was converted to the faith of Christ and also drew the prefect Dignianum to it; and sailing with him to Cyprus, where he saw other Christians crowned for confessing the Lord, offered himself willingly and merited the same crown of martyrdom by decapitation.
In Thrace, the holy Thirty-Seven Martyrs, who, under the prefect Appellianus, for the faith of Christ, had their hands and feet cut off and were cast into a burning furnace.
In the same place, the holy Martyrs Severus and Memnon the Centurion; who, put to death in the same manner, departed as victors into heaven.
At Córdoba, in Spain, the holy Martyrs Leovigild and Christopher, Monks, who, in the Arabian persecution, imprisoned for the defense of the Christian faith and soon after beheaded and given to the flames, obtained the palm of martyrdom.
On the island of Hérieu, Saint Philibert, Abbot.
At Rome, blessed Porphyrius, who was a man of God, who instructed the holy Martyr Agapitus in the faith and teaching of Christ.
In the castle of Cainone, in Gaul, Saint Maximus, Confessor, who was a disciple of the blessed Bishop Martin.

The twenty-second of March

At Narbonne, in Gaul, the birth into heaven of Saint Paul, Bishop and disciple of the Apostles, who is said to have been Sergius Paulus the Proconsul. He was baptized by the blessed Apostle Paul and, when Paul was journeying into Spain, was left by him at Narbonne and there granted the dignity of Bishop; and there, having fulfilled the office of preaching with diligence, he departed to heaven renowned for miracles.
At Terracina, in Campania, Saint Epaphroditus, disciple of the Apostles, who was ordained Bishop of that city by the blessed Apostle Peter.
At Ancyra, in Galatia, Saint Basil, Priest and Martyr, who, under Julian the Apostate, was afflicted with the most grievous torments and gave back his soul to God.
At Carthage, Saint Octavian the Archdeacon, and many thousands of Martyrs, who were slain by the Vandals for the Catholic faith.
In Africa, the holy Martyrs Saturninus and nine others.
In Galatia, the birth into heaven of the holy Martyrs Callinicus and Basilissa.
At Rome, Saint Pope Zachary, who governed God's Church with the greatest vigilance and, renowned for his merits, rested in peace.
At Carthage, Saint Deogratias, Bishop of Carthage, who redeemed many captives brought from Rome by the Vandals, and celebrated for other holy works, rested in the Lord.
At Osimo, in Picenum, Saint Benvenutus, Bishop.
At Rome, Saint Lea, Widow, whose virtues and passing to God Saint Jerome describes.

The twenty-second of July

Near Marseilles, in Gaul, the birth into heaven of Saint Mary Magdalene, from whom the Lord cast out seven demons, and who merited to be the first to see the Savior himself risen from the dead.
At Lisbon, in Portugal, the birth into heaven of Saint Lawrence of Brindisi, Confessor, of the Order of Friars Minor Capuchin, whom Pope Leo XIII, illustrious for the preaching of the word of God, heavenly learning, pontifical legations, and achievements happily accomplished for the glory of God and the benefit of the Church, enrolled in the catalogue of the Saints; and Pope John XXIII declared him a Doctor of the universal Church and ordered his feast to be celebrated on the preceding day.
At Philippi, in Macedonia, Saint Syntyche, of whom the blessed Apostle Paul makes mention.
At Ancyra, in Galatia, the birth into heaven of Saint Plato, Martyr, who, under the vicarius Agrippinus, was beaten with rods, torn with iron hooks, afflicted with other most savage forms of torture, and at last, with his head cut off, gave back his unconquered soul to God. His miracles in assisting captives are attested by the Acts of the Second Council of Nicaea.
In Cyprus, Saint Theophilus the Praetor, who was captured by the Arabs and, when he could not be moved by gifts or threats to deny Christ, was put to death by the sword.
At Antioch, Saint Cyril, Bishop, conspicuous for learning and holiness.
At Menat, in the territory of Auvergne, Saint Menelaüs, Abbot.
In the monastery of Fontenelle, in Gaul, Saint Wandregisilus, Abbot, renowned for miracles; whose body was afterward transferred to the monastery of Saint Peter at Ghent, in Flanders.
At Scythopolis, in Palestine, Saint Joseph the Count.

The twenty-second of November

At Jerusalem, the Presentation of the blessed Mother of God, the Virgin Mary, in the Temple.
On the same day, the birth into heaven of blessed Rufus, of whom the blessed Apostle Paul writes to the Romans.
At Rome, the passion of the holy Celsus and Clement.
At Rheims, in Gaul, Saint Albert, Bishop of Liège and Martyr; who was killed in defense of ecclesiastical liberty.
Near the Tiber's mouth, the birth into heaven of the holy Martyrs Demetrius and Honorius.
In Spain, the holy Martyrs Honorius, Eutychius, and Stephen.
In Pamphylia, Saint Heliodorus, Martyr, in the persecution under Aurelian, under the prefect Aetius. After him, however, his very torturers, converted to the faith, were drowned in the sea.
At Rome, Saint Pope Gelasius I, conspicuous for learning and holiness.
At Verona, Saint Maurus, Bishop and Confessor.
In the monastery of Bobbio, the deposition of Saint Columbanus, Abbot, who, founder of many monasteries and father of countless monks, renowned for many virtues, rested in a good old age.

The twenty-second of January

At Valencia, in Tarraconensian Spain, Saint Vincent, Levite and Martyr; who, under the most impious prefect Dacianus, endured imprisonment, hunger, the rack, the dislocation of his limbs, red-hot iron plates, a burning iron grate, and other kinds of torment, and soared to the reward of martyrdom in heaven; the noble triumph of whose passion Prudentius celebrates in splendid verse, and whom the blessed Augustine and Saint Pope Leo commend with the highest praise.
Near Bethsaloe, in Assyria, Saint Anastasius the Persian Monk, who, after many torments of prison, beatings, and chains which he had endured in Caesarea of Palestine, was afflicted with many punishments by Chosroes, King of the Persians, and at last was beheaded, having first sent seventy companions, who had been drowned in a river, ahead of him to martyrdom. His head was brought to Rome, to the Aquae Salviae, together with his venerable image, by the sight of which, as the Acts of the Second Council of Nicaea attest, demons are put to flight and diseases are cured.
At Embrun, in Gaul, the holy Martyrs Vincent, Orontius, and Victor, who were crowned with martyrdom in the persecution of Diocletian.
At Novara, Saint Gaudentius, Bishop and Confessor.
At Sora, Saint Dominic, Abbot, renowned for miracles.

The twenty-second of June

At Rome, Saint Aloysius Gonzaga, Cleric of the Society of Jesus and Confessor, most renowned for contempt of princely rank and innocence of life, whom, enrolled in the catalogue of the Saints by the Supreme Pontiff Benedict XIII and given as Patron especially to studious youth, Pope Pius XI solemnly confirmed and again declared the heavenly Patron of all Christian youth.
Likewise at Rome, Saint Demetria, Virgin, who, daughter of the holy Martyrs Flavian and Dafrosa and sister of the holy Virgin and Martyr Bibiana, was herself also crowned with martyrdom under Julian the Apostate.
On the same day, Saint Eusebius, Bishop of Samosata; who, in the time of the Arian Emperor Constantius, visited the churches of God in disguise under a soldier's garb to strengthen them in the Catholic faith. Afterwards, under Valens, he was exiled to Thrace; but, when peace was restored to the Church in the time of Theodosius, recalled from exile, he at last, while again visiting the churches, had his head broken by a tile thrown upon him from above by an Arian woman, and thus died a Martyr.
At Iconium, in Lycaonia, Saint Terentius, Bishop and Martyr.
At Syracuse, in Sicily, the birth into heaven of the holy Martyrs Rufinus and Martia.
In Africa, the holy Martyrs Cyriacus and Apollinaris.
At Mainz, Saint Alban, Martyr, who, for the faith of Christ, after long labors and hard struggles, was found worthy of the crown of life.
At Pavia, Saint Urciscenus, Bishop and Confessor.
Near Tongres, Saint Martin, Bishop.
In the district of Evreux, Saint Leufredus, Abbot.

The twenty-second of May

At Rome, the holy Martyrs Faustinus, Timothy, and Venustus.
In Africa, the holy Martyrs Castus and Emilius, who completed their martyrdom through the fire of suffering. These men (as the blessed Cyprian writes), defeated in their first encounter, the Lord restored as victors in the second contest, so that those who had given way before fire might become stronger in fire.
At Comana, in Pontus, Saint Basiliscus, Martyr, who, under the Emperor Maximian and the prefect Agrippa, was shod with iron sandals fitted with red-hot nails, and after enduring many other torments, was at last beheaded and thrown into a river, and thus attained the glory of martyrdom.
In Corsica, Saint Julia, Virgin, who was crowned with the punishment of the cross.
In Spain, Saint Quiteria, Virgin and Martyr.
At Ravenna, Saint Marcian, Bishop and Confessor.
At Pistoia, in Tuscany, blessed Atto, Bishop, of the Order of Vallombrosa.
In the district of Auxerre, blessed Romanus, Abbot, who ministered to Saint Benedict in his cave; afterward departing to Gaul, he built a monastery there and left behind many children of holiness, and rested in the Lord.
Near Aquino, Saint Fulco, Confessor.
At Auxerre, Saint Helena, Virgin.
At Cascia, in Umbria, Saint Rita, Widow, Nun of the Order of Hermits of Saint Augustine; who, after wedded life in the world, loved Christ, her eternal Spouse, with singular devotion.

The twenty-second of December

At Rome, on the Via Lavicana, between the two Laurels, the birth into heaven of thirty holy Martyrs, who were all crowned with martyrdom on one day in the persecution of Diocletian.
Likewise at Rome, Saint Flavian, former Prefect, husband of the blessed Martyr Dafrosa and father of the blessed Virgins and Martyrs Bibiana and Demetria; who, under Julian the Apostate, condemned for the faith of Christ by a written sentence and sent into exile at Aquae Taurinenses, in Etruria, there gave up his spirit to God in prayer.
In Egypt, the holy Chaerémon, Bishop of Nicopolis, and very many other Martyrs. Of these, some, scattered in flight during the fury of the Decian persecution, wandered in solitudes and were killed by wild beasts; others were consumed by hunger, cold, and disease; others were slain by barbarians and robbers; and so all, by diverse kinds of death, were crowned with the same glory of martyrdom.
Near the mouth of the Tiber, the holy Martyrs Demetrius, Honoratus, and Florus.
At Alexandria, Saint Ischyrion, Martyr, who, when he was compelled by insults and violence to offer sacrifice and refused, was for that reason run through the middle of his entrails with a sharpened stake and given over to death.
At Nicomedia, Saint Zeno the soldier, who, having mocked Diocletian while he was sacrificing to Ceres, had his jaw-bones broken and teeth knocked out, and was beheaded for this.
At Chicago, Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, Virgin, Foundress of the Institute of Missionary Sisters of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, outstanding for extraordinary charity, unconquered strength of soul, and humility, whom Pope Pius XII enrolled in the catalogue of the Saints and appointed as heavenly Patron before God of all emigrants.

The twenty-second of February

At Rome, the birth into heaven of Saint Gabinius, Priest and Martyr, who was brother of the blessed Pope Caius, and, long afflicted by Diocletian with custody and chains, gained for himself the joys of heaven by a precious death.
In Africa, the holy Martyrs Publius, Julian, Marcellus, and others.
In Palestine, a commemoration of the holy Monks and other Martyrs who were most savagely slaughtered for the faith of Christ by the Saracens, under the duke Alamundarus.
At Naples, in Campania, Saint Quodvultdeus, Bishop of Carthage, who, together with his Clergy, was put by the Arian King Genseric on broken ships without oars or sails, and, beyond all hope, arrived at Naples, where, living in exile, he died as a Confessor.
At Jerusalem, Saint Zambdas, Bishop.
At Soli, in Cyprus, Saint Auxibius, Bishop.
Near Benevento, Saint Barbatus, Bishop, who, celebrated for holiness, converted the Lombards and their Duke to Christ.
At Milan, Saint Mansuetus, Bishop and Confessor.

The twenty-second of April

At Canterbury, in England, Saint Anselm, Bishop, Confessor, and Doctor of the Church, conspicuous for holiness and learning.
In Persia, the birth into heaven of Saint Simeon, Bishop of Seleucia and Ctesiphon, who, at the command of the Persian King Sapor, was arrested, laden with chains, and brought before unjust tribunals; and when he refused to worship the sun and bore witness to Jesus Christ with a free and most steadfast voice, he was first worn down for a long time in a prison cell together with a hundred others—of whom some were Bishops, some Priests, some Clerics of various orders. Then, when Usthazanes, the king's foster-father, who had previously fallen from the faith but had been recalled to repentance by him, had steadfastly undergone martyrdom, on the following day—which was the annual day of the Lord's Passion—all were beheaded before Simeon's eyes, each of whom he vigorously exhorted; and last of all he himself was beheaded. The most distinguished men Abdechalas and Ananias, who were his Priests, also suffered with him. Pusicus, too, the Superintendent of the King's craftsmen, because he had strengthened the wavering Ananias, was put to a cruel death by having his neck pierced through the tendon and his tongue pulled out through it; and after him his daughter also, a sacred Virgin, was afflicted with many dreadful torments and at last beheaded with a sword.
At Alexandria, the holy Martyrs Arator the Priest, Fortunatus, Felix, Silvius, and Vitalis, who rested in prison.
At Nicomedia, the holy Martyrs Apollo, Isaac, and Codrates; of whom the last, under the Emperor Diocletian, was beheaded, and, a few days after him, the first two perished of hunger in their chains, and they merited the crown of martyrdom.
At Antioch, Saint Anastasius, Bishop of Sinai.
At Old Oettingen, in Bavaria, Saint Conrad of Parzham, Confessor, of the Order of Friars Minor Capuchin, outstanding for charity and prayer, whom, renowned for miracles, Pope Pius XI enrolled in the number of the Saints.

The twenty-second of October

At Jerusalem, Saint Mary Salome, mother of the holy Apostles James and John, who is mentioned in the Gospel as being solicitous about the Lord's burial.
Likewise at Jerusalem, blessed Mark, Bishop, a most distinguished and learned man, who was the first drawn from the Gentiles to govern the Church of Jerusalem, and not much later, under the Emperor Antoninus, merited the palm of martyrdom.
At Hadrianople, in Thrace, the birth into heaven of the holy Martyrs Philip, Bishop; Severus, Priest; Eusebius and Hermes; who, under Julian the Apostate, after imprisonment and floggings, were burned in fire.
Likewise, the holy Martyrs Alexander, Bishop; Heraclius the soldier; and their companions.
Near Fermo, in Picenum, the birth into heaven of Saint Philip, Bishop and Martyr.
Near Cologne, Saint Cordula, who, being one of the companions of Saint Ursula and having hidden herself, terrified by the sufferings and slaughter of the others, repented the following day and gave herself up willingly to the Huns, and, the last of all, received the crown of martyrdom.
At Huesca, in Spain, the holy Virgins Nunilo and Alodia, sisters, who, punished by capital sentence by the Saracens for confessing the faith, completed their martyrdom.
At Hierapolis, in Phrygia, Saint Abercius, Bishop, who flourished under the Emperor Marcus Antoninus.
At Rouen, Saint Melanius, Bishop, who was ordained by the holy Pope Stephen and sent there to preach the Gospel.
In Tuscany, Saint Donatus Scottus, Bishop of Fiesole.
At Verona, Saint Verecundus, Bishop and Confessor.

The twenty-second of September

In Ethiopia, the birth into heaven of Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist; who, preaching in that region, suffered martyrdom. His Gospel, written in the Hebrew tongue, was discovered at his own revelation, together with the body of the blessed Apostle Barnabas, in the time of the Emperor Zeno.
In the land of Saar, Saint Jonah the Prophet, who was buried at Geth.
In Ethiopia, Saint Iphigenia, Virgin, who, baptized by the blessed Apostle Matthew and consecrated to God, rested in a holy death.
At Rome, Saint Pamphilus, Martyr.
On the same day, on the Via Claudia, at the twentieth milestone from the City, the passion of Saint Alexander, Bishop, who, under the Emperor Antoninus, for the faith of Christ, endured chains, blows, the rack, burning lamps, the tearing of flesh-hooks, wild beasts, and the flames of a furnace, and at last, struck down by the sword, attained a glorious life. His body was afterward transferred to the City by the blessed Pope Damasus on the twenty-sixth of November.
In Cyprus, Saint Isaac, Bishop and Martyr.
In Phoenicia, Saint Eusebius, Martyr, who, having gone of his own accord to the prefect and declared himself a Christian, was afflicted by him with many torments and beheaded.
In Cyprus, Saint Meletius, Bishop and Confessor.

The twenty-second of August

The feast of the Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
At Rome, on the Via Ostiensis, the birth into heaven of Saint Timothy, Martyr, who was seized by the Prefect of the City Tarquinius, worn down by a long imprisonment, and, when he had refused to sacrifice to idols, beaten three times and subjected to the most grievous torments, and at last beheaded.
At the Port of Rome, Saint Hippolytus, Bishop, most renowned for learning, who, under the Emperor Alexander, for his outstanding confession of the faith, was thrown with hands and feet bound into a deep pit full of water, and received the palm of martyrdom; whose body was buried by Christians near that same place.
At Autun, Saint Symphorian, Martyr, who, in the time of the Emperor Aurelian, when he refused to sacrifice to idols, was first afflicted with floggings, then cast into prison; and at last, with his head cut off, completed his martyrdom.
At Todi, in Umbria, the birth into heaven of Saint Philip Benizi, Confessor, of Florence, who was the propagator of the Order of the Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary and a man of exceptional humility; and he was enrolled in the number of the Saints by Pope Clement X. His feast, however, is celebrated on the following day.
At Rome, Saint Antoninus, Martyr, who, when he confessed himself a Christian with a free voice, was condemned to capital punishment by the Judge Vitellius and buried by the Priest Rufinus on the Via Aurelia.
At Tarsus, in Cilicia, a commemoration of the holy Athanasius, Bishop and Martyr; Anthousa, a noble woman whom he had baptized; and likewise the Martyrs Charisius and Neophytus, servants of that same Anthousa, who suffered under the Emperor Valerian.
At the Port of Rome, the holy Martyrs Martialis, Saturninus, Epictetus, Maprilis, and Felix, with their companions.
At Nicomedia, the passion of the holy Martyrs Agathonicus, Zoticus, and their companions, under the Emperor Maximian and the prefect Eutolmius.
At Rheims, in Gaul, the holy Martyrs Maurus and his companions.
In Spain, the holy Martyrs Fabrician and Philibert.
At Pavia, Saint Gunifortus, Martyr.

In this prayer, the letter N. expresses the name of the Titular of one's own church, provided the Titular is not a divine Person or a Mystery of the Lord, or that an Office or Commemoration has not already been made of him by reason of the Feast, or that his name is not already expressed in the same Suffrages Prayer; and the names of the holy Angels and of Saint John the Baptist, if they are Titulars, are placed before the name of Saint Joseph. In all these cases, however, the words «and blessed N.» are omitted.

Let us pray.
Defend us, we beseech you, O Lord, from all dangers of soul and body: and, through the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of God, together with blessed Joseph, your blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and blessed~
N. and all the Saints, graciously grant us salvation and peace; that, with all adversities and errors destroyed, your Church may serve you in secure freedom.

In this prayer, the letter N. expresses the name of the Titular of one's own church, provided the Titular is not a divine Person or a Mystery of the Lord, or that an Office or Commemoration has not already been made of him by reason of the Feast, or that his name is not already expressed in the same Suffrages Prayer; and the names of the holy Angels and of Saint John the Baptist, if they are Titulars, are placed before the name of Saint Joseph. In all these cases, however, the words «and blessed N.» are also omitted. If the Titular is to be named before all others, the particle «with» is omitted before the names of Saints Peter and Paul and placed before the name of Saint Joseph.

Visit, we pray, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it all the snares of the enemy: let your holy Angels dwell in it, to keep us in peace; and let your blessing be upon us always.

To the supper of the Lamb made ready,
And clothed in garments white and bright,
After the crossing of the Red Sea,
Let us sing to Christ the Prince.

Whose most holy body,
Consumed upon the altar of the Cross,
By drinking of his crimson Blood
We live for God.

Protected on the evening of the Passover
From the devastating Angel,
Delivered from the most harsh
Dominion of Pharaoh.

Now Christ our Pasch is sacrificed,
Who is the Lamb immolated:
The unleavened bread of sincerity,
His flesh is offered.

O truly worthy Victim,
Through whom the depths of hell were broken,
The captive people were redeemed,
And the rewards of life restored.

Christ rises from the tomb,
Victor returning from the abyss,
Thrusting the tyrant into chains,
And opening Paradise.

We pray, O Author of all things,
In this paschal joy,
From every assault of death
Defend your people.

Glory to you, O Lord,
Who rose from the dead,
With the Father and the Holy Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

To the royal feast of the Lamb,
Clothed in bright white robes,
After the crossing of the Red Sea,
Let us sing to Christ our King:

Whose divine charity
Offers the sacred Blood to drink,
And love, as priest, immolates
The members of his nurturing Body.

The destroying Angel shudders
At the blood sprinkled on the doorposts;
The divided sea flees;
The enemies are plunged beneath the waves.

Now Christ is our Passover,
The same, our Paschal Victim,
And the pure unleavened bread of sincerity
For pure and clean minds.

O true Victim of heaven,
To whom the nether regions are made subject,
The bonds of death are loosed,
The rewards of life are received.

Victor, with the lower regions subdued,
Christ unfolds his trophies;
And with heaven laid open, he leads
The subjected king of darkness in his train.

That you may be, O Jesus, an everlasting
Paschal joy for our minds,
Free those reborn to life
From the dread death of sins.

To God the Father be glory,
And to the Son, who rose from the dead,
And to the Paraclete,
For ever and ever.
Amen.

The herald of the day, the bird,
Heralds the approaching light;
Christ, the awakener of minds,
Now calls us to life.

"Put away your beds," he cries,
"You who are sluggish with unhealthy sleep;
Be chaste, upright, and sober,
Keep watch—I am already near."

Let us call upon Jesus with our voices,
Weeping, praying, sober;
Earnest supplication
Forbids a pure heart to sleep.

You, O Christ, dispel slumber;
You break the bonds of night;
You loosen ancient sin,
And pour in new light.

To God the Father be glory,
And to his only Son,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Both now and for ever.

Whose glory resounds throughout all the world,
Grant us this.
Amen.

Behold, now the shadow of night grows thin,
The glowing light of dawn flashes bright:
Let us, your suppliants, implore the Lord of all things
With harmonious voice:

That God, having mercy on us,
May drive away all weakness, grant salvation,
And bestow upon us the gifts
Of everlasting peace.

May the blessed Deity of the Father,
The Son, and likewise the Holy Spirit,
Whose glory re-echoes throughout all the world,
Grant us this.
Amen.

Behold, a clear voice challenges
All that is obscure, ringing out:
Far away let dreams be driven;
Jesus shines forth from on high.

Now let the torpid mind arise,
No longer lying prostrate on the ground;
A new star already blazes forth
To remove all that is harmful.

Behold, the Lamb is sent to us
Freely to loose the debt;
Let all of us together with tears
Pray for pardon.

That when he shines forth a second time
And girds the world with fear,
He may not punish us for our guilt,
But then may mercifully protect us.

Power, honor, praise, and glory
To God the Father with the Son,
And likewise to the Holy Paraclete,
Through ages upon ages.
Amen.

Taught by mystic custom,
Let us observe this fast,
Measured by the well-known circuit
Of four times ten days.

The law and the prophets first
Prefigured this; afterward
Christ consecrated it, the King
And maker of all times.

Let us therefore use more sparingly
Words, food, and drink,
Sleep and amusements, and keep
A stricter watch.

Let us avoid the harmful things
That undermine wandering minds:
And let us give no place
To the tyranny of the cunning foe.

Let us bend the avenging wrath,
Let us weep before the Judge,
Let us cry with suppliant voice,
Let us all say on bended knee:

By our offenses we have angered
Your clemency, O God:
Pour out upon us from above,
O Forgiver, your indulgence.

Remember that we are your creation,
Though perishable:
We pray you, give not the glory of your name,
We beseech you, to another.

Loosen the evil that we have done,
Increase the good that we seek:
That we may at last be able
To please you here and for ever.

Grant this, O blessed Trinity;
Bestow it, O simple Unity;
That the offerings of our fasting
May be fruitful for your own.
Amen.

O maker of man from on high,
Who alone ordering all things
Bid the earth bring forth
The race of creeping things and beasts:

And the great bodies of creation,
Made living by your commanding word,
Appointing them to serve in order,
You subjected to your little servants:

Repel whatever from the force of desire
Assails us,
Or insinuates itself in our behavior,
Or intrudes itself in our actions.

Grant us the rewards of joys,
Grant us the gifts of grace:
Loose the bonds of strife:
Bind fast the covenants of peace.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

Now, O Christ, Sun of justice,
Let the darkness of minds grow bright:
That the light of the virtues may return
As you restore day to the earth.

Granting an acceptable time,
Grant also a repentant heart,
That your kindness may convert
Those whom a long-suffering devotion endures.

Grant us to bear some measure
Of penance, even for grave sins,
By your greater gift,
Through which sins are taken away.

The day comes, your day,
In which all things reflourish:
Let us rejoice in this, brought back
To your path by your grace.

May the universe of creation,
O merciful Trinity, adore you,
And may we, made new through pardon,
Sing a new song.
Amen.

Now that the morning star has risen,
Let us humbly pray to God,
That in our daily actions
He may keep us from all harm.

May he hold back and bridle the tongue,
Lest the din of strife ring out:
May he guard the eyes with care,
Lest they drink in vanities.

Let the depths of the heart be pure,
And let folly be far away;
May sparing use of food and drink
Curb the pride of the flesh.

That when the day shall pass away
And fortune bring back the night,
Pure through our abstinence from the world,
We may ourselves sing his glory.

To God the Father be glory,
And to his only Son,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Both now and for ever.
Amen.

Now the fiery sun withdraws:
You, eternal light, O Unity,
Pour light into our hearts,
O blessed Trinity.

In the morning with a hymn of praise,
In the evening we implore you;
Be pleased that we your suppliants
May praise you among the heavenly hosts.

To the Father, and likewise to the Son,
And to you, O Holy Spirit,
As it was, so let it be always,
Glory through every age.
Amen.

Jesus, our redemption,
Our love and our longing,
God, Creator of all things,
Made man at the end of time:

What mercy overcame you
To bear our sins,
Suffering a cruel death,
That you might lift us from death!

Penetrating the gates of hell,
Redeeming your own captives,
Victor in a glorious triumph,
You sit at the right hand of the Father.

May your own loving kindness compel you
To overcome our evils
By pardoning, and satisfy us who have obtained our desire
With the sight of your face.

Be our joy,
You who are to be our reward;
May our glory be in you
Through all ages for ever.
Glory to you, O Lord,
Who ascend above the stars,
With the Father and the Holy Spirit,
For ever and ever.
Amen.

Vast Creator of the heavens,
Who, dividing the flowing waters
Lest they intermingle in confusion,
Set the sky as their limit:

Making a place for the heavenly bodies,
And likewise for the streams of earth;
That the water might temper the flames,
And not dissolve the surface of the earth:

Pour in now, O most loving One,
The gift of lasting grace:
Lest ancient error wear us down
By the occasions of new deceit.

May faith find the light;
So may it bring forth the ray of brightness:
That it may overcome all vanities:
Let no falsehood suppress it.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

O most excellent Creator of light,
Bringing forth the light of days,
At the beginning of new light,
Preparing the origin of the world:

You who command morning joined to evening
To be called day:
The gloomy chaos flows in;
Hear our prayers with tears.

Lest the mind, burdened with sin,
Be exiled from the gift of life,
While it thinks of nothing lasting
And entangles itself in faults.

Let it knock at the innermost heaven,
Let it carry off the prize of life:
Let us avoid all that is harmful:
Let us purge all that is worst.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

He who has now completed six lustres,
Fulfilling the time of his body,
The Redeemer, by his own free will
Given over to his Passion,
Is lifted up as the Lamb
To be immolated on the timber of the Cross.

Behold, given gall to drink, he languishes;
Spines, nails, and lance
Have pierced his gentle body;
Water and blood flow forth:
Earth, sea, stars, the world—
By what a river they are washed!

O faithful Cross, above all other
One noble tree:
No forest brings forth such
In leaf, in flower, in bud:
Sweet the iron, sweet the timber,
Sweet the burden they sustain.

Bend your branches, high tree,
Relax your tight-strung fibers,
And let that rigidity be softened
Which your native hardness gave:
And stretch the limbs of the King on high
Upon your gentle timber.

You alone were worthy
To bear the Victim of the world;
And to prepare a harbor
For the shipwrecked world as an ark,
Wet through with the sacred blood
Poured from the body of the Lamb.

Eternal glory to the blessed Trinity:
Equal to the Father, and to the Son,
Equal honor to the Paraclete:
Let all creation praise
The name of the One and Triune.
Amen.

He who, with six lustres now accomplished,
Fulfilling the time of his body,
Born of his own will for this very purpose,
Given over to his Passion,
Is lifted up as the Lamb
To be immolated on the timber of the Cross.

Here vinegar, gall, a reed,
Spittle, nails, and lance:
His gentle body is pierced through;
Blood and water flow forth:
Earth, sea, stars, the world—
By what a river they are washed!

O faithful Cross, above all other
One noble tree:
No forest brings forth such
In leaf, in flower, in bud:
Sweet wood, sweet nails,
A sweet burden it sustains.

Bend your branches, high tree,
Relax your tight-strung fibers,
And let that rigidity be softened
Which your native hardness gave:
That you may stretch the limbs of the King on high
Upon your gentle timber.

You alone were worthy
To bear the ransom of the age,
And to prepare a harbor
For the shipwrecked world as navigator,
Wet through with the sacred blood
Poured from the body of the Lamb.

Glory and honor to God
Most high in every place:
Equal to the Father and to the Son,
To the renowned Paraclete:
To whom be praise and power
Through eternal ages.
Amen.

Behold, golden light now rises;
Let pale blindness depart,
Which has long dragged us headlong
With wandering error.

May this light bestow serenity
And render us pure before it:
Let us speak nothing crafty:
Let us turn over nothing obscure.

So may the whole day pass,
Lest the lying tongue, or the hands,
Or the wanton eyes sin,
Lest harmful guilt defile the body.

A watchman stands above,
Who on all our days,
Surveys our actions
From the first light to the evening.

To God the Father be glory,
And to his only Son,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Now and through every age.
Amen.

O God of great power,
Who take the race that sprang from water
And partly restore it to the deep,
And partly raise it into the air:

Sinking some beneath the waters,
Watering others raised to the heavens:
That from one stock they spring
And fill different places:

Grant to all your little servants,
Washed by the wave of your Blood,
To know no falls into sin
And to bear no weariness of death.

That no fault may cast anyone down:
Let no boasting exalt anyone:
Let the crushed mind not collapse:
Let the exalted mind not fall.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

Rising by night, let us all keep watch,
Let us meditate always in the psalms,
And with harmonious voice let us sweetly
Sing hymns to the Lord.

That singing together to the pious King,
We may merit with his Saints
To enter the hall of heaven
And lead a life that endures for ever.

May the blessed Deity of the Father,
The Son, and likewise the Holy Spirit,
Whose glory resounds throughout all the world,
Grant us this.
Amen.

The dark night covers all
The colors of the earth:
We who make confession pray to you,
O just Judge of hearts.

That you may take away our offenses
And wash away the stains of our minds:
And, O Christ, grant grace
That sins may be kept far off.

Behold, the wicked mind grows torpid,

It longs to remove the dark things

Drive away the darkness

Grant this, most loving Father,

Reigning through every age.

Night, and darkness, and clouds,
Disordered and turbulent in the world:
The light enters, the sky grows white:
Christ comes: depart.

The gloom of the earth is cleft
Struck by the shaft of the sun,
And color now returns to things
At the face of the shining star.

You alone, O Christ, we know:
To you with pure and simple mind,
Weeping and singing we pray:
Be attentive to our senses.

There are many things daubed with deceits
That your light may cleanse:
You, the light of the morning star,
Illuminate us with your serene countenance.

To God the Father be glory,
And to his only Son,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Both now and for ever.
Amen.

Sing, my tongue, the laurels
Of the glorious contest,
And above the trophy of the Cross
Proclaim a noble triumph:
How the Redeemer of the world
Vanquished as an immolated Victim.

The Creator, grieving for the deceit
Of the first-formed father,
When in the deadly bite of the harmful fruit
He fell to destruction,
Then himself marked out the tree,
To undo the harm of the tree.

The order of our salvation
Had demanded this work,
That the craft of the manifold deceiver
Might be deceived by craft,
And that a remedy might come
From where the foe had done the harm.

When therefore the fullness
Of sacred time had come,
The Son was sent from the citadel of the Father,
Creator of the world,
And coming forth clothed in flesh
From a virginal womb.

His limbs wrapped in swaddling clothes:

Strengthening with lasting power.

He may reward with blessed gifts.

Now, O paternal brightness,
We earnestly beseech you:
Let foul desire be absent
And every harmful deed.

Let not the bond of our body
Be foul or wanton,
By reason of whose fires
Hell itself may burn us more fiercely.

Therefore, O Redeemer, we pray
That you wash away our reproaches,
And graciously bestow upon us
The good things of everlasting life.

That, exiled from fleshly acts,
We ourselves made chaste,
As we wait in prostration,
May sing the song of glory.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

On the first day, when the blessed
Trinity established the world,
Or when the risen Creator
Frees us, with death overcome:

With drowsiness driven far away,
Let us all arise more quickly,
And in the night let us seek God
As the prophet bids us:

That he may hear our prayers
And stretch out his right hand,
And, expiated from defilements,
May restore us to the dwelling places of heaven:

That all who at the most sacred
Time of this day,
Sing the quiet hours,
He may reward with blessed gifts.

Now, O paternal brightness,
We earnestly beseech you:
Let the flames of desire be absent
And every harmful deed.

Let not the bond of our body
Be foul or wanton,
Because of whose fires
Hell may burn us more fiercely.

O Redeemer of the world, we pray
That you wash away our reproaches;
And abundantly bestow upon us
The good things of everlasting life.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

Mighty and true God, our Ruler,
Who govern the changes of things,
With splendor you illumine the morning
And the noon with fires:

Quench the flames of strife,
Drive off harmful heat,
Bring health to our bodies
And true peace to our hearts.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Reigning through every age.
Amen.

Grant a bright evening,

But may the eternal glory
Press upon us as the reward of holy death.

Grant this, most loving Father,

Amen.

Press upon us as the reward of holy death.

Grant this, most loving Father,

Amen.

O eternal King of the heavenly ones,
Creator of all things,
The Son, equal before all ages,
Ever with the Father:

You who, as the world came into being,
Imparting to Adam the image of your countenance,
Joined a noble spirit
To his body of clay:

When envy and the deceit of the demon
Had defiled the human race:
You, clothed in flesh, as the craftsman
Reform the lost image.

You who, once born of a Virgin,
Are now born from the tomb,
And bid us who are buried with you
Rise from the dead.

You who, as the eternal shepherd, wash the flock
With the water of Baptism:
This is the washing of minds:
This is the burial place of sins.

You who, long due as our Redeemer,
Were fixed to the Cross,
And lavishly gave your blood
As the price of our salvation.

That you may be, O Jesus, an everlasting
Paschal joy for our minds,
Free those reborn to life
From the dread death of sins.

To God the Father be glory,
And to the Son, who rose from the dead,
And to the Paraclete,
For ever and ever.
Amen.

O eternal Lord and King,
Creator of all things,
Who were before all ages
Ever the Son with the Father:

Who in the beginning of the world
Shaped Adam as a human being:
And gave him a countenance
Like to your own image.

Whom the devil had deceived,
The enemy of the human race,
Whose form of body
You were pleased to take upon yourself:

To redeem the human being
Whom you had earlier formed:
And to join us to God
Through the fellowship of the flesh.

Him who, born of a Virgin,
Every soul trembles to behold:
Through whom we also believe with devout mind
That we shall rise.

Who in Baptism
Granted us forgiveness
To us who were held in bonds,
Bound by conscience.

Who were pleased to take up
The Cross on behalf of man:
You gave your blood
As the price of our salvation.

We pray, O Author of all things,
In this Paschal joy,
Defend your people
From every assault of death.

Glory to you, O Lord,
Who rose from the dead,
With the Father and the Holy Spirit,
For ever and ever.
Amen.

With sweet words the Angel
Foretold to the women:
The Lord is to be seen in Galilee
With all speed.

While they hasten to tell this
To the Apostles,
Seeing him alive,
They kiss the feet of the Lord.

When this was known, the disciples
Hastily departed to Galilee
To see the longed-for face
Of the Lord.

In the bright joy of Easter
The sun shines upon the world with its ray,
Now that the Apostles
Behold Christ with bodily sight.

The wounds shown to them
Glowing in the flesh of Christ,
They publicly declare in voice
That the Lord has risen.

O Christ, most merciful King,
Take possession of our hearts:
That we may render you the praises due
At all times.

We pray, O Author of all things,
In this Paschal joy,
Defend your people
From every assault of death.

Glory to you, O Lord,
Who rose from the dead,
With the Father and the Holy Spirit
For ever and ever.
Amen.

With our limbs refreshed by sleep,
Casting aside our beds, we rise:
We beseech you, Father, to be present

Let the tongue first begin with you,
Let the ardor of the mind embrace you:
That you, O Holy One, may be the beginning
Of the actions that follow.

Let darkness give way to light,
And night to the star of day,
That the fault which night has brought
May melt away by the gift of light.

We pray likewise as suppliants
That you may cut away all wrongs,
And be praised by the voice of those who sing
At all times.

Grant this, most loving Father,

Amen.

Radiance of the Father's glory,
Bringing forth light from light,
Light of light, and fountain of brightness,
Day illumining the day:

And you, true sun, glide in,
Gleaming with perpetual brightness:
And pour the radiance of the Holy Spirit
Into our senses.

Let us also call upon the Father in our prayers,
The Father of everlasting glory,
The Father of powerful grace,
That he may banish the slippery fault.

May he strengthen vigorous deeds:
May he blunt the teeth of the envious:
May he prosper in harsh adversities:
May he grant the grace to act rightly.

May he govern and rule the mind,
With a chaste and faithful body:
May faith burn with fervor,
May it know nothing of the poison of deceit.

May Christ be our food,
And may faith be our drink:
Let us joyfully drink the sober
Intoxication of the spirit.

May this day pass joyfully,
May modesty be like the dawn,
Faith like the noon,
Let the mind know no twilight.

The dawn advances the course,
May all of dawn go forth:
The Son entirely in the Father,
And the Father entirely in the Word.

To God the Father be glory,
And to his only Son,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Both now and for ever.
Amen.

One in power

Mercifulley receive with kindness

That with a heart pure from defilements
We may enjoy you more abundantly.

Scorch the loins and the ailing liver

O eternal Creator of all things,
Who govern night and day,
And grant the seasons their times,
To relieve our weariness:

Now the herald of the day sounds out,
Keeping watch in the deep of night,
Night's light for those who travel,
Dividing night from night.

Roused by this, the morning star
Frees the sky from darkness;
The whole band of night-wanderers
Abandon the way of harm.

At this the sailor gathers strength,
And the straits of the sea grow calm:
At this, the very rock of the Church,
As it crows, washes away his fault.

Let us rise therefore with vigor;
The cock rouses those who lie down
And rebukes the drowsy,
The cock rebukes those who deny.

At the cock's crow hope returns,
Health is poured back to the sick,
The robber's sword is sheathed,
Faith returns to the fallen.

Look upon us as we stumble, O Jesus,
And by your gaze correct us:
If you look upon us, faults fall away,
And by weeping sin is dissolved.

You, the light, shine upon our senses,
Drive away the sleep of the mind:
Let our voice first sound of you,
And let us pay our vows to you.

To God the Father be glory,
And to his only Son,
With the Spirit the Paraclete,
Both now and for ever.

Let dreams and the phantoms of the night

Grant this, almighty Father,

Amen.

O kindly Creator of the earth,
Who, separating the surface of the world,
With the troubles of the water driven away,
Made the earth firm and stable:

That, bringing forth fitting seed,
Beautiful with tawny flowers,
It might stand fruitful in fruit
And render welcome pasture:

Wash the wounds of the scorched mind
With the green freshness of grace:
That it may wash away what it has done with tears
And wear down evil impulses.

May it comply with your commands:
May it draw near to no evils:
May it rejoice to be filled with good things,
And know nothing of the stroke of death.

Grant this, most loving Father,
And you, the Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,

You, Unity of the Trinity,
who mightily govern the world,
attend to the song of praise
that we who keep watch sing.

For we rise from our bed
in the quiet hour of night,
that we may implore from you
the healing of all our wounds.

Whatever we have done amiss in the nights,
through the deceit of demons,
may the power of your glory
wipe it away from on high.

Let no sordid flesh be present,
nor let torpor press upon our hearts,
lest the contagion of sin
cool the ardor of the spirit.

For this reason, Redeemer, we pray,
fill us with your light,
through which, in the circuits of days,
we may not fall by any deeds.

Grant this, most loving Father,
and you, Only-Begotten, the Father's equal,
with the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete,
reigning through all ages.
Amen.

who, born, come to the aid of the world
as the course of time declines:

Illuminate our hearts now,
and set them aflame with your love;
that, hearing the proclamation,
the allurements may at last be driven away.

And when you shall come afterward as Judge
to search the deeds of the heart,
rendering recompense for hidden things,
and the kingdom for righteous good deeds:

May we not then be confined to punishments
according to the measure of our crimes,
but with the blessed as sharers
may we be everlasting dwellers in heaven.

Praise, honor, power, glory,
to God the Father and to the Son,
and likewise to the Holy Paraclete,
unto ages of ages.
Amen.

The Word on high, coming forth
from the bosom of the eternal Father,
who, born, come to the aid of the world
as the course of time slips away:

Illuminate our hearts now,
and set them aflame with your love;
that the heart, forsaking transient things,
the joy of heaven may fill.

So that, when the tribunal of the Judge
shall condemn the guilty to fire,
and a friendly voice shall call
the righteous to heaven as their due;

May we not be rolled in the black whirlwinds
of devouring flames,
but, possessing the face of God,
may we enjoy the joys of heaven.

and to you, Holy Spirit,

the mystery of the Cross shines bright,

Grant, we pray, almighty God, that just as we go before the glorious feast of your Apostles Simon and Jude, so may they themselves intercede before your majesty on our behalf, to merit your benefits for us.
O Lord, our God, multiply your grace upon us: and grant us to follow in holy profession the joy of those whose glorious solemnities we anticipate.

O Lord our God, who revealed heavenly secrets to blessed Bridget through your Only Begotten Son: grant to us your servants, by her devout intercession, to rejoice with gladness in the revelation of your eternal glory.

O Lord Jesus Christ, our Mediator before the Father, who deigned to establish the most blessed Virgin, your Mother, as our mother also and as mediatrix before you: graciously grant that whoever approaches you to seek benefits may rejoice to have obtained all things through her:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who endowed Saint Paul with a singular charity for preaching the mystery of the Cross, and through him were pleased that a new family should flourish in the Church: grant us through his intercession that, continually meditating on your Passion on earth, we may merit to obtain its fruit in heaven:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who enriched your Church for the renewed commemoration of the sorrows of your most holy Mother with a new family of her Servants through the seven blessed Fathers: graciously grant that we may be so united in their weeping as to share also in their joys.
O Lord Jesus Christ, who made blessed Veronica the Virgin wonderful through the signs of your Passion: graciously grant that, crucifying the flesh, we may merit to attain eternal joys:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who, as the world grows cold, renewed the sacred Stigmata of your Passion in the flesh of most blessed Francis, to enkindle the fire of your love in our hearts: graciously grant that by his merits and prayers we may continually bear the Cross and bring forth fruits worthy of penance:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who taught us in the garden to pray in word and example, to overcome the dangers of temptations: graciously grant that we, always intent on prayer, may merit to obtain its abundant fruit:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who wonderfully revealed to blessed Margaret Mary the Virgin the unfathomable riches of your Heart: grant us by her merits and imitation, that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may merit to have a lasting dwelling in that same Heart of yours:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who led the holy Virgin Frances Xavier Cabrini, enkindled with the fire of your Most Sacred Heart, through the vast regions of the world to win souls for you, and through her raised up a new family of Virgins in your Church: we pray that, through her intercession, we may be clothed in the virtues of that same Heart of yours, and may merit to arrive at the eternal harbor of blessedness.

O Lord Jesus Christ, pattern and reward of true humility: we pray that, as you made blessed Francis a glorious imitator of you in contempt of earthly honor, so you may grant us to be sharers in the same imitation and glory:

O Lord Jesus Christ, who granted blessed Pope Urban to contend successfully for the liberty and honor of your Church, and strengthened him through the power of the Cross to ransom from the power of unbelievers the memorials of your mortal life and Passion: grant that, through his intercession, we who struggle against the enemies of our soul on earth may merit to receive the prize of eternal glory:

O Lord Jesus, who caused your blessed virgin Irmengard to despise the delights of the world and to bless your name: grant, we pray, that through her intercession we may please you all the days of our life.
O Lord Jesus, who gave to blessed Bernardine your Confessor an exceeding love of your holy Name: graciously pour into us, we pray, by his merits and intercession, the spirit of your love:

O Lord, who have said: Unless you become as little children, you shall not enter the Kingdom of Heaven: grant us, we pray, so to follow in the steps of the holy Virgin Thérèse in humility and simplicity of heart, that we may attain eternal rewards.

Let us pray.
O God, Creator and Redeemer of all the faithful, grant to the souls of your servants and handmaids the remission of all their sins: that through devout supplications they may obtain the pardon they have always desired:

Grant, we pray, O Lord, to your Church, through the intercession of your holy Martyrs Vitus, Modestus, and Crescentia, not to think proud thoughts, but to advance in the humility that is pleasing to you: so that, despising what is perverse, she may freely exercise charity in whatever is right.
Grant us, we pray, O Lord, to glory in the solemnities of your blessed Apostle Thomas: that we may always be upheld by his patronage and may follow the faith with fitting devotion.

Grant us, we pray, O Lord, to imitate what we venerate: that we may learn to love even our enemies, for we celebrate the Finding of him who knew how to pray even for his persecutors to our Lord Jesus Christ your Son:

Grant us, we pray, O Lord, to imitate what we venerate: that we may learn to love even our enemies, for we celebrate the birth of him who knew how to pray even for his persecutors to our Lord Jesus Christ your Son:

Grant us, we pray, merciful God, through the intercession of blessed Isidore the Farmer your Confessor, not to think proud thoughts: but to serve you always with a humility pleasing to you, following his merits and examples.

Grant us, we pray, merciful God: through the intercession of blessed Isidore the Farmer, your Confessor, not to think proud thoughts; but to serve you always with a humility pleasing to you, following his merits and examples.

Grant us, we pray, almighty God, through the intercession of blessed Cyril the Bishop: so to know you as the one true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent; that we may merit to be numbered continually among the sheep who hear his voice.
Grant us, almighty God, to extinguish the flames of our vices; you who granted to blessed Lawrence to overcome the flames of his torments.

Grant us, Father of eternal consolation, through the prayers of blessed Nonnosus the Abbot, peace and health of mind and body: that we may cleave to your precepts with the whole heart of love; and may accomplish with all our strength the things that are pleasing to you.

Grant, we pray, almighty God, through the intercession of blessed Eugene your Confessor and Bishop: that we may serve you with our whole heart; for no hostility will prevail against us if we truly trust in you.

Hear, we pray, O Lord, our prayers which we offer on the solemnity of your blessed Confessor and Bishop N.: and may he, who merited to serve you worthily, by his interceding merits absolve us from all our sins.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of your blessed Martyrs Hippolytus and Cassian may both increase our devotion and bring us salvation.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who keep the feast of your blessed Virgin Catherine may both rejoice in the annual solemnity and advance by the example of so great a virtue.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who keep the feast of your blessed Virgin and Martyr Prisca may both rejoice in the annual solemnity and advance by the example of so great a faith.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who keep the feast of your blessed Virgin and Martyr Thecla may both rejoice in the annual solemnity and advance by the example of so great a faith.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of your blessed Martyr Boniface may be assisted by his intercessions before you.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of your blessed Martyr and Bishop Urban may be assisted by his intercessions before you.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of your blessed Martyrs Gordian and Epimachus may be assisted by their intercessions before you.

Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we, advancing in the knowledge of the Saints after the example of Saint John the Confessor, and showing mercy to others, may obtain pardon before you through his merits.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of your blessed Martyrs Pontian and Hippolytus may both increase our devotion and bring us salvation.

Grant, we pray, almighty and eternal God, that we who venerate with a festive celebration the most pure and perfect Virginity of the Virgin Mary may obtain, through her intercession, purity of mind and body.

O God, author of peace and lover of charity, who adorned blessed John your Confessor with the wonderful grace of reconciling those in disagreement: grant by his merits and intercession that, confirmed in your charity, we may be separated from you by no temptations.

O God, whose right hand raised up blessed Peter as he walked upon the waves lest he sink, and delivered his fellow Apostle Paul, shipwrecked for the third time, from the depths of the sea: hear us with favor and grant that, by the merits of both, we may attain the glory of eternity:

O God, whose praise the Holy Innocents confessed on this day not by speaking but by dying: put to death in us all the evil of our vices; that our life may also confess by its conduct the faith which our tongue proclaims.
O God, whose Only Begotten Son appeared in the substance of our flesh: grant, we pray, that through him whom we have known as like us outwardly, we may merit to be reformed inwardly:

O God, whose Only Begotten Son by his life, death, and Resurrection has won for us the rewards of eternal salvation: grant, we pray, that, meditating upon these mysteries by the most holy Rosary of the blessed Virgin Mary, we may both imitate what they contain and attain what they promise.

O God, rewarder of faithful souls, who consecrated this day by the martyrdom of your blessed Priest Apollinaris: grant, we pray, to us your servants that, as we celebrate the venerable feast of him, we may obtain pardon through his prayers.

O God, the exaltation of the humble, who raised up blessed Francis your Confessor to the glory of your Saints: grant, we pray, that by his merits and imitation we may happily attain the rewards promised to the humble.

O God, in whose Passion the sword of sorrow pierced the most sweet soul of the glorious Virgin and Mother Mary, according to the prophecy of Simeon: graciously grant that we who reverently commemorate her sorrows may happily obtain the saving effect of your Passion:

O God, the strength of those who hope in you, who strengthened your blessed Confessor and Bishop Gregory with the virtue of constancy in defending the liberty of the Church: grant us, by his example and intercession, to overcome all adversity with fortitude.

O God, consoler of the sorrowful and salvation of those who hope in you, who mercifully accepted the devout tears of blessed Monica for the conversion of her son Augustine: grant us, through the intercession of both, to lament our sins and to find the indulgence of your grace.

O God, Father of mercies, through the merits and intercession of blessed Jerome, whom you willed to be a helper and father to orphans: grant that we may faithfully guard the spirit of adoption, by which we are called and are your children.

O God, giver of all good things, who in your servant Bibiana joined the palm of martyrdom to the flower of virginity: unite our souls to you in charity through her intercession, so that, dangers being removed, we may attain eternal rewards.
Almighty God, whose service is the highest and fullest happiness: * grant us, through the intercession of blessed Hugh the Abbot, § to serve you in holiness and justice without fear.
O God, for whose Church the glorious Bishop Thomas fell beneath the swords of the wicked: grant, we pray, that all who implore his aid may obtain the saving effect of their petition.
O God, for whose honor the glorious Bishop Stanislaus fell beneath the swords of the wicked: grant, we pray, that all who implore his aid may obtain the saving effect of their petition.

O God, who, to call to the knowledge of your name the Africans taken into slavery, strengthened blessed Peter with a wonderful charity and patience in helping them: grant us through his intercession that, seeking the things of Jesus Christ, we may love our neighbors in deed and in truth.

O God, who for the salvation of souls were pleased that your blessed Confessor and Bishop Francis should become all things to all men: graciously grant that, filled with the sweetness of your charity, and guided by his counsels and supported by his merits, we may attain eternal joys.

O God, who raised up Saint John Baptist de la Salle your Confessor, for the Christian education of the poor and to strengthen youth in the way of truth, and gathered through him a new family in the Church: graciously grant that, through his intercession and example, burning with zeal for your glory in the salvation of souls, we may be able to become sharers in his crown in heaven.

O God, who deigned to choose blessed Pius as Supreme Pontiff to crush the enemies of your Church and to restore divine worship: make us to be defended by his protection and so to adhere to your service that, all the snares of every enemy being overcome, we may rejoice in perpetual peace.

O God, who strengthened Saint Altmann your Confessor and Bishop with fortitude of soul to promote the liberty and honor of your Church: grant through his intercession that, overcoming all adversity on earth, we may merit to be crowned with him in heaven.

O God, who adorned your blessed Bishop and Doctor Robert with wondrous learning and virtue to repel the snares of error and to champion the rights of the Apostolic See: grant by his merits and intercession that we may grow in love of truth and that the hearts of those who err may return to the unity of your Church.

O God, who strengthened blessed Vincent with apostolic virtue to preach the Gospel to the poor and to promote the honor of the ecclesiastical order: grant, we pray, that we who venerate his devout merits may also be instructed by the examples of his virtues.

O God, who deigned to adorn blessed Canute the King with the palm of martyrdom and with glorious miracles to illustrate your Church: graciously grant that, as he himself was an imitator of the Lord's Passion, so we, walking in his footsteps, may merit to attain eternal joys.

O God, who strengthened the Church Militant with a new support through blessed Ignatius to spread the greater glory of your name: grant that, striving on earth with his help and in his imitation, we may merit to be crowned with him in heaven.

O God, who deigned to send blessed Patrick your Confessor and Bishop to preach your glory to the nations: grant by his merits and intercession that we may be able to fulfill what you command us to do, through your mercy.

O God, who bestowed upon blessed Lawrence your Confessor and Doctor the spirit of wisdom and fortitude for every arduous work for the glory of your name and the salvation of souls: grant us in the same spirit both to know what must be done; and, knowing it, to accomplish it through his intercession.

O God, who bestowed upon blessed Lawrence your Confessor the spirit of counsel and fortitude for every arduous work for the glory of your name and the salvation of souls: grant us in the same spirit both to know what must be done; and, knowing it, to accomplish it through his intercession.

O God, who for the salvation of souls, redeemed by your precious blood, gathered through blessed Gaspar a new family in your Church: graciously grant that, through his intercession, we may obtain the abundant fruit of your redemption:

O God, who strengthened blessed Peter your Confessor with virtue and learning to defend the Catholic faith: graciously grant that through his examples and counsels those who err may come to their senses unto salvation, and the faithful may persevere in the confession of truth.

O God, who filled Saint Pius the Supreme Pontiff with heavenly wisdom and apostolic fortitude to defend the Catholic faith and to restore all things in Christ: graciously grant that, following his ordinances and examples, we may attain eternal rewards.

O God, who strengthened your blessed Confessor and Bishop Urban with constancy to defend boldly the rights of the Apostolic See and to spread the Catholic faith widely: make us, assisted by his protection, so to serve the Church Militant that we may merit to be united with the Church Triumphant.

O God, who disposed your Only Begotten Son, when he was lifted up from the earth, to draw all things to himself: graciously bring it to pass that, raised by the merits and example of your seraphic Confessor Joseph above all earthly desires, we may merit to attain to him.

O God, who were pleased to illumine the peoples of England with the light of the true faith through the preaching and miracles of your blessed Confessor and Bishop Augustine: grant that, through his intercession, the hearts of those who err may return to the unity of your truth, and that we may be in accord with your will.

O God, who were pleased to bestow upon blessed Anne the grace that she might merit to become the mother of the Mother of your Only Begotten Son: graciously grant that we may be aided by her patronage before you, whose solemnities we celebrate.

O God, who through the mystery of the incarnate Word mercifully consecrated the House of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and wondrously placed it in the bosom of your Church: grant that, separated from the dwellings of sinners, we may be made worthy inhabitants of your holy House.

O God, who adorned your blessed servant Frances, among the other gifts of your grace, with the familiar companionship of an Angel: grant, we pray, that, aided by the help of her intercession, we may merit to attain the fellowship of the Angels.

O God, who taught blessed Hedwig to pass with her whole heart from the pomp of the world to the humble following of your Cross: grant that, by her merits and example, we may learn to tread underfoot the perishing pleasures of the world, and to overcome all adversities in the embrace of your Cross.

O God, who made blessed Hyacinth your Virgin a victim of continual mortification and charity: grant us, by her example and intercession, that we may be able to weep over our sins and always to love you.

O God, who were pleased wondrously to refresh blessed Juliana your Virgin, suffering from a grievous illness, with the precious Body of your Son: grant, we pray, that, through the intercession of her merits, we too may be refreshed and strengthened by the same in the agony of death, and be led to the heavenly homeland.

O God, who rescued blessed Mary from the darkness of vices and presented her to yourself as a bride: hear us with favor and grant that, by her prayers and merits, we may be cleansed from the stains of our sins.

O God, who on this day willed that blessed Mary ever-Virgin, the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, should be presented in the temple: grant, we pray, that, through her intercession, we may merit to be presented in the temple of your glory.
O God, who made blessed Margaret the queen wonderful in her exceptional charity toward the poor: grant that, through her intercession and example, your charity may continually increase in our hearts.

O God, who were pleased to enroll blessed Rose in the company of your holy Virgins: grant us, we pray, that through her prayers and merits we may be cleansed of all faults, and may enjoy the eternal fellowship of your majesty.

O God, who granted to your blessed Confessor Cajetan to imitate the apostolic manner of life: grant us, through his intercession and example, always to trust in you and to desire heavenly things alone.

O God, who granted to your blessed Confessor Ferdinand to wage your battles and to overcome the enemies of the faith: grant that we, fortified by his intercession, may be freed from the enemies of mind and body.

O God, who granted to your blessed Martyr and Bishop Irenaeus that he both defeated heresies by the truth of his teaching and happily confirmed the peace of the Church: grant, we pray, constancy in holy religion to your people, and give your peace to our times.

O God, who entrusted to your blessed Apostle Peter, by conferring upon him the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, the power of binding and loosing: grant that, aided by the help of his intercession, we may be freed from the bonds of our sins.
Commemoration of Saint Paul the Apostle
Holy Paul the Apostle, preacher of truth and teacher of the Gentiles, intercede for us to God, who chose you.
You are a vessel of election, holy Paul the Apostle.
Preacher of truth throughout the whole world.

Let us pray.
O God, who through the preaching of the blessed Apostle Paul taught the multitude of the Gentiles: grant us, we pray, that we may experience his patronage before you, whose commemoration we honor.

O God, who made your blessed Confessor Alexis wonderful in his contempt for the world: grant, we pray, that, aided by the help of his intercession, your faithful may despise earthly things and always aspire toward heavenly things.

O God, who made your blessed Bishop and Doctor Albert great in subjecting human wisdom to the divine faith: grant us, we pray, so to adhere to the footsteps of his teaching that we may enjoy perfect light in heaven.

O God, who exalted your blessed Confessor and Bishop Anthony Mary with apostolic virtues, and through him gathered new families of clerics and virgins in your Church: grant, we pray, that, guided by his counsels and aided by his merits, we may continually strive to seek the salvation of souls.

O God, who raised your blessed Bishop Benedict to heaven by the grace of your blessing: sanctify your people, we pray, with a new blessing, and defend them from all impending evils, by your power, through his merits and prayers.

O God, who adorned your blessed Clement Mary with wondrous strength of faith and the virtue of unconquered constancy: make us, we pray, through his merits and examples, so strong in faith and fervent in charity that we may attain eternal rewards.

O God, who made your blessed Confessor and Bishop Cyril an unconquered defender of the divine maternity of the most blessed Virgin Mary: grant, through his intercession, that we who truly believe her to be the Mother of God may be saved by her motherly protection.

O God, who adorned your blessed Martyr and Bishop Emygdius with the glory of victory over idols and with the glory of miracles: graciously grant that, through his intercession, we may merit to prevail against the powers of evil spirits.

O God, who were pleased to call your blessed Confessor Felix from the desert by a heavenly summons to the office of redeeming captives: grant, we pray, that, freed from the captivity of our sins by the grace, through his intercession, we may be led to the heavenly homeland.

O God, who were pleased to crown your blessed Fidel, enkindled with the seraphic ardor of spirit in the propagation of the true faith, with the palm of martyrdom and with glorious miracles: grant, we pray, through his merits and intercession, so to confirm us by your grace in faith and charity that we may merit to be found faithful in your service even unto death.

O God, who adorned your blessed Francis, the founder of a new order, with zeal for prayer and love of penance: grant your servants so to advance in his imitation that, always praying and bringing the body into subjection, they may merit to attain heavenly glory.

O God, who taught your blessed Gabriel continually to recall the sorrows of your most sweet Mother, and through her exalted him with the glory of holiness and miracles: grant us, through his intercession and example, so to be united to the tears of your Mother that we may be saved by her motherly protection.

O God, who wondrously brought your blessed Martyr Gallicanus to knowledge of you, and were pleased through him to illustrate your Church with a new example of charity: graciously grant that, through his prayers and imitation, we may attain the rewards promised to the merciful.

O God, who willed that your blessed Confessor and Bishop Gregory should be renowned for pastoral solicitude and compassion for the poor: graciously grant that we may imitate the examples of charity of him whose merits we celebrate.

O God, who strengthened your blessed Martyr Hermes with the virtue of constancy in his passion: grant us from his imitation that we may despise worldly prosperity for love of you, and fear no adversity of the world.

O God, who taught your blessed Martyr Hermenegild to prefer the heavenly kingdom to an earthly principality: grant us, we pray, following his example, to despise transient things and to pursue eternal ones.

O God, who observe that your blessed Confessor and Bishop Innocent, adorned with the gifts of knowledge and prudence, was made a conciliator of peace and unity: grant us, through his intercession, to savor heavenly things and to pursue all good things with harmonious zeal.

O God, who wondrously enkindled your blessed Confessor John to promote fittingly the devotion to the sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary, and through him willed to gather new families in your Church: grant, we pray, that we who venerate his holy merits may also be instructed by the examples of his virtues.

O God, who were pleased wondrously to stir up your blessed Confessor John for the propagation of the faith among the nations, and through him gathered in your Church a new family for the instruction of the faithful: grant to us your servants so to advance in his institutions that we may attain eternal rewards.

O God, who made your blessed John, enkindled with love of you, walk unharmed through flames, and through him made your Church fruitful with new offspring: grant, through the intercession of his merits, that our vices may be healed by the fire of your charity, and that eternal remedies may come to us.

O God, who equaled your blessed Confessor and Bishop Leo with your holy ones in merit: graciously grant that we who solemnly observe the feast of his commemoration may also imitate the examples of his life.

O God, who translated your blessed Confessor Louis from an earthly kingdom to the glory of the heavenly kingdom: grant, we pray, through his merits and intercession, that you may make us sharers in the reign of the King of kings, Jesus Christ your Son.
O God, who exalted your blessed Evangelist Mark with the grace of evangelical preaching: grant, we pray, that we may always advance through his instruction and be defended by his prayer.
O God, who united your blessed Matthias to the company of your Apostles: grant, we pray, that through his intercession we may always experience the depths of your loving kindness toward us.
O God, who adorned your blessed Bishop Nicholas with countless miracles: grant, we pray, that through his merits and prayers we may be freed from the fires of hell.

O God, who made your blessed Confessor and Bishop Norbert an outstanding herald of your word, and through him made your Church fruitful with new offspring: grant, we pray, that, aided by his merits and intercession, we may be able, with your help, to practice what he taught by word and deed alike.

O God, who adorned your blessed Confessor Paschal with wondrous love for the sacred mysteries of your Body and Blood: graciously grant that we may merit to receive the same spiritual richness that he drew from this divine banquet.
O God, who caused your blessed Apostle Peter, freed from his chains, to depart unharmed: absolve, we pray, the chains of our sins, and in your mercy drive away all evils from us.

O God, who raised your blessed Confessor Peter Celestine to the height of the supreme pontificate, and taught him to set humility before it: graciously grant that, following his example, we may happily merit to despise all things of the world and to attain the rewards promised to the humble.

O God, who willed that your blessed Confessor and Bishop Peter Chrysologus, divinely designated beforehand, should be chosen to govern and instruct your Church: grant, we pray, that we who had him as a Doctor of life on earth may merit to have him as an intercessor in heaven.
