O God, who were pleased to illustrate your blessed Confessor Peter with the gift of admirable penance and deepest contemplation: grant us, we pray, that, aided by his intercession, mortified in the flesh, we may more readily lay hold of heavenly things.
O God, who raised your blessed Confessor Philip with the glory of your Saints: graciously grant that we who rejoice on his solemnity may advance through the example of his virtues.
O God, who gave the blessed Archangel Raphael to your servant Tobias as a companion on the way: grant us your servants that we may always be protected by his guardianship and fortified by his aid.

O God, who chose your blessed Raymond as a distinguished minister of the Sacrament of Penance, and wondrously led him across the waves of the sea: grant that, through his intercession, we may bring forth fruits worthy of penance and attain the port of eternal salvation.
O God, who crowned your blessed Confessor King Edward with the glory of eternity: grant us, we pray, so to venerate him on earth that we may be able to reign with him in heaven.
O God, who made your blessed Confessor and Bishop Siricius an outstanding promoter of ecclesiastical discipline: grant to your Church to advance in his institutions and to be aided by his merits.

O God, who adorned your blessed Bishop Thomas with the virtue of remarkable mercy toward the poor: grant, we pray, that, through his intercession, you may mercifully pour out upon all who implore you the riches of your mercy.

O God, who adorned your blessed Confessor and Bishop Titus with apostolic virtues: grant, through his merits and intercession, that, living justly and devoutly in this age, we may merit to attain the heavenly homeland.

O God, who through the palm of martyrdom translated your blessed Wenceslaus from an earthly principality to heavenly glory: guard us by his prayers from all adversity, and grant that we may rejoice in his fellowship.

O God, who adorned the Order of Carmel with the singular title of the most blessed ever-Virgin and Mother of God, Mary: graciously grant that we who today celebrate her Commemoration with solemn office, fortified by her protection, may merit to attain everlasting joy.
O God, who observe that we subsist by no virtue of our own: graciously grant that, through the intercession of your blessed Confessor and Bishop Martin, we may be fortified against all adversity.
O God, who observe that our own evils disturb us on every side: grant, we pray, that the glorious intercession of your blessed Apostle and Evangelist John may protect us.

O God, who willed that your Word should take flesh from the womb of the Blessed Virgin Mary at the announcement of the Angel: grant to your suppliants that we who truly believe her to be the Mother of God may be aided by her intercessions before you.

O God, who gave the law to Moses on the summit of Mount Sinai, and in the same place wondrously placed the body of your blessed Virgin and Martyr Catherine through your holy Angels: grant, we pray, that through her merits and intercession we may be able to attain to the mountain that is Christ.

O God, who were pleased to give us the Mother of your beloved Son as our Mother and Patron: graciously grant that, under the protection of this Mother, we may be defended from every assault of our enemies, and serve you without fear in holiness and righteousness.

O God, who were pleased to provide for your Church your blessed Confessor Jerome as a most eminent Doctor in the exposition of the sacred Scriptures: grant, we pray, that, aided by his merits, we may be able, with your help, to practice what he taught by word and deed alike.
O God, who glorify your Church by the learning of your blessed Confessor and Doctor Bede: graciously grant your servants always to be enlightened by his wisdom and to be aided by his merits.

O God, who were pleased to illuminate your Church with the merits and teachings of your blessed Confessor Dominic: grant that, through his intercession, she may not be deprived of temporal assistance and may always advance in spiritual growth.

O God, who willed to illustrate your Church with the wondrous learning and the distinguished merits of life of your blessed Confessor and Doctor Ephrem: we humbly implore you that, through his intercession, you may defend her by your enduring power against the snares of error and wickedness.

O God, who enlarge your Church with new offspring through the merits of your blessed Francis: grant us, from his imitation, to despise earthly things and always to rejoice in sharing in heavenly gifts.

O God, who enlarged your Church with the zeal of religion and apostolic labors of your blessed Confessor and Bishop Gregory: grant, through his merits and intercession, that she may always receive new growth in faith and holiness.

O God, who glorify your Church with the wondrous learning of your blessed Confessor Thomas and make her fruitful with holy action: grant us, we pray, both to perceive by understanding what he taught, and to fulfill by imitation what he did.

O God, who were pleased to illustrate your Church with the merits and preaching of your blessed Confessor Vincent: grant us your servants both to be instructed by his examples and to be freed from all adversities by his patronage.

O God, who in the glorious Transfiguration of your Only Begotten Son confirmed the mysteries of faith by the testimony of the Fathers, and wondrously prefigured the perfect adoption of children by the voice descending in a bright cloud: graciously grant that you may make us co-heirs of the King of glory himself, and grant that we may be sharers in the same glory.

O God, who mercifully led your servant Margaret from the path of perdition to the way of salvation: grant us by the same mercy that we who were not ashamed to follow her when she first went astray may glory in following her eagerly now that she has repented.

O God, who on this day translated your glorious Bishop Willibald, heir of an English kingdom, to the eternal inheritance of the Angels: graciously grant that, through his merits and intercession, we may merit to be his co-heirs in your glory.

O God, who on this day strengthened your blessed Martyr and Bishop Dionysius with the virtue of constancy in his passion, and were pleased to give him Rusticus and Eleutherius as companions for the preaching of your glory to the nations: grant us, we pray, following their example, to despise worldly prosperity for love of you, and to fear no adversity of the world.

O God, who on this day translated your blessed Confessor Henry from the height of an earthly empire to the eternal kingdom: we humbly implore you that, as you made him, prevented by the abundance of your grace, to overcome the allurements of the age, so you may make us, following his example, to avoid the flatteries of this world and to come to you with pure minds.

O God, who on this day revealed your Only Begotten Son to the Gentiles by the guidance of a star: graciously grant that we who have now come to know you by faith may be led to the contemplation of the vision of your majesty.
O God, who consecrated this day by the martyrdom of your Apostles Peter and Paul: grant to your Church to follow their precepts in all things, through whom she received the beginning of religion.

O God, who have consecrated this day by the triumph of your blessed Martyr Venantius: hear the prayers of your people and grant that we, who venerate his merits, may imitate the steadfastness of his faith.

O God, who in the weakness of flesh assumed willed to be fastened with Nails and wounded with a Lance for the salvation of the world: graciously grant that we, who celebrate the solemnity of those same Nails and Lance on earth, may rejoice in the glorious triumph of your victory in heaven.
O God, who in your blessed Virgin Crescentia mercifully bestowed a model of Christian perfection: grant, we pray, that, ever cleaving to imitation of her, we may attain eternal glory.

O God, who prepared in the heart of your blessed Virgin Gertrude a joyful dwelling for yourself: by her merits and intercession, mercifully cleanse the stains of our heart, and grant us to rejoice in fellowship with her.

O God, who in the heart of your blessed Confessor Andrew, by his arduous daily vow of advancing in virtue, disposed wonderful ascents toward you: grant us, by his merits and intercession, to become such sharers in that same grace that, ever pursuing more perfect things, we may be happily led to the summit of your glory.
O God, who in your Church ever renew new models of virtue: grant your people so to follow the footsteps of your blessed Confessor and Bishop Andrew, that they may attain his reward.

O God, who in liberating your faithful from the captivity of the impious made your blessed Confessor Raymond wonderful: grant us by his intercession that, loosed from the bonds of sin, we may carry out with free minds the things that are pleasing to you.

O God, who made your blessed Confessor Leonard powerful in deed and word in bending the stubborn hearts of sinners to repentance: grant, we pray, that through his prayers and merits we may be able to draw tears of contrition from our hearts.
O God, who at the glorious Finding of the life-giving Cross raised up the wonders of your Passion: grant that by the power of the wood of life we may obtain the suffrage of eternal life.

O God, who, as a model of your charity and for the redemption of the faithful, by divine inspiration taught your holy Peter to make your Church fruitful with new offspring: grant us by his intercession that, freed from the slavery of sin, we may rejoice in perpetual liberty in the heavenly homeland.

O God, who willed to gather the peoples of the Indies into your Church by the preaching and miracles of blessed Francis: graciously grant that we, who venerate his glorious merits, may also imitate his models of virtue.

O God, who in your ineffable providence were pleased to choose blessed Joseph as the spouse of your most holy Mother: grant, we pray, that he whom we venerate as protector on earth, we may merit to have as intercessor in heaven.

O God, who in your ineffable providence are pleased to send your holy Angels to watch over us: bestow upon your suppliants both always to be defended by their protection and to rejoice in their eternal company.

O God, who have set before your people the example and support of your Saints for treading the path of salvation in our weakness: grant us so to venerate the merits of blessed Abbot William, that we may receive his intercession and follow his footsteps.

O God, who among the other wonders of your power have bestowed even upon the fragile sex the victory of martyrdom: graciously grant that we, who celebrate the birthday of your blessed Virgin and Martyr Philomena, may advance toward you by her example.

O God, who among the other wonders of your wisdom have bestowed even in tender age the grace of mature holiness: grant, we pray, that, by the merits and examples of blessed Stanislaus and John, redeeming time by working earnestly, we may hasten to enter into eternal rest.

O God, who among the other wonders of your wisdom have bestowed even in tender age the grace of mature holiness: grant, we pray, that, by the example of blessed Stanislaus, redeeming time by working earnestly, we may hasten to enter into eternal rest.

O God, who among the other Angels chose the Archangel Gabriel to announce the mystery of your Incarnation: graciously grant that we, who celebrate his feast on earth, may experience his patronage in heaven.

O God, who among the countless gifts of your grace work great things even in the female sex: graciously grant that we may experience the patronage of your blessed Virgin Walburga before your mercy, by whose examples of chastity we are illumined and by whose glory of miracles we are gladdened.

O God, who among the first Martyrs of Japan crowned blessed Philip, bound to the Cross and pierced with a triple lance, with martyrdom first of all: graciously grant that, upheld by his patronage, we may be crowned together with him in heaven.

O God, who strengthened holy Casimir with the virtue of constancy amid royal delights and worldly allurements: we beseech you that, by his intercession, your faithful may despise earthly things and always aspire to heavenly things.
O God, who in wondrous order dispense the ministries of Angels and of men: graciously grant that our life on earth may be defended by those who always stand ministering to you in heaven.

O God, who willed to open the door of your mercy to the faithful: we humbly implore you that, through the intercession of your blessed Confessor Conrad, you may grant us both temporal support and eternal.

O God, who promised a hundredfold in the world to come and eternal life to those who forsake all things for you in this world: graciously grant that, cleaving to the footsteps of holy Bishop Paulinus, we may be able to despise earthly things and desire heavenly things alone.
O God, who have instructed the multitude of nations by the preaching of your blessed Apostle Paul: grant us, we pray, that we, who celebrate his birthday, may experience his patronage before you.
Commemoration of Saint Peter the Apostle
You are the shepherd of the sheep, Prince of the Apostles; to you have been given the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven.
You are Peter.
And upon this rock I will build my Church.

Let us pray.
O God, who by conferring on your blessed Apostle Peter the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven bestowed upon him the office of binding and loosing: grant that, by the help of his intercession, we may be freed from the bonds of our sins.

O God, who were pleased by the zeal of your blessed Martyr and Bishop Boniface to call the multitude of peoples to knowledge of your name: graciously grant that we, who celebrate his solemnity, may also experience his patronage.

O God, who have bestowed on the soul of your servant Gregory the rewards of eternal blessedness: graciously grant that we, who are weighed down by the burden of our sins, may be lifted up by his prayers before you.

O God, who caused the soul of your blessed Virgin and servant Scholastica to enter heaven in the form of a dove, to show the way of innocence: grant us by her merits and prayers so to live innocently that we may merit to attain eternal joys.

O God, who in the holy Shroud, in which your most sacred body was wrapped by Joseph when taken down from the Cross, have left us the marks of your Passion: graciously grant that through your death and burial we may be led to the glory of the Resurrection.
O God, who gladden us by the merits and intercession of your blessed Apostle Barnabas: graciously grant that we, who seek your blessings through him, may obtain them by the gift of your grace.
O God, who surround and protect us by the glorious confession of your blessed Bishop Benno: grant us both to advance by imitation of him and to rejoice in his intercession.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Confessor Eusebius: graciously grant that we, who celebrate his birthday, may advance toward you by his example.
O God, who gladden us by the merits and intercession of your blessed Martyr George: graciously grant that we, who seek your blessings through him, may obtain them by the gift of your grace.
O God, who grant us to rejoice in the birthday of your blessed Martyr Saturninus: grant that we may be aided by his merits.
O God, who surround and protect us by the glorious confession of your blessed Martyr Theodore: grant us to advance by imitation of him and to be sustained by his prayer.

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Confessor and Bishop Ulrich: graciously grant that, by his merits and intercession, we may be freed from the dangers of our sins and merit to enjoy eternal joys.
O God, who see that we fail through our own weakness: mercifully restore us, through the examples of your Saints, to love of you.
O God, who see that we fail through our own weakness: mercifully restore us, through the example of your blessed Martyr and Bishop Callistus, to love of you.
O God, who grant us to celebrate the birthdays of your holy Martyrs Sixtus, Felicissimus, and Agapitus: grant us to rejoice in their company in eternal blessedness.

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of the Exaltation of the holy Cross: grant, we pray, that we, who have come to know its mystery on earth, may merit the rewards of its redemption in heaven.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your Apostles Philip and James: grant, we pray, that we, who rejoice in their merits, may be instructed by their examples.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Virgin and Martyr Agnes: grant, we pray, that we, who honor her in our observance, may also follow her example of holy conduct.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Virgin and Martyr Cecilia: grant that we, who honor her in our observance, may also follow her example of holy conduct.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Martyr and Bishop Clement: graciously grant that we, who celebrate his birthday, may also imitate the virtue of his Passion.

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of the glorious Passion of your blessed Martyr Florian: in the abundance of your accustomed loving kindness graciously grant that we, who venerate with devout love his celebrated triumph in his honor on earth, may merit, by your gift, to attain the joy of fellowship with him in heaven.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Martyrs Marcellinus and Peter: grant, we pray, that we, who rejoice in their merits, may be enkindled by their examples.
O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed Martyrs Marcellinus, Peter, and Erasmus: grant, we pray, that we, who rejoice in their merits, may be enkindled by their examples.
O God, who have granted us to come to knowledge of your name through your blessed Apostles Simon and Jude: grant us both to celebrate their eternal glory by advancing and to advance by celebrating.

O God, who gladden us by the annual expectation of our redemption: grant that we may behold with confidence, as he comes in judgment, your Only Begotten Son whom we joyfully receive as Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ your Son.
O God, who surround and protect us by the glorious confessions of your holy Martyrs Processus and Martinianus: grant us both to advance by imitation of them and to rejoice in their intercession.

O God, who willed that through blessed Angela a new college of sacred Virgins should flourish in your Church: grant us, by her intercession, to live according to angelic ways, that, renouncing all earthly things, we may merit to enjoy eternal joys.

O God, who by the invincible sacramental silence of blessed John adorned your Church with a new crown of martyrdom: grant us, by his intercession and example, to guard our tongue with care, and to endure all evils in this world rather than harm to the soul.

O God, who by the invincible sacramental silence of blessed John adorned your Church with a new crown of martyrdom: grant us, by his intercession and example, to guard our tongue with care, and to endure all evils in this world rather than harm to the soul.

O God, who counsel your peoples with indulgence and rule them with love: grant the spirit of wisdom to those who aid you by the merits of the bishops of your Church, to whom you have given the governance of discipline, that from the progress of your holy flock there may come forth the eternal joy of the shepherds.

O God, who through your blessed Confessor and Bishop Alphonsus Mary, enkindled with zeal for souls, have made your Church fruitful with new offspring: we beseech you that, instructed by his salutary counsels and strengthened by his examples, we may happily attain to you.

O God, who through your blessed Bishop and Martyr Gregory granted the people and king of the nation of Armenia to receive the light of the true faith: grant your Church to rejoice in such great triumphs and to be aided before you by his merits and prayers.

O God, who through blessed John enabled your faithful to triumph over the enemies of the Cross by the power of the most holy Name of Jesus: grant, we pray, that, with the snares of spiritual enemies overcome by his intercession, we may merit to receive from you the crown of justice.

O God, who through your blessed Confessor Philip have given us a distinguished model of humility: grant your servants, by imitation of him, to despise worldly prosperity and always to seek heavenly things.

O God, who through your blessed Confessor and Bishop Victor, in declining and in defending the highest dignity of the Church, gave a distinguished example of humility and fortitude: grant us, by his merits and imitation, to overcome with invincible spirit all the snares of our enemies.

O God, who through the most glorious Mother of your Son were pleased to enlarge your Church with new offspring for the liberation of Christ's faithful from the power of the pagans: grant, we pray, that we, who devoutly venerate her as foundress of so great a work, may likewise by her merits and intercession be freed from all sins and from the captivity of the devil.

O God, who through the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son: we humbly beseech you that we, celebrating the Apparition of that same Virgin, may obtain health of mind and body.

O God, who through the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son: we beseech you that, as you preserved her from all stain by reason of the foreseen death of that same Son of yours, you may also grant that we, made pure by her intercession, may come to you.

O God, who by heaven's inspiration were pleased through Saint John to establish the Order of the Most Holy Trinity for the redemption of captives from the power of the Saracens: grant, we pray, that, aided by his merits, we may, with your help, be freed from the captivity of body and soul.

O God, who through your blessed Confessor Joseph were pleased to provide a new support for your Church for instructing youth in the spirit of understanding and piety: grant, we pray, that, by his example and intercession, we may so do and teach as to attain eternal rewards.

O God, who through the foolishness of the Cross wondrously taught your blessed Martyr Justin the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ: grant us by his intercession that, with the entanglement of errors driven away, we may attain firmness of faith.

O God, who willed that blessed Joachim should be father of the Mother of your Son above all your other Saints: grant, we pray, that we, who venerate his feast, may also continually experience his patronage.

O God, who made this present day honorable for us in the birth of blessed John: grant your peoples the grace of spiritual joys, and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of eternal salvation.

O God, who consecrated the first fruits of faith in the northern regions of America by the preaching and blood of your holy Martyrs Isaac, John, and their Companions: graciously grant that, by their intercession, the flourishing harvest of Christians may everywhere increase day by day.

O God, who consecrated the beginnings of Roman faith with the abundant blood of Martyrs: grant, we pray, that we may be made firm by steadfast virtue in the struggle of so great a contest, and rejoice in holy victory.

O God, who were pleased to bestow such great grace on holy Rita that she loved her enemies and bore on her heart and forehead the marks of your charity and Passion: grant us, we pray, by her intercession and merits, so to spare our enemies and to contemplate the sufferings of your Passion, that we may attain the rewards promised to the meek and those who mourn.

O God, who bestowed on your holy Saints Abdon and Sennen the abundant gift of grace for coming to this glory: grant your servants pardon of their sins, that they may merit, through the interceding merits of your Saints, to be freed from all adversities.

O God, who by zeal for humility and love of poverty made your blessed Confessor Benedict Joseph cleave to you alone: grant us by his interceding merits to despise all earthly things and always to seek heavenly things.

O God, who adorned holy Camillus with a singular prerogative of charity to aid souls struggling in their final agony: pour into us, we pray, through his merits, the spirit of your love, that in the hour of our death we may merit to overcome the enemy and to attain the heavenly crown.

O God, who adorned your blessed Confessor John the Baptist with charity and patience in preaching the Gospel to the poor: grant, we pray, that we, who venerate his holy merits, may also imitate his models of virtue.

O God, who adorned your blessed Confessor John the Baptist with charity and patience in preaching the Gospel to the poor: grant, we pray, that we, who venerate his holy merits, may also imitate his models of virtue.

O God, who raised up holy John, Confessor of yours, as a father and master of youth, and through him, with the aid of the Virgin Mary, willed that new religious families should flourish in your Church: grant, we pray, that, enkindled with the same fire of charity, we may seek souls and be able to serve you alone.
O God, who made holy John, your Confessor and Doctor, a lover outstanding in perfect self-denial and of the Cross: grant that, clinging continually to his imitation, we may attain eternal glory.

O God, who adorned holy John the Baptist, your Confessor, with charity and patience in proclaiming the Gospel to the poor: grant, we pray, that, as we venerate his holy merits, we may likewise imitate the examples of his virtues.

O God, who willed that those placed under the singular patronage of the most Blessed Virgin Mary should be enriched with perpetual blessings: grant your suppliants that, as we rejoice in her commemoration on earth, we may rejoice in her presence in heaven.

O God, who by the Passion of your Only Begotten Son and the shedding of his Blood through his five Wounds restored human nature lost by sin: grant us, we pray, that, as we venerate on earth the Wounds he received, we may merit to obtain in heaven the fruit of that same most precious Blood.

O God, who appointed your Only Begotten Son as Redeemer of the world, and through him, with death overcome, mercifully restored us to life: grant that, recalling these benefits, we may merit to cling to you in perpetual charity and to receive the fruit of that same redemption.
O God, who instructed the whole world through the preaching of the blessed Apostle Paul: grant us, we pray, that, as we celebrate today his Conversion, we may advance toward you by his example.
O God, who deigned to choose the virginal dwelling of the Blessed Mary as your dwelling place: grant, we pray, that, fortified by her defense, you may make us glad to be present at her feast.
O God, glory of your priests: grant, we pray, that we may feel the help of your holy Martyr and Bishop Donatus, whose feast we celebrate.

O God, lover of virginity, who adorned Blessed Mary Magdalene, Virgin, enkindled with love of you, with heavenly gifts: grant that, as we venerate her with joyful solemnity, we may imitate her in purity and charity.
Graciously enlighten your Church, O Lord, that, illumined by the teachings of your blessed Apostle and Evangelist John, she may attain everlasting gifts.

Guard your Church, O Lord, with the constant protection of holy Charles, your Confessor and Bishop: that, as pastoral solicitude made him glorious, so his intercession may make us ever fervent in love of you.
May the votive solemnity of blessed Anthony, your Confessor, gladden your Church, O God: that she may be ever fortified by spiritual helps and merit to enjoy eternal joys.
May the votive solemnity of blessed Anthony, your Confessor and Doctor, gladden your Church, O God: that she may be ever fortified by spiritual helps and merit to enjoy eternal joys.
Enlarge your Church, we pray, O Lord, with heavenly grace: which you have willed to adorn with the glorious merits and teachings of blessed John Chrysostom, your Confessor and Bishop.
Be, O Lord, the sanctifier and guardian of your people: that, fortified by the protection of your Apostle James, it may both please you in its conduct and serve you with tranquil mind.
Hear your people, O Lord, as they supplicate under the patronage of your Saints: that you may grant us to rejoice in the peace of this temporal life and to find the aid of eternal life.
Hear our prayers, O Lord: and, through the intercession of blessed Mark, your Confessor and Bishop, graciously grant us pardon and peace.
Hear our prayers, O Lord: and, through the intercession of blessed Damasus, your Confessor and Bishop, graciously grant us pardon and peace.
Hear us, O God our Savior: that, as we rejoice in the feast of blessed Teresa, your Virgin, we may be nourished by the food of her heavenly teaching and instructed in the spirit of devout piety.

Hear us, O God our Savior: that, as we rejoice in the feast of blessed Rosalia, your Virgin, we may be instructed in the spirit of devout piety and, through her intercession, be mercifully delivered from the scourges of your wrath.

Hear, we pray, O Lord, the prayers we offer at the solemnity of blessed Rupert, your Confessor and Bishop: and, as he merited to serve you worthily, may we, through his interceding merits, be absolved from all our sins.
Stir up in your Church, O Lord, the Spirit whom blessed Lawrence the Levite served: that, filled with that same Spirit, we may strive to love what he loved and to carry out in deed what he taught.

Stir up, we pray, O Lord, in your Church the Spirit by whom blessed Josaphat, your Martyr and Bishop, was filled and laid down his life for his sheep: that, through his intercession, we who are moved and strengthened by that same Spirit may not fear to lay down our lives for our brethren.

Bestow, we pray, O Lord, the gift of heavenly grace upon your servants: that, as the birth of the Blessed Virgin was the beginning of salvation for them, the votive solemnity of her Nativity may grant them an increase of peace.

Bestow, we pray, O Lord, the gift of heavenly grace upon your servants: that, as the birth of the Blessed Virgin was the beginning of salvation for them, the votive solemnity of her Visitation may grant them an increase of peace.

Grant us, O Lord God, to learn, through the spirit of the Apostle Paul, the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ, by which blessed Anthony Mary was wondrously instructed and gathered new families of clerics and virgins in your Church.
Grant us, O Lord Jesus, to walk in simplicity and innocence of heart: out of love for which you descended from the bosom of your Mother into the arms of your Confessor blessed Felix.
Grant, we pray, O Lord, that we may always devotedly follow the feasts of your holy Martyrs Tryphon, Respicius, and Nympha: that by their intercession we may experience the gifts of your protection.
Grant, we pray, O Lord, that we may always devotedly follow the feasts of your holy Martyrs Primus and Felician: that by their intercession we may experience the gifts of your protection.

Bestow, we pray, O Lord, upon your servants the gift of heavenly grace: that, as the birth of the Blessed Virgin was the beginning of salvation for them, the votive solemnity of her Betrothal may grant them an increase of peace.
Commemoration of Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Behold the faithful and prudent servant, whom the Lord set over his household.
Glory and riches are in his house.
And his justice endures for ever and ever.

Let us pray.
May we be aided, O Lord, we pray, by the merits of the Spouse of your most holy Mother: that what our own ability does not obtain may be granted to us through his intercession.
And Jesus himself was beginning to be about thirty years old, being (as it was supposed) the son of Joseph, who was of Heli, who was of Matthat,
(said at the hour of Vespers)
Then Joseph, arising from sleep, did just as the Angel of the Lord had instructed him, and he accepted her as his wife.
He set him as lord over his house.
And ruler of all his possessions.
Pardon, we pray, O Lord, the sins of your servants: that we who are unable to please you by our deeds may be saved through the intercession of the Mother of your Son our Lord.

Bestow, we pray, O Lord, upon your servants the gift of heavenly grace: that, as the birth of the Blessed Virgin was the beginning of salvation for them, the votive solemnity of her Conception may grant them an increase of peace.

Follow your faithful, we pray, O Lord, with gracious favor: that those to whom you showed, in blessed Anna Maria, a pattern of all domestic virtues, you may graciously deign to confirm, as they follow in her footsteps, in holy works continually.
May the brotherly crown of your Martyrs gladden us, O Lord: that it may both bring us growth in the virtues of our faith and console us with its manifold intercession.
May the brotherly crown of your Martyrs gladden us, O Lord: that it may both bring us growth in the virtues of our faith and console us with its manifold intercession.
Look upon our weakness, almighty God: and, since the weight of our own actions burdens us, may the glorious intercession of your blessed Martyrs Fabian and Sebastian protect us.
May your holy Luke the Evangelist intercede for us, O Lord: he who continually bore in his own body the mortification of the Cross, for the honor of your name.
May your Church, O God, rejoice, confident in the intercession of your blessed Martyr Agapitus: and, by his glorious prayers, may she remain devout and stand secure.
We humbly implore your Majesty, O Lord: that, as you continually gladden us with the commemoration of your Saints, so you may always defend us with their supplication.
We humbly implore your Majesty, O Lord: that, as blessed Andrew the Apostle was a preacher and guide of your Church, so may he be a perpetual intercessor for us before you.

Almighty and merciful God, who wondrously established, in the most Blessed Virgin Mary, a perpetual help for the defense of the Christian people: graciously grant that, fortified by such protection, we who struggle in this life may be able in death to gain victory over the malignant enemy.

Almighty and merciful God, who adorned blessed Galla with the outstanding virtue of love for the poor: grant through her merits and prayers that, as we practice works of charity, we may merit to obtain your mercy.

Almighty and merciful God, who endowed blessed Jane Frances, enkindled with love of you, with an admirable strength of spirit along every path of life in the way of perfection, and who willed through her to illustrate your Church with new offspring: grant through her merits and prayers that, as we, conscious of our weakness, trust in your power, we may overcome, with the help of heavenly grace, all things that oppose us.

Almighty and merciful God, who made holy John Mary wonderful by his pastoral zeal and burning ardor of unceasing prayer and penance: grant, we pray, that, by his example and intercession, we may be able to win souls to Christ and to attain eternal glory together with them.

Almighty and merciful God, who illumine the whole world with the light of truth, and deigned to renew the wonders of faith in the regions of Africa through the glorious Martyrs Matthias, Charles, and their Companions: graciously bestow upon your suppliants that, through their intercession, you may preserve in us the gifts of your grace, and that among all peoples the number and worth of those who serve you may increase.

Almighty and most gentle God, who exalted your blessed Confessor Adrian to the apostolic dignity, and mercifully opened for him the gate of the heavenly kingdom: grant, we pray, that through his devout intercessions we may merit to obtain both the supports of this present life and the eternal rewards.

Almighty and most gentle God, who exalted your blessed Confessor Adrian to the apostolic dignity, and mercifully opened for him the gate of the heavenly kingdom: grant, we pray, that through his devout intercessions we may merit to obtain both the supports of this present life and the eternal rewards.
Almighty ever-living God, direct our actions according to your good pleasure: that in the name of your beloved Son we may merit to abound in good works.

Almighty ever-living God, we humbly implore your Majesty: that, as your Only Begotten Son was this day presented in the temple in the substance of our flesh, so you may make us to be presented before you with purified minds.

Almighty ever-living God, who imbued blessed John with heavenly teaching and admirable strength of spirit for the defense of the veneration of sacred images: grant us through his intercession and example that, as we honor the images of those whose likenesses we venerate, we may imitate their virtues and experience their patronage.

Almighty ever-living God, who choose the weak things of the world to confound the strong: graciously grant our humility that, through the devout prayers of your blessed Confessor Didacus, we may merit to be raised up to everlasting glory in heaven.

Almighty ever-living God, who bestowed upon this day the venerable and holy joy in the feast of your blessed Apostle Bartholomew: grant to your Church, we pray, both to love what he believed and to preach what he taught.

Almighty ever-living God, who, so that the human race might have an example to imitate in humility, made our Savior take flesh and undergo the Cross: graciously grant that, as we solemnly commemorate his Passion, we may merit both to have the lessons of his patience and to share in his Resurrection.

Almighty ever-living God, who assumed the Immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of your Son, body and soul into heavenly glory: grant, we pray, that, always intent on the things above, we may merit to be sharers in her glory.

Almighty ever-living God, who prepared the Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary as a worthy dwelling place of the Holy Spirit: graciously grant that, as we devoutly call to mind the feast of that most pure Heart, we may be able to live according to your own Heart.

Almighty ever-living God, who willed to restore all things in your beloved Son, the King of all: graciously grant that all the families of the nations, scattered by the wound of sin, may be made subject to his most gentle dominion.

Almighty ever-living God, who choose the weak things of the world to confound the strong: graciously grant that, as we celebrate the solemnities of your blessed Agnes, Virgin and Martyr, we may experience her patronage before you.

Almighty ever-living God, who granted us to venerate the merits of all your Saints in a single solemnity: we pray that you may lavish upon us the longed-for abundance of your mercy, through the multiplied intercessions.

Almighty ever-living God, who consecrated the firstfruits of the Martyrs in the blood of the blessed Levite Stephen: grant, we pray, that he may stand as intercessor for us, who prayed to our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, even for his persecutors.

Almighty ever-living God, who granted the peoples of Slavonia to come to the knowledge of your name through your blessed Confessors and Bishops Cyril and Methodius: grant that, as we glory in their feast, we may be united to their company.

Almighty ever-living God, who appointed your Only Begotten Son as Redeemer of the world and willed to be appeased by his Blood: grant, we pray, that we may so venerate with solemn worship the price of our salvation and be defended on earth from the evils of this present life by its power, that we may rejoice in perpetual fruit in heaven.
Guard your people, we pray, O Lord, with unceasing devotion: and, through the interceding merits of blessed Roch, keep them safe from all contagion of soul and body.

Grant, O Lord, the fulfillment of our prayers with exultation: that, as we annually recall with devotion the day of the Passion of your holy Martyrs Euphemia, Lucy, and Geminianus, we may also follow their steadfastness in faith.
Grant, we pray, O Lord, that, just as the natalicia of your holy Martyrs Nabor and Felix do not fail to be celebrated, so may they continually accompany us with their intercession.

Grant, we pray, O Lord, that, as the Christian people rejoice in the temporal solemnity of your Martyrs Felix, Simplicius, Faustinus, and Beatrice, so they may enjoy eternal joy, and what they celebrate by their vows they may grasp in effect.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that, as we review the solemnities of your Martyr blessed Felicity, we may be protected by her merits and her prayers.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we may follow with fitting devotion the faith of your blessed Martyr Peter, who merited to obtain the palm of martyrdom for the spread of that same faith.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we may be instructed by the examples of blessed Zephyrinus, your Martyr and Bishop, in whose merits we rejoice.

Grant, we pray, almighty God, that your family may walk on the way of salvation; and, by following the exhortations of blessed John the Precursor, may it come safely to him whom John foretold, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that you permit us not to be shaken by any disturbances, you who have established us on the rock of the apostolic confession.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of blessed Valentine, your Martyr, may be freed by his intercession from all imminent evils.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who have known the glorious Martyrs to be steadfast in their confession, may experience them to be gracious with you in their intercession for us.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who venerate on earth the crown of thorns of our Lord Jesus Christ in memory of his Passion, may merit to be crowned by him with glory and honor in heaven.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your holy Martyrs Mark and Marcellian, may be freed from all imminent evils by their intercessions.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your Saints Alexander, Eventius, Theodulus, and Juvenal, may be freed from all imminent evils by their intercessions.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the feast of your holy Martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus, may likewise imitate their virtues.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the feast of your holy Martyrs Vitalis and Agricola, may be aided by their intercessions with you.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your holy Martyrs Cosmas and Damian, may be freed from all imminent evils by their intercessions.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your Saints Alexander, Eventius, and Theodulus, may be freed from all imminent evils by their intercessions.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your Saints Eventius, Theodulus, and Juvenal, may be freed from all imminent evils by their intercessions.
Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your holy Martyr and Pontiff Alexander and his Companions, may be freed from all imminent evils by their intercessions.
Mercifully hear the prayers of your people, we pray, O Lord, that we may be aided by the merits of blessed Marcellus, your Martyr and Pontiff, in whose Passion we rejoice.

Be gracious, we pray, O Lord, to us your servants through the glorious merits of blessed Valentine, your Confessor and Pontiff (in the Cathedral church is added: "who rests in this Cathedral Church"), that by his devout intercession we may be protected from all adversity.

We pray, almighty God, that the twofold joy of today's feast may receive us, which proceeds from the glorification of blessed John and Paul, whom the same faith and the same Passion made truly brothers.

O God, Creator of all things, who have ordained the law of labor for the human race: mercifully grant that, following the example and under the patronage of Saint Joseph, we may accomplish the works you command and attain the rewards you promise.

May the anniversary of your holy Martyrs Basilides, Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius, we pray, O Lord, shine forth for us with our votive joy; and may what everlasting excellence has bestowed upon them increase through the fruits of our devotion.
May the blessed merits of your holy Martyrs, O Lord, Sergius, Bacchus, Marcellus, and Apuleius, accompany us and ever make us ardent in your love.
May the unceasing protection of your holy Martyrs Tiburtius and Susanna, O Lord, cherish us; for you do not cease to look graciously upon those whom you have granted to be aided by such help.
May the blessed confession of your Saints, O Lord, Victor, Innocentius, Nazarius, and Celsus, strengthen us; and may it graciously implore on our behalf support for our frailty.
We pray, O Lord, that we may be aided by the merits of the Spouse of your most holy Mother; that what our own power cannot obtain, may be granted to us by his intercession.
May we be aided by the merits of Saint Antoninus, O Lord, your Confessor and Pontiff, that as we proclaim you to be wonderful in him, so may we glory that you have been merciful toward us.

May we be aided, we pray, O Lord, by the intercessions of Saint Bruno, your Confessor; that we who have gravely offended your Majesty by our sins, may obtain through his merits and prayers the pardon of our offenses.
May the venerable feast of Saint John the Baptist, your Precursor and Martyr, we pray, O Lord, bring about for us the effect of saving help.
May your Saint Gorgonius, O Lord, gladden us by his intercession and make us rejoice in his devout solemnity.
May the blessed solemnity of your Martyrs Nereus, Achilleus, Domitilla, and Pancras, we pray, O Lord, ever cherish us and render us worthy of your service.
O God, who shows mercy, enlighten the hearts of your faithful; and by the glorious prayers of blessed Elizabeth, make us despise the prosperity of the world and ever rejoice in heavenly consolation.
Follow with heavenly loving kindness, we pray, O Lord, the prayers of your suppliant people, that they may both see what must be done and grow strong to fulfil what they have seen.

From the hinge of the sun's rising
To the bounds of the earth,
Let us sing Christ as our Prince,
Born of the Virgin Mary.

The blessed Author of the age
Took on a servant's body,
That, freeing flesh by flesh,
He might not lose those he had made.

The grace of heaven enters
The womb of the chaste Mother;
The Virgin's womb bears
Secrets it had not known.

The dwelling of a pure heart
Becomes suddenly the temple of God;
Untouched, knowing no man,
She conceived a Son in her womb.

The mother in labor brings forth
Him whom Gabriel had foretold,
Whom the Baptist, leaping in his mother's womb,
Had sensed, enclosed.

He endured to lie on hay;
He did not disdain the manger;
And he was nourished with little milk,
He through whom not even a bird goes hungry.

The choir of heaven rejoices,
And the Angels sing to God;
And the Shepherd, Creator of all,
Is made manifest to the shepherds.

Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

In tender years, fleeing the crowds
Of citizens, you sought the caves of the desert,
Lest your life be stained
By any slight sin of the tongue.

The camel provided a rough covering
For your sacred limbs; a belt of hide;
Spring water for drink, locusts
Mixed with honey for food.

The other prophets only foretold in heart
Presaging that the light was to come;
But you openly point out
Him who takes away the sin of the world.

There was born none more holy
Throughout the wide world than John,
Who merited to baptize in water
Him who washes away the sin of the age.

Glory be to the Father, and to the begotten Son,
And to you, O Spirit, equal power of both,
God, ever one,
For all ages of time.
Amen.

The noble athlete of Christ
Condemns the idols of the nations,
And, wounded by love of God,
Despises the perils of life.

Bound with harsh thongs,
He is hurled headlong from the cliff;
Thorns tear his face;
His body is shredded on the rocks.

While the servants drag the Martyr's limbs,
They languish with thirst;
Venantius by the sign of the Cross
Draws springs of water from the cliff.

O most valiant warrior,
Who offers a draught to your faithless torturers,
Sprinkle us with the dew of grace.

May praise be to the Father, may praise be to the Son,
And to you, O Holy Spirit;
May the prayers of Venantius obtain
For us blessed joys.
Amen.

The tyrant hears with dread
That the Prince of kings draws near,
Who rules the name of Israel
And holds the throne of David.

He cries out, mad at the news:
A successor is at hand, we are driven out;
Guard, go, seize the sword,
Drown the cradles in blood.

What does such great wickedness avail?
What does the crime profit Herod?
Among so many deaths, Christ alone
Is taken up unharmed.

Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

Forerunner of the sun,
Blessed herald of salvation,
Your people in the shadow of night
Supplicantly call upon you, O Virgin.

A torrent drawing all
Into its whirlpool with baleful waves
Sinks to a gentle calm
When the Ark of the covenant passes by.

While the earth burns and dries up,
You alone are bedewed with dew;
With the earth around you moistened,
You alone remain untouched.

The serpent, breathing its deadly venom,
Raises up its head;
But you, unconquered, crush
The swollen head of the dragon.

Gracious Mother, look upon
The tears and prayers of your suppliants,
And as victor over hell,
Guard those who struggle against foes.

Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

Forerunner of the sun,
blessed herald of salvation,
in the shadow of night your people
supplicantly call upon you, O Virgin.

A torrent drawing all
into its whirlpool with baleful waves,
sinks to a gentle calm,
when the Ark of the covenant passes by.

The serpent, breathing its deadly venom,
raises up its head;
but you, unconquered, crush
the swollen head of the dragon.

Gracious Mother, look upon
the tears and prayers of your suppliants,
and as victor over hell,
guard those who struggle against foes.

Jesus, to you be glory,
who were born of the Virgin,
with the Father and the gracious Spirit,
for everlasting ages.
Amen.

Forerunner of the sun,
Heralding the months of flowers,
It greets the sounding house
Of the craftsman in Nazareth.

Hail, head of the household,
Beneath whom the supreme Craftsman,
Dripping with salty sweat,
Practices his fathers' trade.

Set in the high seat
And near the exalted Spouse,
Be present now to those who depend on you,
Whom need distresses.

Let violence and strife be absent,
All fraud from wages;
Let frugality alone measure out
A sufficiency of food and sustenance.

O Unity of the Trinity,
At the prayer of Joseph, we ask
That you guide in peace
The steps and the way of all of us.
Amen.

The blessed queen of heaven
Resounds with joyful songs,
And the earth below with its applause
Chimes in harmony with both poles.

Girt with a nimbus of glory,
Francesca, clinging diligently
To the footsteps of Xavier,
Triumphs among the heavenly.

Already from her tender years
She is consumed with love for Jesus
And turns it over in her heart
To bring him to all peoples.

Behold, a heavenly voice drives
The dove from her native nest;
To the uttermost ends of the world
She often flies with him.

Strength, honor, praise, and glory
To God the Father with the Son
And the Holy Paraclete together
For ages of ages.
Amen.

Blessed Shepherd Peter, graciously receive
The voices of those who pray, and loose
The bonds of their sins by your word,
To whom power was given to open heaven to the earth and to close what is open.

May eternal glory be to the Trinity,
Honor, power, and jubilation,
In the unity that governs all things,
Through all the ages of eternity.
Amen.

Blessed Shepherd Peter, graciously receive
The voices of those who pray, and loose
The bonds of their sins by your word,
To whom power was given to open heaven to the earth and to close what is open.

Excellent Doctor Paul, instruct our manners
And draw our hearts with you to heaven;
While faith still veiled may see the noonday,
And charity alone may reign as the sun.

May eternal glory be to the Trinity,
Honor, power, and jubilation,
In the unity that governs all things,
Through all the ages of eternity.
Amen.

While wars raged far and wide,
And cities groaned, bloody with fraternal slaughter,
The Virgin appeared, ever bringing forth
New gifts of a mother.

She calls seven servants, that they
May faithfully recall in sorrow the sufferings
Which Jesus bore, which she herself shared
Beneath the Cross of her Son.

At once they obey the Lady's call;
Splendid dwellings and riches despised,
They withdraw from the city far to the hidden
Depths of Mount Senario.

Here they afflict their bodies with bitter penances,
Atoning for the sins of guilty men;
Here with prayer and flowing tears
They avert the wrath of God.

The grieving Mother fosters them, and herself
Bids them put on the garb of mourning;
The holy company's devout beginnings rise up,
Wonders are made manifest.

A vine-branch, green in winter, announces
The glories of the fathers; children
With milky lips call upon the servants
Of Mary by her own name.

Glory be to the Father, and to the begotten Son,
And to you, O Spirit, equal power of both,
God, ever one,
For all ages of time.
Amen.

O Juliana, while you seek
The wedding feast of the heavenly Lamb,
You leave your father's house
And lead a chorus of virgins.

And while you weep night and day
For the Spouse nailed to the Cross,
Smitten by the lance of sorrow,
You bear the image of your Spouse.

You weep at the knees of the Mother of God
With sevenfold wounds indeed;
But charity, poured in with tears,
Grows and raises its flames.

Then, as death draws near and wearies you,
In no ordinary way
God consoles and nourishes you,
Offering you the heavenly banquet.

Eternal Creator of all things,
Eternal Son equal to the Father,
And Spirit equal to both,
To you alone be glory.
Amen.

The Angel of the heavenly court,
Disclosing the secrets of the divine will,
Greets with fullness of grace
The Virgin, Mother of God.

The Virgin visits her kinswoman
The mother of John,
Who, enclosed in the womb, leaping,
Announces that Christ is present.

The Word, which before all ages
Proceeded from the mind of the Father,
Is born from the womb of the Virgin Mother,
A mortal Infant.

The Child is presented in the Temple
And the Lawgiver submits to the Law;
Here the Redeemer offers himself,
Redeemed at a poor man's price.

Him whom she had grieved to have lost,
His joyful Mother soon finds again,
Her Son expounding to learned minds
Things unknown to them.
Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

O Joseph, glory of the heavenly,
Sure hope of our life, and pillar of the world,
Graciously receive the praises
Which we joyfully sing to you.

The Creator of all things appointed you
The spouse of the chaste Virgin,
And willed that you be called the father of the Word
And granted you to be the minister of salvation.

You behold with joy the Redeemer lying in the manger,
Whom the chorus of prophets had foretold,
And humbly adore the newborn God.

The King of kings, Lord of the world,
At whose nod the throng of the underworld trembles,
To whom the heavens prostrate themselves in service,
Submits himself to you.

May praise be ever to the exalted Trinity,
Which, bestowing heavenly honors upon you,
Grant us through your merits the joys
Of blessed life.
Amen.

The Redeemer preferred
The womb of the blessed Virgin to high heaven,
Where the future Victim
Clothed himself in a mortal body.

This Virgin has given us
The pledge of our salvation,
Who redeemed us with his Blood
And endured the penalties and the Cross.

Let joyful hope drive far
From our breast anxious fears;
For she bears our tears
And our prayers to her Son.

The Son hearkens to the voice of the Mother
And grants her wishes;
May everyone always love her
And invoke her in times of trouble.

To the Trinity be glory,
Which enriched the untouched womb of the Mother
With the gracious seed;
May praise be throughout every age.
Amen.

O Christ, the glory of the holy Angels,
Creator and Redeemer of the human race,
Grant us graciously to ascend
The blessed dwelling places of the heavenly.

May Raphael, the Angel, physician of our salvation,
Be present from heaven, that he may heal
All who are sick and direct
The uncertain actions of our life.

May the Virgin, guide of peace and Mother of light,
And the holy chorus of Angels
Ever stand by us, together with the kingdom
Of radiant heaven.

May the blessed Deity of the Father,
Of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit
Bring this about for us, whose glory resounds
Through the whole world.
Amen.
To you, O Christ, splendor of the Father,
Life, strength of hearts,
In the sight of the Angels
With vows and voice we sing;
Alternating, with resonant sound,
We render a melody with our voices.

We praise with veneration
All the princes of heaven,
But especially the faithful
Physician and companion,
Raphael, who by his power
Binds the demon.

With him as our guardian, drive far away,
O King Christ most gracious,
All wickedness of the enemy;
With pure heart and body
Restore us to your paradise
By your mercy alone.

May we resound the glory of the Father
With melodious voices;
May we sing the glory of Christ,
The glory of the Paraclete;
Who, three and one God,
Exists before all ages. Amen.

O Christ, the glory of the holy Angels,
Ruler and Author of the human race,
Graciously grant us to ascend
To sacred heaven.

Send Raphael the Angel from the heavens
As physician of our salvation, that he may heal
All who are sick and likewise direct
Our actions.

May Mary, Mother of our God,
And the whole chorus of Angels
Ever stand by us, together with the kingdom
Of radiant heaven.

May the blessed Deity of the Father,
Of the Son, and equally of the Holy Spirit
Bring this about for us, whose glory resounds
Through the whole world.
Amen.

O Christ, the glory of the holy Angels,
Creator and Redeemer of the human race,
Grant us graciously to ascend
The blessed dwelling places of the heavenly.

May the mighty Angel Gabriel,
To drive away the ancient foes,
And, friendly to heaven,
Revisit the temples established by the Conqueror throughout the world.

May the Virgin, guide of peace and Mother of light,
And the holy chorus of Angels
Ever stand by us, together with the kingdom
Of radiant heaven.

May the blessed Deity of the Father,
Of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit
Bring this about for us, whose glory resounds
Through the whole world.
Amen.

O Christ, the glory of the holy Angels,
Creator and Redeemer of the human race,
Grant us graciously to ascend
The blessed dwelling places of the heavenly.

May Michael, the Angel of peace,
Come from heaven into our dwelling,
That, as author of serene peace,
He may consign tearful wars to the depths.

May the mighty Angel Gabriel,
To drive away the ancient foes,
And, friendly to heaven,
Revisit the temples established by the Conqueror throughout the world.

May Raphael, the Angel, physician of our salvation,
Be present from heaven, that he may heal
All who are sick and direct
The uncertain actions of our life.

May the Virgin, guide of peace and Mother of light,
And the holy chorus of Angels
Ever stand by us, together with the kingdom
Of radiant heaven.

May the blessed Deity of the Father,
Of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit
Bring this about for us, whose glory resounds
Through the whole world.
Amen.

O Christ, adorning crown of virtues,
You refresh your servants with divine light,
That they may hold to the heights of heaven
Through a course kept safe for ever.

Conrad, worshipping you in holy love
As the gracious Prince of peace,
With serene brow despises all things good
Gilded with deceit.

Enduring hardship, he stands firm
By the strength of his lofty faith,
Seeking sound salvation
In your heart alone, as in a firm stronghold.

May faith in us, growing green by his merits,
Ever stand; may hope be a pillar
In times of adversity, and the living power
Of gracious love.

Glory be to the Father, and to the begotten Son,
And to you, O Spirit, equal power of both,
God, ever one,
For all ages of time.
Amen.

Christ, having compassion on the human race,
Struck by well-deserved death, has begotten us again
To the life above, and has wiped us clean
With his Blood.

O devout stream, purging all sin!
O inexhaustible ocean of good things,
From which life and salvation flow ever
From a sevenfold source!

But who will minister these sacred waters
To the redeemed? This office is given to Mary,
That she, as steward, may direct the course
Of the divine stream.

All the gifts which the Redeemer has merited for us
Are dispensed by the Mother Mary,
At whose prayer the Son freely pours out
His gifts of his own accord.

May we venerate you through eternal years,
O Trinity, to be celebrated with the highest praise;
May minds with faith and the resounding song of the tongue
Praise you.
Amen.

You tame your body with fasts
And the bloody scourge,
That as an innocent soldier
You may follow the camp of the penitent.

May we too diligently follow
The footsteps of so good a father;
May we follow, so that the spirit
May restrain the license of the flesh.

In the stiffness of winter, you provide
A prudent garment for the poor;
You relieve the thirst and hunger of the needy
With food and drink.

O you who have refused help
To no one who asked, guard your native
Kingdom; Polish citizens and foreigners
Implore you.

May praise be to the Father, may praise be to the Son,
And to you, O Holy Spirit;
May the prayers of John obtain
For us blessed joys.
Amen.

O gracious Creator of the stars,
Eternal light of believers,
O Jesus, Redeemer of all,
Attend to the prayers of your suppliants.
You who, to expiate the common wickedness of the world,
Go forth as an untouched Victim
From the shrine of the Virgin,
To the Cross.

At the sounding of whose glorious power
And name at the first word,
Both the heavenly and the infernal
Bend the knee in trembling.
Who, lest the world perish by the deceits of the demon,
Driven by the force of love,
Have become the remedy
Of a fainting world.
We beseech you, the great Judge
Of the final day,
Defend us from our enemies
With the weapons of heavenly grace.
Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

Cruel Herod, why do you fear
The coming of the King who is God?
He does not seize earthly kingdoms,
Who gives heavenly ones.

The Magi went, following
The star they had seen going before them;
Light they seek by light;
They confess God by their gifts.

The heavenly Lamb approached
The baths of the pure stream;
The sins which he did not commit,
He took away by washing ours.

A new kind of power:
The water-jars blush red;
And the water, commanded to pour wine,
Changed its origin.

Jesus, to you be glory,
Who appeared to the nations,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

We sing of the guardian Angels of men,
Whom the heavenly Father added as companions
To frail nature, lest it succumb
To the assaults of lurking foes.

For, because the treacherous angel fell,
Justly driven from the honors granted him,
Burning with envy he strives to cast down
Those whom God calls to heaven.

Here then, watchful guardian, fly to our aid,
Warding off from the land entrusted to you
Both the sicknesses of the soul and whatever
Does not allow the inhabitants to rest.

May devout praise be ever to the Holy Trinity,
By whose unceasing power this threefold
Machine is governed, whose glory
Reigns through all ages.
Amen.

Splendor of eternity, a golden light
Has bathed this blessed day with holy fires,
Which crowns the Princes of the Apostles
And opens for the condemned a free path to the stars.

Teacher of the world and Keeper of the gate of heaven,
Parents of Rome and judges of the nations,
The one by the sword, the other by the Cross victorious in death,
Laureate, possess the senate of life.

O happy Rome, consecrated
By the glorious blood of two Princes!
Purpled by their blood, you alone
Excel the other beauties of the world.

May eternal glory be to the Trinity,
Honor, power, and jubilation,
In the unity that governs all things,
Through all the ages of ages.
Amen.

O divine charity of Jesus,
You alone accomplish great things,
You who transform virgins themselves
Into fervent apostles.

Through you the renowned Francesca shone forth,
The world despised,
And, greater than her sex, proclaimed
The glory of God throughout the world.

Blessed Mother, look graciously from heaven
Upon your daughters,
And make your work grow and flourish
In their virtues:

Go on to bend the heart of Jesus,
That he may gather all peoples together;
And obtain for us by your prayers
Emulative flames of love.

Strength, honor, praise, and glory
To God the Father with the Son
And the Holy Paraclete together
For ages of ages.
Amen.

Elizabeth the strong preferred
To subdue the impulses of the heart,
And to serve God in poverty,
Above a kingdom.

Behold, received into the radiant
Dwelling places of heaven,
And enriched with the holy joys
Of the starry house,

Now she reigns more blessedly among the heavenly,
And surpasses the stars, teaching
What the true goods of the kingdom are.

May power be to the Father, and glory to the Son,
And everlasting honor
To you, O gracious Spirit.
Amen.

While, darkness banished, the morning star
Announces the approaching day,
Venantius brings back to us
The gifts of blessed light.

For he drove away the darkness of sins
And the night of the underworld,
And imbued the citizens with the true light
Of divinity.

With the waters of sacred Baptism
He purified his homeland;
Those whom the wave baptized as soldiers
He sent as Martyrs to the stars.

Now a partaker of the Angels,
Be present to the prayers of your suppliants;
Drive far away our sins
And shed your light upon us.

May praise be to the Father, may praise be to the Son,
And to you, O Holy Spirit;
May the prayers of Venantius obtain
For us blessed joys.
Amen.

Excellent Doctor Paul, instruct our manners
And draw our hearts with you to heaven;
While faith still veiled may see the noonday,
And charity alone may reign as the sun.

May eternal glory be to the Trinity,
Honor, power, and jubilation,
In the unity that governs all things,
Through all the ages of eternity.
Amen.

From the Heart of Jesus Francesca conceives
Flames, by whose impulse
She hastens as a herald of the faith of Christ
To the uttermost shores.

Wherever she passes, sweet-scented
Lilies at once breathe forth,
And the earth, once bristling with brambles,
Shines with verdure.

Italian emigrants, scattered
Through every land,
Felt her as a mother, ever diligent
To lighten the cares of exiles.

Neither the raging anger of the seas
Nor the snowy summits,
Nor the regions torrid with heat
Delay the steadfast woman.

Strength, honor, praise, and glory
To God the Father with the Son
And the Holy Paraclete together
For ages of ages.
Amen.
Ex S. Anselmo Ep. Cantuariensi

Gracious Mother, free
From every stain of corruption,
Whom he chose who broke
The bonds of dread death.

Merciful one! Grant that those who gladly
Celebrate your festivals
May rejoice and delight
In the light of true light.

First of all, increase faith in us
By your prayers;
Strengthen minds that waver in hope,
Confirm us in charity.

Mother of God! Cause and beginning
Of our hope,
Take away wars and scourges,
Famine, plague, and the sword.

Console the groaning
Of the poor and the imprisoned;
Favor our prayers, giving to the sick
The remedy they desire.

May peace and quiet make
Our days most joyful;
Make foes into friends,
Calm the wicked.

O Mary, devout Mother,
Grant your help,
That we may reign and praise
Your Son for ever.

God the Father, God the Son,
God, gracious Spirit,
Govern us through eternal
Ages, God the Trinity.
Amen.

Go forth, daughters of Zion,
Pure virgins of the King,
Behold the Crown of Christ,
Which his Mother herself wove.

The head, bristling with torn thorns
And bloodied, shudders;
And that deathly pale face
Looks upon approaching death.

What earth, unbroken by furrows,
Stiff with briers and thorns,
Brought forth as its mournful gift?
What savage hand reaped it?

Blushing with the Blood of Christ,
The thorns exchange their points for roses,
And surpassing the palm in its fruits,
The thorn is more fitting for triumphs.

O Christ, thorns sown from the sins of mortals
Wound you;
Root out our thorns from our hearts
And plant yours in ours.

Strength, honor, praise, and glory
To God the Father with the Son,
And the Holy Paraclete together,
For ages of ages.
Amen.

Let the crossroads resound with festal voices,
Let citizens display their joy upon their faces,
Let boys and old men go forth in order
Armed with torches aflame.

While we, mindful, celebrate the Blood
Which the dying Christ poured forth on the hard wood
With many wounds, it is fitting
At least to shed tears.

A grievous destruction came upon the human race
By the sin of the old Adam;
The integrity and piety of the new Adam
Restored life to all.

If the Father on high heard the mighty cry
Of the fainting Son from heaven,
He should have been appeased rather by blood
And given us pardon.

Whoever washes his robe in this blood
Wipes away his stains; and takes on the rosy beauty
By which he straightway becomes like the Angels
And pleases the King.

Let no one thereafter
Draw himself back from the straight path,
But let the final mark be reached;
He will bestow a noble reward,
God who helps the course.

Be propitious to us, O powerful Father,
That those whom you have purchased
With the blood of your only-begotten Son,
And refresh with the gentle Breath,
You may transfer to the heights of heaven.
Amen.

Glory of the Polish nation,
Noble splendor of the clergy,
Ornament of the Lyceum and of his homeland,
O renowned John.

You teach the law of the divine will
As a master, and you practise it.
Knowledge profits nothing; let us strive diligently
To carry out the law.

As a traveler, you visit on foot
The shrines of the Apostles;
To the homeland toward which we are making our way,
Direct our steps and our path.

You seek the city of Jerusalem;
You venerate with reverence the footsteps
Sealed with the Blood of Christ
And water them with the tears you shed.

The bitter wounds of Christ,
Stay fixed in our hearts,
That we may keep in mind to attain
The price of redemption.

May the prostrate fabric of the world,
O merciful Trinity, adore you;
And through grace may we as new beings
Sing a new song.
Amen.

Let us all celebrate the glory
Of the holy Shroud; let us recall with joyful hymns
And devout prayers the sure monuments
Of our salvation.

What the venerable Shroud ever recalls,
Adorned with signs impressed in blood,
Is how it held the body of Jesus
Wrapped, taken down from the high Cross.

This recalls to mind the cruel sufferings
Which Christ, the Redeemer of the human race,
Endured out of pity for Adam's fall,
Death being overcome.

The image shows the side wounded by the lance,
The palms and feet with nails,
The limbs torn by scourges,
And the crown fixed upon the head.

Who that is devout could behold with dry eyes
And without a groan from his inmost heart
The inscribed marks and the living likenesses
Of an undeserved death?

Since your sin alone, O Christ, was
The cause to you of so many evils,
Our life is owed to you; we surrender
Our very life.

To you, O Son, be honor and power,
Who redeem the world with your blood,
And who reign with the supreme Father
And the gracious Spirit. Amen.

This is the day on which the spirit
Of Therese, like a white dove,
Transferred herself to the sacred temples
Of the heavenly.

And she heard the voice of her Spouse:
Come, sister, from the summit
Of Carmel to the wedding feast of the Lamb;
Come to the crown of glory.

To you, O Spouse Jesus, King of Virgins,
May the blessed orders adore,
And in the nuptial song
May they praise you through every age.
Amen.

Now, victorious, death submerged,
Christ returns from the underworld,
And, the bonds of sin broken,
Opens the threshold of heaven.

Having been seen sufficiently by mortals
He ascends to the heavenly realm
And sits at the right hand of the Father
As sharer in the Father's glory.

Him whom he had promised to his own,
To give the Holy Spirit,
With tongues of fire of love
He fills his sorrowing disciples.

Freed from the weight of the flesh,
The Virgin is taken up to the stars,
Received with the jubilation of heaven
And the songs of the Angels.

Twelve stars encircle
The head of the gracious Mother;
Close to the throne of her Son
She holds sway over all creatures.
Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

Let sudden evening now descend over the whole sky
And the sun plunge the dazed day into darkness,
While I recall the mockery of a savage death
And the divine catastrophe.

You were present as a witness to his punishment, O Mother,
Drenched in sorrows, bearing an adamantine heart;
While your Son, hanging on the funereal Cross,
Gave forth deep groans.

Your Son hanging before your eyes, your Son torn
By cruel scourgings, your Son pierced
By gaping wounds — how many piercing thorns
Fixed themselves in you!

Alas! Spittle, blows, scourgings, wounds,
Nails, gall, aloe, sponge, lance,
Thirst, thorns, blood — with how many varied
Tyrannicies did they press upon your devout heart!

Meanwhile you, O Virgin, stand more nobly than all
The Martyrs; by a new wonder,
You, dying amid such great sufferings, do not die,
O Mother fixed fast in dreadful agonies.

May glory, praise, and honor be to the supreme Trinity,
From which with humble supplication and anxious prayer
I ask for strength rivaling
The power of virginal fortitude in trials.
Amen.

O Jesus, crown of Martyrs,
Who after bloody battles
Have called holy Emygdius
To everlasting rewards:

With the purple of his chaste blood
And a noble palm of rejoicing,
Among the choirs of the heavenly
You fill him with blessed light:

Now arouse us who are drowsy
To his victories;
Free those submerged in sleep
To the proclamation of virtue.

As when invoked he restored
Health to languishing limbs,
So may he purify the secrets of the mind
Altogether from the stain of sins.

As by his wondrous deeds
He overthrew the altars of the gods,
So may he ward off the present harms
That threaten us.

As he once by his voice drove out
The wicked worship of demons,
So may he obtain for those who pray
The eternal joys of heaven.

Grant what is asked, O great King
Jesus, King of Martyrs,
Who reign with the Father and the gracious Spirit
Through every age.
Amen.

Jesus, my sweet love,
As if you were present, I draw near;
I embrace you with affection,
Mindful of your Wounds.

O how bare I behold you here,
Wounded, and stretched out,
Defiled, wrapped
In this sacred covering!

Hail, Head crowned with thorns,
Whose sweet face
Has changed its bloom,
Before which the court of heaven trembles.

Hail, Side of the Savior,
Hail, gentle opening,
More red than the rose,
A health-bearing remedy.

Holy hands, I greet you,
Pierced by cruel Nails.
Do not repel me, O Savior,
From your holy Feet.
Amen.

O Jesus, Redeemer of all,
Whom before the origin of light
The supreme Father brought forth
Equal to the Father's glory.

You are the light and splendor of the Father,
You the everlasting hope of all;
Attend to the prayers
Which your little servants pour forth throughout the world.

Remember, O Creator of all things,
That once, of our body,
Born from the sacred womb of the Virgin,
You took on our form.

This present day bears witness,
As it runs through the circle of the year,
That you alone came from the bosom of the Father
As the salvation of the world.

This the stars, the earth, the seas,
This all that is under heaven,
Salute as the Author of new salvation
With a new song.

And we, whom the blessed wave
Of sacred blood has washed,
On account of your birthday
Offer the tribute of our hymn.

Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

You command the rock, and water suddenly rises,
Latent, flowing in a wholesome
Spring of Baptism, and you purify your people
With the sacred stream.

Drive away the hard flints of the breast;
Break the stony hardness of the swollen heart,
That the cleansing water, flowing with tears,
May wash away our defilements.

You do not fear the rage of the savage tyrant,
With blood shed, O noble Martyr;
Nay, with your head cut off, as one dead
You carry it to the very altar.

Now as a conqueror reigning above the stars,
Show us the path and way of entry;
Lead your suppliants, born for the heavenly,
To the seats above.

May the Father in heaven grant assent, and the Son,
May the Spirit, equal power of both, grant assent
To our prayers, God, one for all
Ages of time.
Amen.

The Redeemer, praying on the mount
Planted with olive trees, fell prostrate;
He grieves, is afraid, is exhausted,
Overflowing with a sweat of blood.

Betrayed by a traitor,
God is dragged away to punishment;
Bound in harsh chains,
He is beaten with bloody scourges.

A crown of shame, woven
With sharp thorns,
Clothing him in a filthy purple,
Crowns the King of glory.

Sweating, panting, falling,
He is compelled by force
To carry the three-times-heavy Cross
To the summit of the mountain.

Nailed to the dark stake,
Innocent among criminals,
Praying for his torturers,
Bleeding, he breathes forth his spirit.
Jesus, to you be glory,
Who were born of the Virgin,
With the Father and the gracious Spirit,
For everlasting ages.
Amen.

In the deep shadow of night
And in heavy darkness
A pure flame surveys the dwelling,
So commanding the divine will.

In the night John is born,
The stars descend from heaven;
In the night John is submerged,
The stars attend the funeral.

Hence his heart, burning with fire,
Strong charity inflames;
Hence from his mouth flowing
A wondrous sweetness proceeds.

Now he draws the hearts of the good
With love toward salvation;
Now he draws back the hearts of the wicked
With fear from hell.

He comforts the poor with money,
He aids the forsaken;
He does not allow the just to be cast down,
He prevents harm to their reputation.

Through the holiness of John,
O blessed Trinity,
Grant purity to our minds,
Let charity reign in the heart.
Amen.

The unconquered champion of God,
About to be plunged into the river's wave,
Stands firm in silence,
While the seal is mentioned.

Here the king threatens death,
Here the torturer inflicts wounds;
His hands are bound with ropes,
His limbs burned with fire.

But John despises these things
And has no regard for the king's anger;
He will not reveal the secret,
He shudders to break the seal.

He stands mute as an innocent lamb,
Uttering nothing about what is to be concealed;
He stands; and when the king elicits nothing,
He justly casts him from the bridge.

He is thrown headlong from on high,
Plunged into the deep waves;
But the waves salute him as he is submerged
With attending flames.

Stars swim in the river,
