If, then, we look carefully at what the holy Evangelist himself says in his opening: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word: the solution of this question hangs on that. For what is the teaching of the Father, if not the Word of the Father? Christ himself, therefore, is the teaching of the Father, since he is the Word of the Father. But because the Word cannot belong to no one, but must belong to someone: he both called himself the teaching, and called it not his own, because he is the Word of the Father. For what is so much yours as yourself? And yet what is so little yours as yourself, if what you are belongs to another?

If, then, we perform righteous works, by which we spread the fragrance of a good name through the Church, what are we doing but pouring ointment upon the body of the Lord? But the woman stood behind the feet of Jesus: for we stood against the steps of the Lord when, placed in our sins, we resisted his ways. But if after our sins we turn to true repentance, we now stand behind him at his feet; because we follow the footsteps of him whom we were fighting. The woman bathes his feet with tears: which we too truly do, if we bow down in compassionate love toward even the lowest members of the Lord, if we suffer with his saints in tribulation, if we count their sorrow as our own.

If you cannot walk the lofty path of virginity, follow at least God along the very safe way of humility; from whose rightness if any, even among virgins, shall have strayed, they do not, if I am to speak the truth, follow the Lamb whithersoever he goes. The unclean man who is humble follows the Lamb; the virgin who is proud also follows him, but neither follows him whithersoever he goes: for neither can the one ascend to the purity of the Lamb, who is without blemish; nor does the other deign to descend to the same meekness, by which he was silent before his shearer, indeed before his slayer. Yet the sinner has chosen the more wholesome part of following in humility than the proud man in virginity; for the humility of the one's repentance cleanses even his impurity, while the pride of the other defiles his chastity.

Thus through one man sin entered into the world, and through sin, death: and so death passed unto all men, in whom all have sinned. For by the word "world" in that place the Apostle meant the entire human race. So the matter stood thus: the whole damned mass of the human race lay in evils, or rather was rolling in them, and was being hurled from evil to evil; and, joined to the part of those angels who had sinned, it was paying the most fitting penalty for its impious desertion.

Just as Joseph, sold by his brothers, prefigured the betrayal of our Redeemer: so Enoch, who was translated, and Elijah, who was lifted up to the aerial heaven, both together signified the Lord's Ascension. The Lord therefore had forerunners and witnesses of his Ascension, one before the Law, another under the Law: so that one day he himself might come who could in truth penetrate the heavens. And the very order of these events is distinguished in their respective elevations by certain degrees of increase. For Enoch is said to have been translated, while Elijah is recorded as having been carried up to heaven: that there might come afterward one who, neither translated nor carried up, should penetrate the ethereal heaven by his own power.

Therefore, just as the Resurrection of the Lord at the Paschal solemnity was for us the cause of rejoicing: so his Ascension into the heavens is the source of our present joys, as we recall that day and worthily venerate it, on which our lowly human nature was, in Christ, raised above all the host of heaven, above all the orders of Angels, and beyond the height of all powers, to the throne of God the Father. By this ordering of divine works we are grounded and built up: so that the grace of God would shine more wonderfully, when faith did not fail, hope did not waver, and charity did not grow cold, even after those things had been removed from the sight of men which, by their very presence, had rightly inspired reverence.

Just as it is the duty of the whole body to live devoutly, so it is the duty of the whole of life to bear the Cross: which each one is rightly urged to carry, because it is borne by each according to his own manner and measure. The name of persecution is one, but the cause of the struggle is not one: and often there is more danger in a hidden foe than in an open enemy. Blessed Job, schooled by the alternation of good and evil in this world, spoke with piety and truth: Is not the life of man upon earth a trial? For the faithful soul is assailed not only by bodily pains and torments, but also, while its members remain unharmed, is oppressed by a grievous sickness if it is softened by carnal pleasure. But when the flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh, the rational mind is armed by the protection of the Cross of Christ, and does not consent to the enticement of harmful desires, since it is transfixed with the key of continence and the fear of God.

As he says: As the living Father has sent me, and I live because of the Father: so he who eats me will also live because of me. As if he were saying: That I live because of the Father—that is, that I refer my life to him as to one greater—was brought about by my self-emptying, in which he sent me: but that anyone should live because of me is brought about by participation, through which he eats me. I therefore, humbled, live because of the Father: that one, raised up, lives because of me. But if he said, I live because of the Father, because he is from him, and not the Father from him; this was said without any loss of equality. Nor, however, by saying, And he who eats me will also live because of me, did he signify that his equality and ours are the same, but he showed the grace of the mediator.

Let there be, therefore, some who admonish the mind, who, however sluggish the man may be through weakness of the outer body, may raise his soul to higher things. With their assistance, let him easily both raise himself up and prostrate himself before Jesus, and be found worthy to be seen by the Lord's gaze. For the Lord looks upon humility: because he looked upon the humility of his handmaiden. When he saw their faith, he said: Man, your sins are forgiven you. Great is the Lord, who forgives some by the merits of others: and while he tests some, he releases others from their faults. Why, O man, should a companion not avail before you, when a servant before God has both the merit of interceding and the right of obtaining?

Whether, therefore, in the Law, or in the Prophets, or in the Gospel, the number forty is commended to us in fasting. Now fasting, in its great and universal sense, is to abstain from iniquities and from the illicit pleasures of the world—which is the perfect fast: That denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly and justly and piously in this present age. What reward does the Apostle add to this fast? He continues and says: Awaiting that blessed hope and the manifestation of the glory of our blessed God and Savior Jesus Christ. In this present age, then, we celebrate as it were a Lenten fast of abstinence when we live rightly, when we abstain from iniquities and from illicit pleasures: but because this abstinence will not be without its reward, we await that blessed hope and the revelation of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ. In that hope, when hope shall have given way to reality, we shall receive as our reward the denarius. For this reward is given to the workers in the vineyard, according to the Gospel, which I believe you remember: for not everything need be recalled as to those who are rude and unlearned. The denarius, which takes its name from the number ten, is paid, and joined to forty makes fifty: hence we celebrate with toil the Lent before Easter; but with joy, as having received our reward, the fifty days after Easter.

And others, tempting him, sought from him a sign from heaven: they desired either, after the manner of Elijah, for fire to come down from on high, or, like Samuel, for thunder to rumble, lightning to flash, and rain to fall in summertime—as if they could not have maligned those too, and said that they happened from hidden and varied disturbances of the air. But you, who malign what you see with your eyes, hold in your hands, and perceive by their usefulness—what would you do with things that came from heaven? You would no doubt answer that in Egypt the magicians performed many signs from heaven as well.

Therefore the order of the mystery is observed everywhere, so that medicine is first granted to wounds through the forgiveness of sins, and afterward the nourishment of the heavenly table abounds; although this multitude is not yet refreshed with stronger food, nor are hearts fasting from solid faith nourished with the Body and Blood of Christ. I gave you milk to drink, he says, not solid food; for you were not yet able, nor indeed are you yet. In the manner of milk are the five loaves; the more solid food is Christ himself; the more potent drink is the Blood of the Lord.

And so the most blessed Apostles, and all the disciples, who had been trembling at the manner of the Cross and uncertain in their faith in the Resurrection, were so strengthened by the clear truth that, as the Lord went up to the heights of heaven, they were not only afflicted with no sorrow, but were even filled with great joy. And indeed great and ineffable was the cause of rejoicing, when in the sight of the holy multitude the nature of the human race ascended above the dignity of all heavenly creatures, destined to surpass the orders of Angels and to be exalted beyond the heights of the Archangels; nor was it to find any limit in any heights of its advancement, unless, received into the seat of the eternal Father, it were made a sharer in the glory of him to whose nature it was united in the Son.

Hence it is well said by Paul: For creation has been subjected to vanity, not willingly, but on account of him who subjected it, in hope; because creation itself also will be liberated from the servitude of corruption, into the freedom of the glory of the children of God. For creation is subjected to vanity unwillingly: because man, who of his own will forsook the state of his inborn constancy, pressed down by the just weight of mortality, unwillingly serves the corruption of his own mutability. But this creation is then rescued from the servitude of corruption when, rising incorrupt, it is raised up to the glory of the children of God.

Hence you have well, according to Matthew, that he also set a hedge around it: that is, he fenced it about with the protection of divine safeguarding, lest it lie easily open to the incursions of spiritual beasts. And he dug a winepress in it. How do we understand what a winepress is, unless perhaps because the Psalms are inscribed for the winepresses; in that in them the mysteries of the Lord's Passion have overflowed more abundantly, after the manner of must fervent with the Holy Spirit? Hence also those were thought to be drunk upon whom the Holy Spirit poured forth. Therefore here too he dug a winepress, into which the inner fruit of the rational vine might flow down by spiritual infusion.

Hence comes that voice of hers, caught amid the waves and storms of rushing temptations, and seeking the help of his protection with a groaning cry: Why, O Lord, have you withdrawn far off, and looked away in times of opportunity, in tribulation? She likewise expounds the voice of the pursuing enemy in what follows in the Psalm, adding: For he has said in his heart: God has forgotten; he has turned away his face, so as not to see to the end.

And so even the blessed Apostles themselves, who had been confirmed by so many miracles, instructed by so many discourses, yet had trembled at the cruelty of the Lord's Passion and had not accepted the truth of his Resurrection without hesitation, so greatly profited from the Lord's Ascension that whatever had previously brought them fear was turned into joy. For they had directed the whole contemplation of their minds to the divinity of him sitting at the right hand of the Father: and they were no longer delayed by the obstacle of bodily sight from fixing the gaze of the mind upon that which had neither been absent from the Father by descending, nor departed from the disciples by ascending. Then, therefore, beloved, the Son of Man, the Son of God, became known more excellently and more sacredly when he withdrew into the glory of the paternal majesty: and in an ineffable manner he began to be more present in divinity, who had become more distant in humanity.

Therefore, beloved brethren, it is right that we should follow there in heart, where we believe him to have ascended in body. Let us flee earthly desires; let nothing in the depths any longer delight us, we who have the Father in heaven. And this must be carefully weighed by us: that he who ascended in peace will return in terror; and whatever he commanded us with gentleness, this he will exact from us with exactness. Let no one, therefore, make light of the times of penance granted him, let no one neglect to take care of himself while he is able: for our Redeemer will come then to judgment all the more strict, the more he extended great patience to us before the judgment.

Therefore, the very greatness of the gift bestowed demands from us a reverence worthy of its splendor. For this reason, as the blessed Apostle teaches, we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit which is of God, that we may know the things that are given to us by God; which Spirit is honored piously only if what he himself bestows is offered back to him. What then in the treasury of the Lord's generosity can we find so fitting to honor the present feast as peace, which at the birth of the Lord was first proclaimed by the angelic chorus? For it is peace that begets sons of God, the nurse of love and mother of unity, the rest of the blessed and the dwelling of eternity; whose proper work and special benefit it is to join to God those whom it separates from the world.

And so we too, born into the toil of this pilgrimage, have come here already wearied with distaste, not knowing what we ought to desire. And the more our sickness of distaste increases, the more the mind draws away from tasting that sweetness; and the soul no longer craves inner delights, because it has long grown wholly unaccustomed to eating them. Thus we pine away in our distaste and grow faint with the long plague of starvation. And because we are unwilling inwardly to taste the sweetness prepared for us, we wretches cherish our own hunger in the world outside.

Whoever holds about Christ what ought not to be held about the Only-Begotten Son of God does not ask in his name, even though he does not keep silent about the name of Christ in letters and syllables: because he asks in the name of that one whom he conceives in his mind when he asks. But he who holds about him what ought to be held does ask in his name: and he receives what he asks for, if he does not ask for something contrary to his eternal salvation. He receives it, however, when it is fitting for him to receive it. For some things are not denied, but are deferred so as to be given at the fitting time. Thus it must be understood what he says, He will give to you: so that by these words those benefits are known to be signified which properly belong to those who ask. For all the Saints are heard for themselves, but they are not heard for all their friends, enemies, and any others: because it is not said carelessly, He will give, but, He will give to you.

In a single moment of time, that people, taught the worship of God through the greatest wonders, fell most shamefully back into Egyptian idolatry. From which, if you compare both together, it is possible to see that fasting leads to God, while indulgence destroys salvation. What defiled Esau and made him a servant to his brother? Was it not a single meal, for which he sold his birthright? Was not Samuel obtained for his mother by prayer through fasting? What made the most valiant Samson invincible? Was it not fasting, with which he was conceived in his mother's womb? Fasting conceived him, fasting nourished him, fasting made him a man. This is what the Angel commanded his mother, warning her to touch nothing that comes from the vine, and to drink neither wine nor strong drink. Fasting brought forth the prophets, and strengthens and fortifies the mighty.

But one of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them: You know nothing, nor do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish. Now this he said not of himself: but since he was high priest that year, he prophesied. By this we are taught that even wicked men foretell the future by the spirit of prophecy: which, however, the Evangelist attributes to a divine mystery, because he was a pontiff, that is, the chief priest.

Until now, he says, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you shall receive, that your joy may be full. This joy that he calls full is assuredly not carnal but spiritual: and when it is such that nothing can be added to it, it will beyond all doubt be full. Whatever is asked, therefore, that pertains to the attaining of this joy, this is what is to be asked in the name of Christ, if we understand the divine grace, if we seek truly blessed life. Whatever else is asked for, nothing is asked: not because it is nothing at all, but because in comparison with so great a thing, whatever else is desired is nothing.

Now, in order that the faithful people might recall the institution of so great a Sacrament through the full celebration of the feast, the Roman Pontiff Urban IV, moved by devotion to this Sacrament, piously decreed that the memory of the aforesaid institution should be celebrated by all the faithful on the first Thursday after the Octave of Pentecost; so that those who make use of this Sacrament throughout the course of the whole year for their salvation might especially recall its institution at that time when the Holy Spirit taught the hearts of the disciples to know fully the mysteries of this Sacrament. For it was also in that same season that this Sacrament began to be frequented by the faithful.

Now, in order that the memory of its saving institution might be observed more worthily on the aforesaid Thursday and through the following Octave, and that the solemnity of it might be celebrated more honorably: in place of the material distributions that are bestowed in cathedral churches upon those present at the Canonical Hours, both nocturnal and daytime, the aforesaid Roman Pontiff granted to those who personally attend these Hours in churches during this solemnity spiritual stipends by apostolic largess; so that by these means the faithful might come together more eagerly and abundantly to the celebration of so great a feast.

Therefore, in order that through Melchizedek the priest this might be fittingly celebrated in Genesis, the image of the sacrifice is placed beforehand, consisting, namely, of bread and wine. This the Lord, fulfilling and completing, offered bread and the chalice mixed with wine; and he who is the fullness fulfilled in truth what had been prefigured by the image. And also through Solomon the Holy Spirit forewarns of the type of the Lord's sacrifice—making mention of the immolated victim, the bread and wine, the altar, and the Apostles: Wisdom, he says, has built herself a house, and has set up seven columns; she has slaughtered her victims, she has mixed wine in the bowl, and she has prepared her table. And she has sent forth her servants, calling with a lofty proclamation to the bowl, saying: Whoever is unwise, let him come to me. And to those lacking in sense she said: Come, eat of my breads, and drink the wine that I have mixed for you.

That you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. If one becomes a child of God by keeping God's commandments, then he is not a son by nature, but by his own choice. When therefore you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may be honored by men. Whoever sounds a trumpet when giving alms is a hypocrite. Whoever, when fasting, disfigures his face to show the emptiness of his belly in his countenance—this man too is a hypocrite. Whoever prays in the synagogues and on the corners of the streets to be seen by men is a hypocrite.

Would that those who now exercise us might be converted and be exercised together with us: yet as long as they are such that they exercise us, let us not hate them; because in the fact that one of them is wicked, we do not know whether he will persevere so to the end. And often when you think you hate an enemy, you hate a brother and do not know it. The devil and his angels have been made known to us in the holy Scriptures as destined for eternal fire. It is only their correction that is to be despaired of, those against whom we have a hidden struggle: for which struggle the Apostle arms us, saying: Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood: that is, not against the men you see, but against principalities and powers, and rulers of the world, of these darknesses. Lest perhaps when he said, of the world, you should understand that the demons are rulers of heaven and earth. He said, of the world, of these darknesses: he said, of the world, meaning the lovers of the world: he said, of the world, meaning the impious and the wicked: he said, of the world, of which the Gospel says: And the world did not know him.

He came before the law, because through natural understanding each person, by the example of himself, made known how he ought to act toward his neighbor. He came in the law, because by commanding he taught. He came after the law through grace, because by displaying the presence of his loving kindness he showed it forth. Yet he complains of not finding fruit in three years: for the minds of certain wicked persons are corrected neither by the natural law breathed into them, nor by precepts, nor turned by the miracles of his Incarnation. What is expressed by the vine-dresser, but the order of prelates? For those who preside over the Church thereby exercise care over the Lord's vineyard.

The Lord came: what did he do? He commended a great mystery. He spat upon the ground, and from his saliva he made clay: because the Word was made flesh, and anointed the eyes of the blind man. He was anointed, but did not yet see. He sent him to the pool that is called Siloam. Now it was important for the Evangelist to preserve for us the name of this pool, and he says: which is interpreted, Sent. You already know who is the Sent One. For if that One had not been sent, none of us would have been freed from iniquity. He therefore washed his eyes in that pool which is interpreted, Sent; he was baptized in Christ. If therefore when he baptized him in himself in some manner he then gave him light: when he anointed him, he perhaps made him a catechumen.

David therefore came and found the people of the Jews fighting against the devil; and since there was no one who dared approach to single combat, he who bore the figure of Christ came forward to battle, and took a staff in his hand and went out against Goliath. And in that, what was then prefigured was fulfilled in the Lord Jesus Christ. For the true David, Christ, came and carried his own cross to fight against the spiritual Goliath, that is, the devil. See, brethren, where David struck Goliath: on the forehead, surely, where he bore no sign of the cross. For just as the staff was a type of the cross, so also that stone by which he was struck prefigured Christ the Lord.

A truthful meaning can in no way rightly be called a lie: as in deed, so also in word. For when his father said to him: Who are you, my son? he replied: I am Esau, your firstborn. If this is referred to those two twins, it will seem a lie: but if it is referred to that which is signified by these deeds and words written down, then he is to be understood here in his own body, which is his Church, of whom, speaking on this matter, he says: When you will see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the Prophets in the Kingdom of God, but yourselves cast out. And: They will come from the East and the West, and from the North and the South, and will recline in the Kingdom of God. And: Behold, there are those last who were first, and there are those first who were last. For in some manner the younger brother thus took the primacy of the elder and transferred to himself the rights of his brother.

He engaged in conversation with them, reproved the hardness of their understanding, opened to them the mysteries of sacred Scripture that concerned himself: and yet, because he was still a stranger to their hearts in faith, he made as though to go farther. Now, to feign is to fashion, to shape: hence we call shapers of clay, potters. Therefore simple Truth did nothing by way of duplicity: but showed himself to them in body such as he was in their minds. But it was necessary to test whether those who had not yet loved him as God might at least have been able to love him as a stranger.

Now, in order to establish and perfect the cult of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, and to spread it throughout the whole world, God himself chose as his instrument a most humble virgin of the Order of the Visitation, Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque, who, from her earliest years already burning with love for the Sacrament of the Eucharist, was often visited by Christ the Lord appearing to her; and he deigned to make known to her the riches and desires of his divine Heart. Of these apparitions the most celebrated is that in which Jesus showed himself to her as she prayed before the Eucharist, displayed his most Sacred Heart, and complained that, for all his immense charity, he received nothing but the insults of ungrateful men, and bade her take care to establish a new feast on the Friday after the Octave of Corpus Christi, so that his Heart might be honored with fitting veneration, and the offenses inflicted upon him in the Sacrament of love by sinners might be expiated by worthy acts of reparation. How many and how great were the difficulties that God's servant experienced in carrying out the commands of Christ, there is no one who does not know; but confirmed by the Lord himself and strenuously aided by the spiritual directors of her soul, who labored with incredible ardor in promoting this devotion, she did not cease to fulfill faithfully unto death the ministry entrusted to her from heaven.

But he does not forget the prayer of the poor, nor does he turn his face away from those who hope in him: rather, he both helps those who struggle with enemies that they may conquer, and crowns the victors for eternity. Hence it is also plainly said here that he saw them laboring in their rowing. For the Lord sees those who labor on the sea, even though he himself stands on land: because even if he may seem for a time to delay granting help to those in tribulation, he nonetheless strengthens them by the regard of his loving kindness, lest they fail in their tribulations; and sometimes he even delivers them by manifest assistance, with adversities overcome, as though the rolling waves were trodden down and stilled.

But because they did not understand, he consequently exercised upon them the strictness of deserved punishment: and he drove out the trade in human goods from that house, in which it had been commanded that only divine things should be transacted, that victims and prayers should be offered to God, that the word of God should be read, heard, and sung. And indeed it is to be believed that he found sold or bought in the temple only what was necessary for the ministry of that same temple, in view of what we read done on another occasion, when entering the same temple he found in it those selling and buying sheep, oxen, and doves: for without doubt all these things were bought by those who came from afar from the native inhabitants only so that they might be offered in the house of the Lord.

For they saw themselves bound by a great crime of impiety, in that they had slain him whom they ought to have venerated and adored: and they thought this was inexpiable. For it was a great offense, the consideration of which would cause them to despair: but they ought not to have despaired, those on whose behalf the Lord hanging on the cross deigned to pray. For he had said: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do. He saw some of his own among many strangers: for those very ones he was already seeking pardon, from whom he was still receiving injury. For he did not attend to the fact that he was dying by their hands, but that he was dying for them.

See now also three degrees of guilt: of judgment, of council, and of the fire of Gehenna. For in judgment, room is still given for defense. In council, however, although judgment is also usually rendered there, yet because the distinction itself compels acknowledgment that there is some difference here, the pronouncing of sentence seems to pertain to council; when the matter is no longer argued with the accused himself as to whether he is to be condemned, but those who judge deliberate among themselves as to what punishment the one established as condemned is to receive. The fire of Gehenna, however, has neither the uncertain condemnation of judgment, nor the punishment of the condemned as in council: for in the fire of Gehenna, the condemnation is certain, and the punishment of the condemned.

Consider the valor of Judas Maccabeus's commander from one of his soldiers. For Eleazar, when he noticed an elephant towering above the others and clothed in royal armor, thinking that the king was upon it, rushed at speed into the midst of the legion; and, casting aside his shield, he struck with both hands until he reached the beast, and went under it, and thrust his sword underneath and killed it. And so the beast, falling, crushed Eleazar, and so he died. What greatness of soul! First, not to fear death; then, surrounded by the enemy's legions, to hurl himself into the close-packed foe, pierce through the middle of the column, and, fiercer in his contempt of death, casting aside his shield, with both hands to take and sustain the mass of the wounded beast; afterward to go under it in order to strike with a fuller blow; enclosed rather than crushed beneath its fall, he was buried by his own triumph.

Do you wish to know that you perished by sinning against a fellow man? If he against whom you have sinned should correct you between himself and you alone, and you have heard him, he has gained you. What is, he has gained you, if not that you had perished, if he had not gained you? For if you had not perished, how has he gained you? Let no one, therefore, make light of sinning against a brother. For the Apostle says in one place: But thus sinning against the brethren and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ: therefore because we have all been made members of Christ. How do you not sin against Christ, when you sin against a member of Christ?

For by the voice of our Redeemer it is said: Every kingdom divided against itself shall be laid waste. It is clear, therefore, that Judea had come to the end of its kingdom, which lay divided under so many kings. It is also aptly shown not only by what kings but also by what priests this was brought about: and because John the Baptist proclaimed him who would be at once King and Priest, Luke the Evangelist marked the time of his preaching through the mention of kingdom and priesthood.
Zach 1:4-5

4 Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried out, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn from your evil ways and from your wicked thoughts. But they did not heed, and neither did they pay attention to me, says the Lord.
5 Your fathers, where are they? And will the prophets live unceasingly?
Zach 1:6

6 Yet truly my words and my lawfulness, which I entrusted to my servants the prophets, were indeed comprehended by your fathers, and so they were converted, and they said: Just as the Lord of hosts decided to do to us, according to our ways and according to our inventions, so has he done to us.
Before the face of the fury of your wrath, O God, all the earth is troubled:
But have mercy, O Lord, and do not bring it to utter ruin.
O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name!
Hide your almsgiving in the bosom of the poor, and it will pray for you to the Lord:
For as water extinguishes fire, so almsgiving extinguishes sin.
Give alms, and behold, all things are clean for you.
Jesus took the chalice, after he had supped, saying: This chalice is the new covenant in my blood:
Do this in remembrance of me.
I will be mindful and remember, and my soul shall languish within me.
To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul:
O my God, in you I trust, let me not be put to shame.
Guard my soul, and deliver me.
May the Lord open your heart in his law and in his commandments, and grant you peace in your days:
May he grant you salvation, and redeem you from evils.
May the Lord hear your prayers, and be reconciled to you, and not forsake you in time of trouble.
I, the Lord, led you through the desert for forty years, and your garments were not worn out:
I rained manna from heaven upon you, and you forgot me, says the Lord.
I brought you out of the land of Egypt, and freed you from the house of slavery.
You are my helper and my support, O Lord, and in your word I have hoped:
Depart from me, you evildoers: and I will search out the commandments of my God.
I have hated the wicked: and I have loved your law.
Be my helper, O God:
Do not forsake me.
My helper, to you will I sing, for you, O God, are my protector:
O God, my mercy.
I will be glad and exult in you, I will sing to your name, O Most High.
Adonai, Lord, great and wonderful God, who gave salvation into the hand of a woman,
Hear the prayers of your servants.
Blessed are you, O Lord, who do not forsake those who trust in you, and humble those who glory in their own strength.
Divine fire came, not burning but illumining, not consuming but shining: and it found the hearts of the disciples to be pure vessels:
And bestowed upon them the gifts of charisms, alleluia, alleluia.
It found them united in charity, and the flooding grace of the Godhead enlightened them.
Strangers shall pass through Jerusalem no more:
For on that day the mountains shall drip sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey, says the Lord.
God shall come from Lebanon, and the Holy One from the shady and dense mountain.
My friend betrayed me with the sign of a kiss: He whom I shall kiss, that is he, hold him: this evil sign did he make, who by a kiss accomplished murder.
The unhappy man cast away the price of blood, and in the end hanged himself with a noose.
It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.
Anguish is upon me on every side, and I know not what to choose;
It is better for me to fall into the hands of men, than to forsake the law of my God.
For if I do this, death awaits me; but if I do not do it, I shall not escape your hands.
You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you shall trample underfoot the lion and the dragon.
The Angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and coming near rolled back the stone and sat upon it, and said to the women:
Do not be afraid: for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified: he has risen: come, and see the place where the Lord was laid, alleluia.
And entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were amazed: and he said to them.

The Angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and coming near rolled back the stone and sat upon it, and said to the women: * Do not be afraid: for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified: he has risen: come, and see the place where the Lord was laid, alleluia.
The Angel of the Lord spoke to the women, saying: Whom do you seek? Do you seek Jesus? He has risen:
Come, and see, alleluia, alleluia.
You seek Jesus of Nazareth who was crucified? He is risen, he is not here.
The Angel of the Lord called to Abraham, saying:
Do not stretch out your hand against the boy, because you fear the Lord.
And when he had stretched out his hand to sacrifice his son, behold the Angel of the Lord cried out from heaven, saying.

My beloved soul I delivered into the hands of the wicked, and my inheritance became to me as a lion in the forest: the adversary raised his voice against me, saying: Gather together, and hasten to devour him: they placed me in the desert of solitude, and all the earth mourned over me:
Because there was none found who would acknowledge me, and do good.
Men without mercy rose up against me, and they did not spare my soul.

My beloved soul I delivered into the hands of the wicked, and my inheritance became to me as a lion in the forest: the adversary raised his voice against me, saying: Gather together, and hasten to devour him: they placed me in the desert of solitude, and all the earth mourned over me: * Because there was none found who would acknowledge me, and do good.
Long before, Ezekiel prophesied: I saw a closed gate; behold, God came forth from it before the ages for the salvation of the world:
And it was closed again, signifying the Virgin, because after childbirth she remained a virgin.
The gate that you saw, the Lord alone shall pass through it.

Before I eat, I sigh, and my groaning is like overflowing waters; because the fear that I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has befallen me. Did I not dissemble? did I not keep silence? did I not take rest?
And indignation came upon me.
Behold, there is no help within me, and my kinsmen also have withdrawn from me.
Open your eyes, O Lord, and behold our affliction: the nations have surrounded us to punish us:
But you, O Lord, stretch out your arm, and deliver our souls.
Afflict those who oppress us and make insult in their pride; and guard your own portion.
God appeared to Jacob, and blessed him, and said: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the stone, and made a vow to me:
I will cause you to grow, and will multiply you.
Truly the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it.
There appeared to the Apostles divided tongues as of fire, alleluia:
And the Holy Spirit sat upon each of them, alleluia, alleluia.
And they began to speak in various tongues, as the Holy Spirit gave them utterance.
Christ ascending on high led captivity captive,
He gave gifts to men, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
God ascended with jubilation, and the Lord with the sound of the trumpet.
Looking from afar, behold I see the power of God coming, and a cloud covering the whole earth. * Go out to meet him, and say: * Tell us, are you he, * Who is to reign over the people of Israel.
All you earth-born, and sons of men, the rich and the poor together. Go out to meet him, and say.
O Shepherd of Israel, give ear, you who lead Joseph like a sheep. Tell us, are you he.
Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, O eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter. Who is to reign over the people of Israel.
Look down, O Lord, from your holy dwelling, and think upon us: incline your ear, O my God, and hear:
Open your eyes and see our tribulation.
Look, O Lord, for the city full of riches is made desolate, the mistress of nations sits in sorrow:
There is none to console her, save you, O our God.
She has wept bitterly in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks.
I looked in a vision of the night, and behold upon the clouds of heaven the Son of Man was coming: and to him was given kingdom, and honor:
And all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him.
The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes gathered together,
Against the Lord, and against his Christ.
Why did the nations rage, and the peoples devise vain things?
Attend to me, O Lord, and hear the voices of my adversaries:
Is evil returned for good, because they have dug a pit for my soul?
Attend to me, O Lord, and hear the voices of my adversaries: * Is evil returned for good, because they have dug a pit for my soul?
Attend, O my people, to my law:
Incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in parables: I will speak of things proposed from the beginning of the world.
Hear the word of the Lord, O nations, and declare it in the ends of the earth:
And to the islands that are far off, say: Our Savior will come.
Announce and make it heard: speak, and cry aloud.
I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of great thunder, alleluia: Our God shall reign for ever, alleluia:
For salvation and power and the dominion of his Christ have come, alleluia, alleluia.
And a voice came forth from the throne, saying: Praise our God, all you his Saints, and you who fear God, small and great.
I heard in heaven the voice of many Angels saying:
Fear the Lord, and give glory to him, and adore him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the fountains of waters, alleluia, alleluia.
I saw a mighty Angel of God, flying through the midst of heaven, crying with a loud voice and saying.
Hear, O Lord, the hymn and prayer which your servant prays before you this day, that your eyes may be open, and your ears attentive,
Over this house day and night.
Look down, O Lord, from your sanctuary, and from the high dwelling place of the heavens.
Prepare your hearts to the Lord, and serve him alone:
And he will deliver you from the hands of your enemies.
Turn to him with your whole heart, and put away the foreign gods from your midst.
Put away the foreign gods from your midst.
Hear, O Israel, the commandments of the Lord, and write them on your heart as in a book:
And I will give you a land flowing with milk and honey.
Keep, therefore, and hear my voice: and I will be an enemy to your enemies.
Perceive with your ears, O God, my tears: be not silent towards me, forgive me:
For I am a sojourner with you, and a pilgrim.
Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: Lord, make haste to help me.
Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with you:
The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: for that which shall be born of you is Holy, and shall be called the Son of God.

Bethlehem, city of the most high God, from you shall come forth the Ruler of Israel, and his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity, and he shall be magnified in the midst of all the earth:
And there shall be peace in our land, when he shall come.
He shall speak peace to the nations, and his dominion shall be from sea to sea.
Blessed are they who dwell
In your house, O Lord.
I will bless the Lord at all times:
In the Lord shall my soul be praised; let the meek hear and rejoice.
May God bless us, our God bless us, may God bless us:
And let all the ends of the earth fear him.
May God have mercy on us and bless us.
May the Lord bless you in his power, who through you has brought our enemies to nothing:
That your praise may not fail from the mouth of men.
Blessed is the Lord who created heaven and earth; for he has so magnified your name this day.
Bless the God of heaven and confess him before all the living,
Bless him and sing to him: and declare all his wondrous works.
Blessed is your name, O God of our fathers, who when you are angry will remember mercy,
And in the time of tribulation you forgive sins.
And blessed is the name of your majesty for ever, you who alone work wonders.
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone works great wonders:
And blessed is the name of his majesty for ever.
All the earth shall be filled with his majesty: so be it, so be it.
God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them:
Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.
Behold, I will establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you.
Let us bless the Father and the Son with the Holy Spirit:
Let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.
Blessed are you, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: and worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
It is good to give praise to the Lord, alleluia:
And to sing psalms, alleluia.
Upon the psaltery of ten strings, with canticle and harp.
A blind man sat by the road, as the Lord was passing by, and cried out to him: and the Lord said to him:

What do you want me to do for you?
Lord, that I may see the light.
But Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be brought to him: and when he drew near, he questioned him, saying.
What do you want me to do for you?
Lord, that I may see the light.
Sound the trumpet in Sion, call the nations, announce to the peoples, and say:
Behold, our God the Savior will come.
My eyes have grown dim from weeping: because he who comforted me is gone far from me: See, all you peoples,
If there is any sorrow like my sorrow.
O all you that pass by the way, attend and see.
My eyes have grown dim from weeping: because he who comforted me is gone far from me: See, all you peoples, * If there is any sorrow like my sorrow.
Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously honored; he has thrown the horse and rider into the sea:
The Lord has become my helper and protector unto salvation.
The Lord is as a man of war, Almighty is his name.
Sing to the Lord, alleluia:
Sing a psalm to him, alleluia.
Bring to the Lord glory and honor, bring to the Lord glory for his name.
As they were at supper, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying:
Take and eat: this is my body.
The men of my tabernacle said: Who will give us of his flesh, that we may be satisfied?
Christ, rising from the dead, dies now no more, death shall no longer have dominion over him: for in that he died, he died to sin once:
But in that he lives, he lives unto God, alleluia, alleluia.
He died once for our offenses, and rose again for our justification.
Deceitful men surrounded me: without cause they struck me with scourges:
But you, O Lord my defender, avenge me.
For tribulation is near, and there is none to help.
Lying men surrounded me; without cause they struck me with blows: * But you, O Lord my defender, avenge me.
This city surround, O Lord: and let your Angels guard its walls.
Hear your people, O Lord, with mercy.
Let your wrath be turned away, O Lord, from your people and from your holy city.
Cry out with strength, you who proclaim peace in Jerusalem:
Say to the cities of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Zion: Behold our God, whom we awaited, he shall come.
Ascend a high mountain, you who bring glad tidings to Zion; lift up your voice with strength.
You shall eat flesh and be satisfied with bread:
This is the bread which the Lord has given you to eat.
It was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.

The enemy has blocked my ways; he lay in wait for me like a lion in a hidden place; he filled me and made me drunk with bitterness: they led my life down into the pit of death, and placed a stone against me.
See, O Lord, their iniquities: and judge the cause of my soul, defender of my life.
I have become a mockery to all my people, their song all the day.
Strengthen me, O King, who hold the sovereignty of the holy ones:
And put fitting and well-sounding words in my mouth.
O Lord, King of all power, turn their counsel back upon them.
I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the prudent
And revealed them to little ones.
Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing before you.
I will confess to you, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify your name for ever:
For your mercy, O Lord, is great over me.
You are my God, and I will confess you; you are my God, and I will exalt you.
Let us confess your great name,
For it is terrible and holy.
These in chariots and these on horses, but we shall call upon the name of the Lord our God.
Rejoice with me, all you who love the Lord, for he whom I was seeking has appeared to me:
And while I wept at the tomb, I saw the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.
As the disciples departed, I did not depart, and enkindled by the fire of his love, I burned with longing.
The nations have gathered in multitude to fight against us, and we do not know what we ought to do:
O Lord God, our eyes are upon you, lest we perish.
You know what they plot against us: how shall we be able to stand before their face, unless you help us?
Our enemies have assembled and glory in their power; break their strength, O Lord, and scatter them:
That they may know there is no other who fights for us, but you, our God.
Scatter them in your power, and destroy them, O Lord our protector.

I suffered insults and terrors from those who had been my peaceable companions and who watched at my side, saying: Let us deceive him and prevail over him: but you, O Lord, are with me as a mighty warrior.
Let them fall into everlasting shame, that I may see vengeance upon them, because to you I have revealed my cause.
Judge, O Lord, the cause of my soul, defender of my life.
Abram believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness:
And therefore he was made a friend of God.
He was just before the Lord, and walked in his ways.
When Jacob heard that Esau was coming against him, he divided his sons and wives, saying: If Esau strikes one company, the other shall be saved.
Deliver me, O Lord, who said to me: * I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for their multitude.
O Lord, who said to me, Return to the land of your birth: O Lord, who have fed me from my youth.
Deliver me, O Lord, who said to me.
I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for their multitude.
When the days of Pentecost were being completed, they were all together in the same place, alleluia: and suddenly a sound came from heaven, alleluia,
As of a mighty wind, and it filled the whole house, alleluia, alleluia.
When the disciples were gathered together because of fear of the Jews, a sound suddenly came from heaven and came upon them.
Though he was in the form of God, he emptied himself,
Taking the form of a servant.
He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death.
When the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices,
That they might come and anoint Jesus, alleluia, alleluia.
And very early in the morning, on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had already risen.
When a very great crowd was coming together to Jesus, and people were hastening to him from the cities, he spoke by way of parable:
A sower went out to sow his seed.
And as he sowed, some fell on good ground and brought forth fruit a hundredfold.
He was bound to be made like his brethren in all things,
That he might become merciful.
Though he was the Son of God, he learned obedience from what he suffered.
I grieve over you, my son Jonathan, exceeding fair and beloved beyond the love of women!
For as a mother loves her only son, so did I love you.
My life has failed in sorrow, and my years in groans.
I will love you, O Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firm foundation,
And my refuge.
My deliverer, my God, my helper.
O Lord God, who crush wars from the beginning, lift up your arm over the nations that plot evil against your servants:
And let your right hand be glorified in us.
Shatter their power by your power; let their might fall in your wrath.
O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you:
For you do not spurn, O God, the prayers of the poor.
Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant.
O Lord, my King almighty, all things are placed under your dominion, and there is none who can resist your will:
Deliver us for the sake of your name.
Hear our prayer, and turn our mourning into joy.
O Lord, Father and God of my life, do not abandon me to an evil thought; do not give me haughtiness of eyes, and turn away from me evil desire, O Lord; take from me concupiscence,
And do not deliver me over to a shameless and unruly soul, O Lord.
Do not abandon me, O Lord, lest my ignorances increase, and my offenses be multiplied.
Lord, my servant lies paralyzed at home, and is grievously tormented:
Amen, I say to you, I will come and heal him.
Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.
Lord, if your people have turned back and have prayed toward your sanctuary:
You will hear from heaven, O Lord, and deliver them from the hands of their enemies.
If your people have sinned against you, and, turning back, have done penance, and coming have prayed in this place.
Remember, O Lord, your covenant, and say to the Angel who strikes: Let your hand now be still,
That the land may not be laid waste, and that you may not destroy every living soul.
It is I who have sinned, it is I who have acted wickedly: these who are sheep, what have they done? Let your wrath, I beseech you, O Lord, be turned away from your people.
Let your anger, O Lord, be at rest from your people, and from your holy city:
The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof:
The world, and all who dwell in it.
He himself has founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the rivers.
The Lord is with me as a mighty warrior: therefore they persecuted me, but could not understand: O Lord, you test the reins and the heart:
To you I have revealed my cause.
You have seen, O Lord, their iniquities against me: judge my judgment.
The Lord, who delivered me from the mouth of the lion, and freed me from the hand of the beast,
He himself will deliver me from the hands of my enemies.
God sent his mercy and his truth: he rescued my soul from the midst of lion cubs.
I took you from your father's house, says the Lord, and placed you to shepherd the flock of my people, and I was with you in all places wherever you walked,
Establishing your kingdom for ever.
And I made for you a great name, like unto the name of the great ones who are upon the earth.
Grant me, O Lord, the wisdom that stands beside your throne, and do not cast me away from among your children:
For I am your servant, and the son of your handmaid.
Send her forth from your seat of greatness, that she may be with me and labor with me.
From the mouth of the wise man honey flows forth, alleluia: the sweetness of honey is under his tongue, alleluia:
His lips are a dripping honeycomb, alleluia, alleluia.
Wisdom rests in his heart, and prudence is in the word of his mouth.
The people of Israel sang, alleluia: and the whole multitude of Jacob sang in due order:
And David with the singers struck the harp in the house of the Lord, and sang praises to God, alleluia, alleluia.
The priests and Levites were therefore sanctified: and all Israel led the ark of the covenant of the Lord with jubilation.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unjust man his thoughts, and let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him:
For the Lord our God is good and merciful, and ready to forgive evil.
The Lord does not desire the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live.
The Lord shall descend like rain upon the fleece:
Justice shall spring forth in his days, and abundance of peace.
And all kings shall adore him, all nations shall serve him.
May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the richness of the earth in abundance: may tribes and peoples serve you:
Be lord over your brothers.
And let the sons of your mother bow down before you.
Be lord over your brothers.
O God, I will sing to you a new song, alleluia:
On the psaltery of ten strings I will sing praise to you, alleluia, alleluia.
O God of my lord Abraham, direct my way:
That I may return in safety to the house of my lord.
I beseech you, O Lord, deal mercifully with your servant.
O God, in you have I hoped, O Lord, let me not be confounded for ever: in your justice deliver me,
And rescue me.
Incline your ear to me, and save me.
O God of Israel, for your sake I have borne reproach, shame has covered my face, I have become a stranger to my brothers, and an alien to the sons of my mother:
For zeal for your house has consumed me.
Attend to my soul, and deliver it, rescue me on account of my enemies.
You are my God, do not depart from me:
But you, O Lord, do not withdraw your help far from me: look to my defense.
O my God, rescue me from the hand of the sinner: and from the hand of him who acts against the law, and of the unjust:
For you are my patience.
O my God, be not far from me: O my God, look to my aid.
God is the hearer of all: he himself sent his Angel, and took me from among the sheep of my father:
And he anointed me with the anointing of his mercy.
The Lord, who delivered me from the mouth of the lion, and freed me from the hand of the beast.
Our God was seen upon the earth,
And he conversed with human beings.
He found out all the way of knowledge, and gave it to Jacob his servant.
Let those who have been redeemed now say, alleluia,
By the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.
Whom he redeemed from the hand of the enemy, and gathered together from the lands.
Noah built an altar to the Lord, and offered upon it a burnt offering: and the Lord smelled a sweet fragrance, and blessed him, saying:
You are worthy, O Lord, to receive the book, and to open its seals, alleluia: for you were slain, and have redeemed us to God
In your blood, alleluia.
For you have made us a kingdom and a priesthood to our God.
The Lord taught them discipline and wisdom, alleluia: he strengthened in them the grace of his Spirit,
And filled their hearts with understanding, alleluia.
For the Holy Spirit came upon them with a sudden sound.

The wicked said among themselves, not thinking rightly: Let us beset the just man, for he is contrary to our works: he professes to have knowledge of God, he calls himself the Son of God, and boasts of having God as his Father:
Let us see if his words are true: and if he is truly the Son of God, let him deliver him from our hands: let us condemn him to a most shameful death.
We were counted by him as frivolous, and he abstains from our ways as from uncleanness: and he sets the last end of the just before us.
The Angel said to Jacob:
Let me go, for it is dawn. He answered him: I will not let you go unless you bless me. And he blessed him in that same place.
When Jacob had risen, behold a man wrestled with him until morning: and when he saw that he could not overcome him, he said to him.
The Lord said to Noah: The end of all flesh has come before me: the earth is filled with their iniquity,
And I will destroy them, along with the earth.
Make yourself an ark from smoothed wood; you shall make little dwelling places in it.
The Lord God also said: It is not good for the man to be alone:
Let us make a helper for him similar to himself.
But for Adam there was not found a helper similar to himself; and God said:
Joseph said to his eleven brothers: I am Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt; does our aged father, of whom you spoke to me, still live?
Go, bring him to me, that he may be able to live.
For it is now two years since the famine began upon the land, and there remain five years more, in which there can be neither plowing nor reaping.
Judah said to his brothers: Behold, the Ishmaelites are passing by; come, let him be sold, and let our hands not be defiled:
For he is our flesh and our brother.
For what profit is there if we kill our brother and conceal his blood? It is better that he be sold.
Judas said to Simon his brother: Choose men for yourself and go, and free your brothers in Galilee; but I and my brother Jonathan will go into the country of Gilead.
As will be the will in heaven, so let it be done.
Gird yourselves, O sons of power, and be ready; for it is better for us to die in battle than to see evils come to our nation and to our holy places.
Reuben said to his brothers: Did I not say to you, Do not sin against the boy, and you would not listen to me?
Behold, his blood is exacted.
We deserve to suffer these things, because we have sinned against our brother, seeing the anguish of his soul, when he begged us and we would not listen.
The Lord will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths:
For out of Zion the law will go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob.
I will teach the unjust your ways, and the impious will be converted to you.
Free me from blood, O God, the God of my salvation.
O Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth will announce your praise.
O Ruler, Lord of heaven and earth, Creator of the waters, King of all creation,
Hear the prayer of your servants.
You, O Lord, to whom the prayer of the humble and the meek has always been pleasing.
While the Lord God was walking in paradise in the afternoon breeze, he called out and said: Adam, where are you? I heard, O Lord, your voice,
And I hid myself.
I heard your voice in paradise, and I was afraid, because I was naked.
As Jacob went out from his own land, he saw the glory of God, and said: How terrible is this place!
This is none other than the house of God, and the gate of heaven.
Truly God is in this place, and I did not know it.
As Jacob was going from Beersheba and proceeding toward Haran, the Lord spoke to him, saying:
The land on which you sleep I will give to you and to your offspring.
He built an altar of stones in honor of the Lord, pouring oil over it; and God blessed him, saying:
While Abraham stood at the oak of Mamre, he saw three men coming along the way:
He saw three, and adored one.
Behold, your wife Sarah will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac.
Two Seraphim cried out one to the other:
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God of hosts: * all the earth is filled with his glory.
For there are Three who give testimony in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit. And these Three are One.
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God of hosts.
All the earth is filled with his glory.
Behold, I come from the South, I the Lord your God,
To visit you in peace.
I will look upon you and make you increase; you shall be multiplied, and I will establish my covenant with you.
Behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil:
See to it, lest he put forth his hand and also take from the tree of life, and live forever.
The Lord God also made for Adam a tunic of skins, and clothed him, and said:

1:1 Blessed is the man who has not followed the counsel of the impious, † and has not remained in the way of sinners, * and has not sat in the chair of pestilence.
1:2 But his will is with the law of the Lord, * and he will meditate on his law, day and night.
1:3a And he will be like a tree that has been planted beside running waters, * which will provide its fruit in its time,
1:3b and its leaf will not fall away, * and all things whatsoever that he does will prosper.
1:4 Not so the impious, not so. * For they are like the dust that the wind casts along the face of the earth.
1:5 Therefore, the impious will not prevail again in judgment, * nor sinners in the council of the just.
1:6 For the Lord knows the way of the just. * And the path of the impious will pass away.
10:2 I trust in the Lord. † How can you say to my soul, * “Sojourn to the mountain, like a sparrow.”
10:3 For behold, the sinners have bent their bow. † They have prepared their arrows in the quiver, * so as to shoot arrows in the dark at the upright of heart.
10:4 For they have destroyed the things that you have completed. * But what has the just one done?
10:5a The Lord is in his holy temple. * The Lord’s throne is in heaven.
10:5b His eyes look upon the poor. * His eyelids question the sons of men.
10:6 The Lord questions the just and the impious. * Yet he who loves iniquity, hates his own soul.
10:7 He will rain down snares upon sinners. * Fire and brimstone and windstorms will be the portion of their cup.
10:8 For the Lord is just, and he has chosen justice. * His countenance has beheld equity.
100:1 I will sing mercy and judgment * to you, O Lord.
100:2 I will sing psalms. And I will have understanding within the immaculate way, * when you will draw near to me.
100:2 I wandered about in the innocence of my heart, * in the midst of my house.
100:3 I will not display any unjust thing before my eyes. * I have hated those carrying out betrayals.
100:4 The perverse heart did not adhere to me. * And the malignant, who turned away before me, I would not recognize.
100:5 The one who secretly detracted his neighbor, * this one I pursued.
100:5 The one with an arrogant eye and an insatiable heart, * with that one I would not eat.
100:6 My eyes looked toward the faithful of the earth, to sit with me. * The one walking in the immaculate way, this one ministered to me.
100:7 He who has acted arrogantly will not dwell in the midst of my house. * He who has spoken iniquity was not guided with the sight of my eyes.
100:8 In the morning, I executed all the sinners of the earth, * so that I might scatter all the workers of iniquity from the city of the Lord.
101:2 O Lord, hear my prayer, * and let my outcry reach you.
101:3 Do not turn your face away from me. * In whatever day that I am in trouble, incline your ear to me.
101:3 In whatever day that I will call upon you, * heed me quickly.
101:4 For my days have faded away like smoke, * and my bones have dried out like firewood.
101:5 I have been cut down like hay, and my heart has withered, * for I had forgotten to eat my bread.
101:6 Before the voice of my groaning, * my bone has adhered to my flesh.
101:7 I have become like a pelican in solitude. * I have become like a night raven in a house.
101:8 I have kept vigil, * and I have become like a solitary sparrow on a roof.
101:9 All day long my enemies reproached me, * and those who praised me swore oaths against me.
101:10 For I chewed on ashes like bread, * and I mixed weeping into my drink.
101:11 By the face of your anger and indignation, * you lifted me up and threw me down.
101:12 My days have declined like a shadow, * and I have dried out like hay.
101:13 But you, O Lord, endure for eternity, * and your memorial is from generation to generation.
101:14 You will rise up and take pity on Zion, * for it is time for its mercy, for the time has come.
101:15 For its stones have pleased your servants, * and they will take pity on its land.
101:16 And the Gentiles will fear your name, O Lord, * and all the kings of the earth your glory.
101:17 For the Lord has built up Zion, * and he will be seen in his glory.
101:18 He has noticed the prayer of the humble, * and he has not despised their petition.
101:19 Let these things be written in another generation, * and the people who will be created will praise the Lord.
101:20 For he has gazed from his high sanctuary. * From heaven, the Lord has beheld the earth.
101:21 So may he hear the groans of those in shackles, * in order that he may release the sons of the slain.
101:22 So may they announce the name of the Lord in Zion * and his praise in Jerusalem:
101:23 while the people convene, * along with kings, in order that they may serve the Lord.
101:24 He responded to him in the way of his virtue: * Declare to me the brevity of my days.
101:25 Do not call me back in the middle of my days: * your years are from generation to generation.
101:26 In the beginning, O Lord, you founded the earth. * And the heavens are the work of your hands.
101:27 They will perish, but you remain. * And all will grow old like a garment.
101:28 And, like a blanket, you will change them, and they will be changed. * Yet you are ever yourself, and your years will not decline.
101:29 The sons of your servants will live, * and their offspring will be guided aright in every age.
102:1 Bless the Lord, O my soul, * and bless his holy name, all that is within me.
102:2 Bless the Lord, O my soul, * and do not forget all his recompenses.
102:3 He forgives all your iniquities. * He heals all your infirmities.
102:4 He redeems your life from destruction. * He crowns you with mercy and compassion.
102:5 He satisfies your desire with good things. * Your youth will be renewed like that of the eagle.
102:6 The Lord accomplishes mercies, * and his judgment is for all who patiently endure injuries.
102:7 He has made his ways known to Moses, * his will to the sons of Israel.
102:8 The Lord is compassionate and merciful, * patient and full of mercy.
102:9 He will not be angry forever, * and he will not threaten for eternity.
102:10 He has not dealt with us according to our sins, * and he has not repaid us according to our iniquities.
102:11 For according to the height of the heavens above the earth, * so has he reinforced his mercy toward those who fear him.
102:12 As far as the east is from the west, * so far has he removed our iniquities from us.
102:13 As a father is compassionate to his sons, so has the Lord been compassionate to those who fear him. * For he knows our form.
102:14 He has called to mind that we are dust. * Man: his days are like hay. Like the flower of the field, so will he flourish.
102:16 For the spirit in him will pass away, and it will not remain, * and he will know his place no longer.
102:17 But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity, * and even unto eternity, upon those who fear him.
102:17 And his justice is with the sons of the sons, * with those who serve his covenant
102:18 and have been mindful of his commandments * by doing them.
102:19 The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, * and his kingdom will rule over all.
102:20 Bless the Lord, all you his Angels: * powerful in virtue, doing his word, in order to heed the voice of his discourse.
102:21 Bless the Lord, all his hosts: * his ministers who do his will.
102:22 Bless the Lord, all his works: * in every place of his dominion. Bless the Lord, O my soul.
103:1 Bless the Lord, O my soul. * O Lord my God, you are exceedingly great.
103:1 You have clothed yourself with confession and beauty; * you are dressed with light like a garment,
103:2 while you stretch out heaven like a tent. * You cover its heights with water.
103:3 You set the clouds as your stairs. * You walk upon the wings of the winds.
103:4 You make your Angels a breath of life, * and your ministers a burning fire.
103:5 You founded the earth upon its stable base. * It will not be bent from age to age.
103:6 The abyss, like a garment, is its clothing. * The waters will remain standing above the mountains.
103:7 At your rebuke, they will flee. * At the voice of your thunder, they will dread.
103:8 The mountains ascend, and the plains descend, * to the place which you have founded for them.
103:9 You have set a limit that they will not cross. * And they will not return to cover the earth.
103:10 You spring forth fountains in steep valleys. * The waters will cross through the midst of the mountains.
103:11 All the wild beasts of the field will drink. * The wild donkeys will anticipate in their thirst.
103:12 Above them, the flying things of the air will dwell. * From the midst of the rocks, they will utter voices.
103:13 You irrigate the mountains from your heights. * The earth will be satiated from the fruit of your works,
103:14 producing grass for cattle * and herbs for the service of men.
103:14 So may you draw bread from the earth, * and wine, in order to cheer the heart of man.
103:15 Then he may gladden his face with oil, * and bread will confirm the heart of man.
103:16 The trees of the field will be saturated, along with the cedars of Lebanon, which he planted. * There, the sparrows will make their nests.
103:17 The leader of them is the house of the heron. * The heights of the hills are for the deer; the rock is a refuge for the hedgehog.
103:19 He has made the moon for seasons; * the sun knows its setting.
103:20 You appointed darkness, and it has become night; * all the beasts of the forest will cross through it.
103:21 The young lions will roar, * while searching for and seizing their meal from God.
103:22 The sun arose, and they were gathered together; * and in their dens, they will lie down together.
103:23 Man will go forth to his work * and to his activities, until the evening.
103:24 How great are your works, O Lord! * You have made all things in wisdom. The earth has been filled with your possessions.
103:25 This sea is great and its hands are spacious. * There are creeping things without number:
103:26 the small animals with the great. * There, the ships will pass by
103:27 this sea-serpent that you have formed to mock them. * All these expect you to give them food in due time.
103:28 What you give to them, they will gather. * When you open your hand, they will all be filled with goodness.
103:29 But if you turn your face away, they will be disturbed. * You will take away their breath, and they will fail, and they will return to their dust.
103:30 You will send forth your Spirit, and they will be created. * And you will renew the face of the earth.
103:31 May the glory of the Lord be for all ages. * The Lord will rejoice in his works.
103:32 He considers the earth, and he makes it tremble. * He touches the mountains, and they smoke.
103:33 I will sing to the Lord with my life. * I will sing psalms to my God, as long as I am.
103:34 May my speech be pleasing to him. * Truly, I will take delight in the Lord.
103:35 Let sinners fade away from the earth, along with the unjust, so that they may not be. * Bless the Lord, O my soul.
104:1 Confess to the Lord, and invoke his name. * Announce his works among the nations.
104:2 Sing to him, and sing psalms to him. * Describe all his wonders.
104:3 Be praised in his holy name. * Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
104:4 Seek the Lord, and be confirmed. * Seek his face always.
104:5 Remember his miracles, which he has done, * his portents and the judgments of his mouth:
104:6 you offspring of Abraham his servant, * you sons of Jacob his elect.
104:7 He is the Lord our God. * His judgments are throughout the entire earth.
104:8 He has remembered his covenant for all ages: * the word that he entrusted to a thousand generations,
104:9 which he assigned to Abraham, * and his oath to Isaac.
104:10 And he stationed the same for Jacob with a precept, * and for Israel with an eternal testament,
104:11 saying: To you, I will give the land of Canaan, * the allotment of your inheritance.
104:12 Though they may have been but a small number, * very few and foreigners there,
104:13 and though they passed from nation to nation, * and from one kingdom to another people,
104:14 he allowed no man to harm them, * and he reproved kings on their behalf.
104:15 Do not be willing to touch my Christ, * and do not be willing to malign my prophets.
104:16 And he called a famine upon the land, * and he crushed every foundation of the bread.
104:17 He sent a man before them: * Joseph, who had been sold as a slave.
104:18 They humbled his feet in shackles; the iron pierced his soul, * until his word arrived.
104:19 The eloquence of the Lord inflamed him. * The king sent and released him; he was the ruler of the people, and he dismissed him.
104:21 He established him as master of his house * and ruler of all his possessions,
104:22 so that he might instruct his princes as himself, * and teach his elders prudence.
104:23 And Israel entered into Egypt, * and Jacob became a sojourner in the land of Ham.
104:24 And he helped his people greatly, * and he strengthened them over their enemies.
104:25 He turned their heart to hate his people, * and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
104:26 He sent Moses, his servant, * and Aaron, the one whom he chose.
104:27 He placed with them signs of his word, * and portents in the land of Ham.
104:28 He sent darkness and made it conceal, * and he did not afflict them with his speech.
104:29 He turned their waters into blood, * and he slaughtered their fish.
104:30 Their land brought forth frogs, * even in the inner chambers of their kings.
104:31 He spoke, and there came forth common flies * and gnats, in every region.
104:32 He gave them a shower of hail * and a burning fire, in the same land.
104:33 And he struck their vineyards and their fig trees, * and he crushed the trees of their region.
104:34 He spoke, and the locust came forth, and the caterpillar, * of which there was no number.
104:35 And it devoured all the grass in their land, * and it consumed all the fruit of their land.
104:36 And he struck all the first-born in their land, * the first-fruits of all their labor.
104:37 And he led them out with silver and gold, * and there was not an infirm one among their tribes.
104:38 Egypt was joyful at their departure, * for the fear of them lay heavy upon them.
104:39 He spread a cloud for their protection, * and a fire, to give them light through the night.
104:40 They petitioned, and the quail came; * and he satisfied them with the bread of heaven.
104:41 He ruptured the rock and the waters flowed: * rivers gushed in the dry land.
104:42 For he had called to mind his holy word, * which he kept near to his servant Abraham.
104:43 And he led forth his people in exultation, * and his elect in rejoicing.
104:44 And he gave them the regions of the Gentiles, * and they possessed the labors of the peoples,
104:45 so that they might observe his justifications, * and inquire about his law.
105:1 Confess to the Lord, for he is good, * for his mercy is with every generation.
105:2 Who will declare the powers of the Lord? * Who make a hearing for all his praises?
105:3 Blessed are those who keep judgment * and who do justice at all times.
105:4 Remember us, O Lord, with good will for your people. * Visit us with your salvation,
105:5 so that we may see the goodness of your elect, so that we may rejoice in the joy of your nation, * so that you may be praised along with your inheritance.
105:6 We have sinned, as have our fathers. * We have acted unjustly; we have wrought iniquity.
105:7 Our fathers did not understand your miracles in Egypt. * They did not remember the multitude of your mercies.
105:7 And they provoked you, while going up to the sea, * even the Red Sea.
105:8 And he saved them for the sake of his name, * so that he might make known his power.
105:9 And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up. * And he led them into the abyss, as if into a desert.
105:10 And he saved them from the hand of those who hated them. * And he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
105:11 And the water covered those who troubled them. * Not one of them remained.
105:12 And they believed his words, * and they sang his praises.
105:13 As soon as they had finished, they forgot his works, * and they would not endure his counsel.
105:14 And they coveted their desire in the desert, * and they tempted God in a waterless place.
105:15 And he granted to them their request, * and he sent abundance into their souls.
105:16 And they provoked Moses in the camp, * and Aaron, the holy one of the Lord.
105:17 The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, * and it covered the congregation of Abiram.
105:18 And a fire broke out in their congregation. * A flame burned up the sinners.
105:19 And they fashioned a calf at Horeb, * and they adored a graven image.
105:20 And they exchanged their glory * for the likeness of a calf that eats hay.
105:21 They forgot God, who saved them, * who did great things in Egypt: miracles in the land of Ham, terrible things at the Red Sea.
